entry.title: FM power-up: script notes
entry.content:
FM RF power-up script

Date: 2026-09-23　Device <设备IP> (Alpine / SC9832A / Marlin2 combo)
Background: zz_fm.start used to only bring up fm_user_daemon and never sent on,
so after boot the device presented a “daemon present, chipid=0x2341 normal, but RF off“ false-available state.

1. Power-up chain (all links required)

The manifestation of any missing link is ioctl -110 (set_marlin_wakeup ack timeout).

2. The three scripts

FilePurpose
/root/fm_powerup.shRF power-up, idempotent. Usage sh /root/fm_powerup.sh [freq_kHz] [vol], defaults to 97400 5
/etc/local.d/zz_fm.startboot autostart: start the daemon → call fm_powerup.sh → start keep-alive
/root/fm_watchdog.shchecks the daemon every 5s; if it dies, restart the daemon and asynchronously top up the power once

fm_powerup.sh internal flow

  1. Precondition check: wcnd is running and /dev/fm exists (otherwise FATAL exit with a prompt to run bt_bringup first)
  2. Start the daemon if it is not running; poll and wait for /tmp/fm_ctl.sock to appear (at most 30s)
  3. Read state; skip if already on; otherwise send on, retrying at most 3 times
    — on failure, restart the daemon to rebuild @wcnd’s long-lived FM-OPEN connection and try again (this is the standard cure for -110)
  4. On success, set tune / vol / mute 0, and print the final state
  5. Logs are also written to /var/log/fm_boot.log

Note: the script deliberately does not call rssi — that ioctl blocks for a fixed ~4.2s each time before timing out.
Socket interactions uniformly go through python with settimeout(6), to avoid hanging the script.

3. Measured results (2026-09-23)

Keep-alive: pid=30867; running the script again exits 0 by itself (the pid file single-instance takes effect).

4. Vulnerability fixed along the way

fm_watchdog.sh used to have nobody responsible for starting it (a global grep found its own name only inside its own file),
i.e. once the daemon died it would never self-heal. It is now started at the end of zz_fm.start, and after a restart it asynchronously tops up the power.

5. Pitfalls encountered

Using ps -o pid,args | grep '[f]m_watchdog.sh' to judge liveness will misjudge it as “already running” —
it hits the sh -c process itself carrying this command (PID 29166).
The [f] trick only avoids grep itself, not the shell’s sh -c.
Single-instance shell scripts should always use a pid file + kill -0 to judge.

6. Known side effects

After the FM RF powers up, the kernel continuously spams (FM_RDS) / FM_DRV logs and pushes up load (about 9 lines/second);
when debugging other kernel issues, first turn off the RF with python3 /root/fm_cli.py off.

Copyright: This article is an original work by whiteleibniz (organized with AI assistance). All rights reserved. Please credit the source and keep the original link: https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: FM audio output: the vendor's official audio path and practical steps
entry.content:
FM audio output: the vendor’s official audio path (2026-09-23)

Background: this device’s FM is “connected at the application layer” (TUNE / RDS / volume are all there), but there is no sound.
The previous conclusion was “FM audio is not feasible in user space”, on the grounds that: the card1 DAPM route is incomplete, all 8 captures return EIO,
and codec_reg is an empty file.
This round overturns half of that conclusion: FM audio does not have to rely on the few audio ioctls in marlin_fm.ko —
the vendor actually wrote the FM audio path into the Android partition’s configuration files, and
all these kcontrols exist on this device’s card1.
The reason it did not come out before is that nobody ever configured it according to that configuration.

Status: pending your manual verification on the device (I will not run the verification again). This document gives the control names, order, commands, and troubleshooting points.

1. Conclusions first

ItemConclusion
OVER_BT_ENABLE(0x1d) / I2S_SETTING(0x21) / ANA_SWITCH(0x1e) / GET_AUDIO_INFO(0x30)these are empty shells in this device’s marlin_fm.ko: fm_ioctl enters the case, printks one line with the name, and returns, sending no SDIO commands at all (confirmed by disassembly). Stop hoping to switch the audio path with FM ioctls.
Upstream open-source driver (the same marlin2_fm)likewise writes these cases as ret = 0; break; — the vendor never implemented them on this chain. This is the authoritative evidence that the OVER_BT_ENABLE path is dead.
Where the real path ison the AP codec side; the vendor gave the full definition in the Android system partition’s /etc/tiny_hw.xml. The audio coming out of the FM chip (digital DIGFM or analog AIL/AIR line-in) → codec → SPK/headphones, the AP does not need to move the audio data.
Whether this device has itIt does. In card1 (sprdphone), controls like Digital FM Function, AD IISMUX (enum includes DIGFM), Line Function, ADCL/ADCR Mixer AILADCL/AIRADCR, SPKL Mixer ADCLSPKL, HPL Mixer ADCRHPL all exist.
Why it did not come out beforepreviously only Speaker Function was set (connecting DACL→EAR), without setting any control on the FM side, and without opening hw:1,4(Dfm) PCM to trigger DAPM power-up. Neither was done, so naturally there was no sound.

2. The vendor’s official path definition (verbatim)

Source: the device’s Android system partition /etc/tiny_hw.xml (read-only mounted at /mnt/android_sys).

2.1 Digital FM — <device name="digital-fm">

AD IISMUX‘s enum options (measured on this device’s card1):
[0]=AUDIIS0 [1]=DIGFM [2]=EXTDIGFM [3]=EXTIIS6 [4]=AUDIIS1

⚠️ Note: the enum order dumped on this device is (AUDIIS0/DIGFM/EXTDIGFM/EXTIIS6/AUDIIS1),
in which val="2" falls on EXTDIGFM rather than DIGFM. The XML was written for another kernel/codec version,
so both values must be tried (recommended: 2 first, then 1). This is the value in this plan most likely to need on-site tuning.

2.2 Analog FM (line-in → codec loop)

2.3 Output side (digital FM needs one configured too)

Reference: public analysis of the same SoC on the SC9832A platform confirms that FM audio enters the
codec from AIL/AIR (a MIC-like line-in), then either outputs directly via the “FM playback patch” or goes through VBC for the main control to record — fully consistent with the configuration file above.

3. How you run it (manual verification steps)

3.0 Preparation

  1. Bring up the FM power-up chain first: WiFi firmware download → bt_bringup.start (including wcn BT-OPEN) → send wcn FM-OPEN to @wcnd
    and keep the connection long-term.
  2. fm_user_daemon keeps /dev/fm open (socket /tmp/fm_ctl.sock); TUNE to a local strong-signal station.
  3. Execute mute 0 via /tmp/fm_ctl.sock to confirm FM is not muted (for the socket command syntax, see
    AI工作流/*/docs/ and lv_pages/radio_page.c).
  4. Without amixer/tinymix, use the existing /root/fm_ctl: fm_ctl <op> <card> ...

3.1 First confirm the controls’ real names (very important)

The names dumped earlier do not necessarily equal the full ALSA names (for example, the dump has ADCL Mixer AILADCL,
while the XML has ADCL Mixer AILADCL Switch). Grep once to get the real names:

3.2 Plan A: digital FM → speaker (recommended to try first)

Step 3 is the easiest one to miss: the reason the Dfm PCM device exists is to “open the stream and pull DAPM up”;
setting only the kcontrols without the stream coming up leaves bias_level stuck at Off (exactly the previously observed phenomenon).

3.3 Plan B: analog line-in → speaker / headphones

3.4 Off / reset

4. Troubleshooting points

PhenomenonPossible causeHandling
Completely silent, bias_level still Offhw:1,4 not opened/writtenconfirm the fm_pcm process is running and writei has not returned an error
Audible but very quiet / distortedgoing through the line-in analog path, with gain unconfiguredkeep only one route (two open at once interfere with each other), and try another AD IISMUX value
AD IISMUX cannot be setdifferent enum value rangefirst fm_ctl get card1 "AD IISMUX" to see the allowed value range
Headphones requiredthe FM antenna may be on the headphone linetry TUNE to the strongest station without headphones; if they must be plugged in, the UI needs a prompt
Digital FM never worksthis device’s firmware may not have connected the FM digital port to VBCfall back to plan B (analog line-in), which has the most complete route

Following the “end-to-end evidence” principle: the criterion is the human ear hearing the station audio, not the ioctl returning 0.

5. Pending confirmation checklist (to be backfilled after verification)

  • The correct value of AD IISMUX (which of 1 / 2 / 3 is DIGFM)
  • Which of digital FM and analog line-in actually works on this device
  • Whether headphones are needed as an antenna
  • Whether volume is controlled by SETVOL(0x04) or by the codec’s pga (the digital-fm profile in codec_pga.xml uses VBC STL DG Set / VBC STR DG Set)
  • The crosstalk situation when FM and A2DP are on at the same time (determines how channel arbitration should be written)

6. Appendix: evidence sources

FileContent
/mnt/android_sys/etc/tiny_hw.xmlthe vendor’s full mixer path definitions (the verbatim source of §2 in this article)
/mnt/android_sys/etc/codec_pga.xmldigital-fm profile → VBC STL DG Set(bit 0) / VBC STR DG Set(bit 16)
radio_docs/mixer_card1.txtthe full kcontrol dump of this device’s card1 (confirming the controls exist)
LKML [PATCH 2/2] misc: added Spreadtrum's radio driver (Chunyan Zhang, 2017)the driver’s upstream source: the full FM_IOCTL_* table, the chip-side FM_*_CMD numbering, and the empty implementations of the I2S/AudioInfo cases
Public analysis《Sprd 9832A Android6.0 FM 模式下的几种 Audio 路径》AIL/AIR input, the signal flow of the three modes (Line_in-Codec / Line_in-VBC-Codec / Digital FM-VBC-Codec)

entry.title: FM radio startup flow: Android vs Alpine comparison
entry.content:
Spreadtrum SC9832A FM radio startup flow — Android vs Alpine (this device) comparison

Audience: anyone who needs to understand “why we do it this way on Alpine”
Core value: Android natively has a whole framework, and on Alpine we replace it with as little code as possible — this article aligns every stage of the two sides, so you know clearly which segment we replaced and what the basis for the replacement is

1. Chip physical architecture (shared by both systems)

Whether Android or Alpine, the bottom three layers are exactly the same, which is the prerequisite for being able to compare them:

Measured values (spd-box, this device):

ItemValue
SDIO modaliassdio:c00v0000d2331
FM drivermarlin_fm (Used by sprdwl)
FM device nodes/dev/fm (misc 23), /dev/log_radio (misc 35)
FM PCM01-04: Dfm sprd-codec-fm-4 (playback)
KernelLinux 3.10.65

The driver states: SDIO radio driver for marlin2 FM Radio Receivers, share SDIO with BT/WIFI
— this statement holds under both systems and is the starting point for analyzing shared-resource issues.

2. Android 6.0 native FM startup flow

2.1 Startup chain

2.2 Android key points

StageWhat Android does
Permissions/access controlSELinux + device node permissions; /dev/fm only allows access by the radio group
Audio routingFMHalSource holds the pcmHandle; FMHalThread::threadLoop() reads PCM → RingBuffer → AudioFlinger mixing
State managementBroadcastRadioService manages radios uniformly and provides the RadioManager API to apps
RDS handlingparsed inside the HAL (rds_parser lives on the driver or HAL side) and reported to apps via RadioMetadata
Multi-app contentionthe service layer arbitrates uniformly; apps use it as API clients
Middleware thicknessvery thick: App → RadioManager → BroadcastRadioService → JNI → HAL → /dev/fm

Evidence sources (readable directly from the Android partition on this device):

3. The Alpine (this device) FM solution

3.1 Goal: replace a whole framework with minimal code

On Alpine we have no binder / SystemServer / AudioFlinger / SELinux radio policy.
So what must be replaced is layers ④ and ⑤; layers ①–③ are kept as they are.

3.2 Proposed startup chain

3.3 Correspondences on the Alpine side

Android componentAlpine replacementNotes
insmod + node permissionsinherits the existing WiFi chain; no extra action needed/dev/fm is already available
BroadcastRadioServiceNonereplaces service-layer arbitration with single-instance mutual exclusion in the daemon
FM HAL (libFMHalSource.so)the audio thread inside fm_radio_daemonisomorphic logic: read PCM → buffer → output
JNI / libfmjni.soNonea unix socket text protocol is used between the UI and the daemon
libengfm.so(fm_runcommand)implement the command encapsulation yourselfthe hint is to adopt the AT command style
RadioManager APIsocket text commandsfew commands, easy to debug, consistent with the Bluetooth daemon
AudioFlinger mixing/focuswrite the audio focus arbitration yourselfmust be done, otherwise FM/A2DP/local playback will cross-talk
FM App (APK)LVGL radio_page720×1280 portrait screen, 31px line-height grid

4. Stage-by-stage comparison table

StageAndroidAlpine (this device)Key differences
Firmware downloaddownload in initdownload via openrcbasically the same; Alpine relies on the WiFi auto-start chain
Power-up managementwcnd manages uniformlywcnd likewisethe same
Driver loadinginsmod sprdwl → marlin_fmthe same (auto-loaded)note that marlin_fm is depended on by sprdwl
Device node/dev/fm (restricted access)/dev/fm (misc 23)under Alpine root connects directly, with no SELinux constraints
Command interfaceHAL wraps ioctl/ATthe daemon sends directlythe command numbers have been reverse-engineered (0xC004F500 | nr, 47 of them)
Audio sourceFMHalSource + FMHalThread + RingBufferthe daemon builds its own read threadisomorphic architecture, simplified implementation
Audio mixingAudioFlingera focus arbitration must be builtAndroid is backed by the framework; Alpine must write it itself
RDS reportingRadioMetadata → Appsocket text fieldsthe RDS parsing capability already exists in the driver; take it directly
UIAPK + full FM appLVGL radio pagelimited by MCU-class resources, designed lean for 720×1280
Multi-app contentionservice-layer arbitrationsingle-daemon exclusive access + upper-layer arbitrationsimple but sufficient
Command-line toolsamixer/tinymix/tinyplay (bundled with Android)none of themyou can only write C against libasound.so.2

5. Key principles (why this works)

  1. The combo chip sharing SDIO is the key constraint:
    the firmware is burned once and power-up is managed uniformly, so it is impossible to burn firmware for FM alone or power it up alone.
    This is also the root cause of “if WiFi does not work, FM certainly does not work”.

  2. The driver has already done all the complex RF/demodulation/RDS work:
    user space does not need to implement any FM protocol; it only needs to operate according to the command set.
    Therefore, on the Alpine side it is feasible to replace Android’s “whole HAL + service + JNI stack” with “a thin daemon”.

  3. Audio is the only framework capability that must be added yourself:
    Android has AudioFlinger for mixing and focus management; on the Alpine side nothing handles this,
    three-way arbitration among FM / A2DP / local playback must be explicitly implemented, otherwise users will certainly encounter cross-talk.

  4. The socket text protocol is a deliberate choice:
    it stays consistent with the existing Bluetooth daemon (/tmp/bt_ctl.sock, state/on/off),
    and the team already has the mental model and the pitfall experience (especially “you must set a socket timeout, or the UI freezes”).

6. One-line summary

Android holds FM up with a whole framework (Service + HAL + JNI + AudioFlinger);
on Alpine we keep the same bottom three layers (hardware/firmware/driver),
use a single fm_radio_daemon to replace the middleware, use an LVGL radio page to replace the app,
and add ourselves the piece that Android’s framework backs up — audio focus arbitration.
The only former uncertainty, the ioctl command numbers, has been removed (see “FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原”), and the whole chain can now run end to end.

Copyright: This article is an original work by whiteleibniz (organized with AI assistance). All rights reserved. Please credit the source and keep the original link: https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: FM radio ioctl command table: reverse-engineered reconstruction
entry.content:
Spreadtrum SC9832A FM radio — reverse-engineered reconstruction of the ioctl command table (with field-test confirmation)

Audience: engineers responsible for the FM daemon / UI; engineers who want to reuse this technique when connecting other peripherals later.
How to use: when writing /dev/fm-related code, look up the command numbers directly in the tables in this article; do not guess again, and do not wait for the vendor’s header files again.
Core value: it turns the former “number one blocker” into a constant table you can code directly, and provides a reusable forensics method.

0. One-line summary

marlin_fm.ko is not stripped, and the command numbers are written right in the machine code of fm_ioctl().
All commands are uniformly encoded as _IOWR(0xF5, nr, 4) = 0xC004F500 | nr;
of the 47 commands, 45 have been confirmed by on-device tests (the kernel log printed the command names), and the other 2 were inferred by static disassembly.
The only hard blocker has been removed; you can start writing the daemon.

0.1 ⚠️ Important corrections (added 2026-09-22, read before use)

The command number table itself is still accurate, but the following three capability-level conclusions have been overturned by later field tests; do not design according to the old conclusions:

Old conclusion (original draft of this article)Field-test correction
SCAN 0x08 + SCAN_GETRSSI 0x24 are usable and can draw a spectrum/signal strength❌ Both are empty shells: the calls return 0 but with zero SDIO traffic; GETRSSI 0x07 is the only signal-class command that really sends SDIO, but it always returns ETIMEDOUT after 4.2s with a barely changing return value → this device cannot obtain a trustworthy signal strength
SEEK 0x03 can “search up/down for the next station”❌ The driver truncates the start frequency to 1 byte (freq & 0xFF goes into the AT frame), so in-band frequencies cannot be passed in; field tests show only two fixed return values, 92.5MHz / 103.1MHz, independent of the current frequency → station seeking cannot be implemented
write(/dev/fm) can be used to write AT text and bypass the ioctl❌ Always -1 / EINVAL(22), with no SDIO traffic at all

In addition, audio-class commands such as OVER_BT_ENABLE 0x1d / ANA_SWITCH 0x1e / I2S_SETTING 0x21 are all empty shells
(disassembly of fm_ioctl shows R_ARM_CALL calling only 7 functions, with no audio path functions).

→ For detailed field-test data, see FM收音_SEEK与场强_实测结论.md.

1. Conclusion table (usable directly as fm_ioctl.h)

Encoding: cmd = 0xC004F500 | nr, i.e. _IOWR(magic=0xF5, nr, size=4).

nrCommand numberCommand nameConfirmation methodReturn value measured on this devicePurpose
0x000xC004F500power upmeasured0Power-up (note: not TUNE)
0x010xC004F501power downmeasured0Power-down
0x020xC004F502TUNEmeasured-1 (ETIMEDOUT)Tune to a specified frequency (parameter = frequency)
0x030xC004F503SEEKmeasured0Search up/down for the next station
0x040xC004F504SETVOLmeasured0Set the volume
0x050xC004F505GETVOLmeasured0Read the volume
0x060xC004F506MUTEmeasured0Mute switch
0x070xC004F507GETRSSImeasured0Signal strength (UI signal bar)
0x080xC004F508SCANmeasured0Full-band scan
0x090xC004F509STOP_SCANstatic inference-1 (no log printed)Interrupt the scan
0x0a0xC004F50AGETCHIPIDmeasured0Chip ID (this device returns 0x2341)
0x0b0xC004F50BEM_TESTmeasured0Engineering mode
0x0c0xC004F50CRW_REGmeasured0Register read/write (debugging)
0x0d0xC004F50DGETMONOSTEROmeasured0Mono/stereo status
0x0e0xC004F50EGETCURPAMDmeasured0Current PAMD value
0x0f0xC004F50FGETGOODBCNTmeasured0Good block count (audio quality statistics)
0x100xC004F510GETBADBNTmeasured0Bad block count
0x110xC004F511GETBLERRATIOmeasured0Block error rate
0x120xC004F512RDS_ONOFFmeasured-1RDS switch
0x130xC004F513RDS_SUPPORTmeasured0Whether RDS is supported
0x170xC004F517SIM_DATAmeasured0Simulation data (production testing)
0x180xC004F518IS_FM_POWERED_UPmeasured0Whether it is already powered up (for daemon startup self-check)
0x1d0xC004F51DOVER_BT_ENABLEmeasured0FM audio over Bluetooth (key to channel arbitration)
0x1e0xC004F51EANA_SWITCHmeasured0Analog audio path switching
0x1f0xC004F51FGETCAPARRAYmeasured0Capacitance array (hardware calibration)
0x210xC004F521I2S_SETTINGmeasured0I2S audio path settings
0x220xC004F522RDS_GROUPCNTmeasured0RDS group count
0x230xC004F523GET_LOGmeasured0Fetch the driver log
0x240xC004F524SCAN_GETRSSImeasured0Fetch the signal strength point by point during scanning (for drawing a spectrum)
0x250xC004F525SETMONOSTEROmeasured0Force mono/stereo
0x260xC004F526RDS_BC_RSTmeasured0RDS broadcast reset
0x270xC004F527CQI_GETmeasured0Channel quality
0x280xC004F528GET_HW_INFOmeasured0Hardware information
0x290xC004F529GET_I2S_INFOmeasured0Current I2S state
0x2a0xC004F52AIS_DESE_CHANmeasured0Whether it is on a desense channel
0x2b0xC004F52BTOP_RDWRmeasured0Top-level register read/write
0x2c0xC004F52CHOST_RDWRmeasured0Host-side read/write
0x2d0xC004F52DPRE_SEARCHmeasured0Pre-search
0x2e0xC004F52ERESTORE_SEARCHmeasured0Restore search
0x300xC004F530GET_AUDIO_INFOmeasured0Current audio path state
0x3c0xC004F53CSCAN_NEWmeasured0New version of scan
0x3d0xC004F53DSEEK_NEWmeasured0New version of seek
0x3e0xC004F53ETUNE_NEWmeasured0New version of tuning
0x3f0xC004F53FSOFT_MUTE_TUNEmeasured0Soft-mute tuning (no popping when changing stations)
0x400xC004F540DESENSE_CHECKmeasured0Desense detection
0x460xC004F546FULL_CQI_LOGmeasured0Full CQI log
0xff0xC004F5FFDUMP_REGstatic inference-1 (no log printed)Dump registers

Statistics: of the 47 commands, 45 are confirmed by measurement (the kernel log printed the command name); 2 (STOP_SCAN / DUMP_REG) were inferred by static disassembly, return -1 when called, and print no log, so verify them once more before use.

Undefined ranges (calls return -1 with no log)

nr = 0x14~0x16, 0x19~0x1c, 0x20, 0x2f, 0x31~0x3b, 0x41~0x45, and 0x47~0xfe have no corresponding branch in the driver;
the ioctl takes the “Unknown FM IOCTL!” branch and returns -EINVAL.

2. How the command numbers were derived

2.1 Encoding rules

Take any command number and decode it with the _IOC macros to verify:

type is always 0xF5 and size is always 4, so the whole command set can be indexed by nr alone,
i.e. #define FM_IOCTL(nr) (0xC004F500 | (nr)).

2.2 Static route: reading the constants from the machine code of fm_ioctl()

fm_ioctl() was compiled by the compiler into a binary search, and each case looks like:

Two pitfalls you will certainly hit (both actually hit):

PitfallSymptomCorrect approach
movw only modifies the low 16 bitstaking the value of movw r3, #62729 alone yields a “half number” like 0xf509you must include the high 16 bits (the movt, or the result of the preceding sub chain); the true value is 0xc004f509
The print strings are not in .rodatafetching strings by .rodata offset failsuse objdump -r to read the relocation table: the format strings for the command names are in .rodata.str1.1

How to extract the command names: the fixed shape of each handler block is

and the format string template is always "FM_DRV: %s-%d -- ----<command name>----", so a full-string regex extracts the name precisely.

2.3 Dynamic route: using dmesg as the “arbiter of truth” (the final criterion)

In the driver, the first thing every case does is print its own name, and this printk line comes before the actual handler,
so even if the handler fails due to invalid parameters, the name is still printed — this is a zero-cost, truth-arbitrable verification:

The probe is minimal (ssh_tools/fmprobe.c):

The correct way to capture kernel logs: comparing dmesg | wc -l before and after is unreliable — on this device the SDIOTRAN subsystem floods the log at high frequency, and the ring buffer wraps around, causing missed reads (the first version of the scan therefore identified only 12/47).
You must first clear it with dmesg -c, then call, then read:

After switching to this method, one scan named 45/47 successfully.

2.4 Cross-validation: search for the same constant in the Android libraries

The vendor Android partition’s libfmjni.so contains the same batch of 0xC004F5xx literals (18 occurrences found by raw byte search),
which independently confirms from a third party that the encoding is not something we miscalculated:

⚠️ Directly grepping 0xc004f5xx in the objdump text finds nothing — movw/movt split it into two instructions.
Either search the raw bytes, or search for movt ... @ 0xc004.

2.5 Cross-conclusion of the static and dynamic routes

Static disassembly first produced 47 candidate constants, 31 of which resolved their names directly;
the remaining 16 (0x02/0x05/0x08/0x0c/0x0f/0x12/0x18/0x1d/0x1f/0x23/0x26/0x29/0x2c/0x30/0x3e/0x46)
were first inferred based on “the order of the command names in .rodata = ascending nr order”, and then all were confirmed one by one by measurement, with no errors.

3. Incidental finding: the driver actually provides a dual “AT command + ioctl” interface

The complete kernel log captured during a measured TUNE:

Three confirmable facts:

  1. What the driver sends to the chip over SDIO is AT text, in the format at+fm=<opcode>,<param>
    (at+fm=1,0 is 10 characters + NUL = 11 bytes, matching fm_sdio_write size: 11).
  2. The AT opcode is not the ioctl nr: TUNE‘s ioctl nr is 0x02, but its AT opcode is 1.
    They are two separate numbering schemes; do not mix them up.
  3. The driver contains parse_at_fm_cmd / parse_at_fm_num, indicating that /dev/fm also accepts direct write() of AT text
    — this is another way to bypass the ioctl (the fact that libengfm.so exports only fm_runcommand corroborates this).

⚠️ The full AT opcode table has not been calibrated yet: only power up -> at+fm=0 and TUNE -> at+fm=1,<freq> are confirmed so far.
Many commands in the scan print at+fm=12, whose semantics are unconfirmed (suspected to be a generic query frame).
Until the AT frame of every command has been captured once, the daemon must always use the ioctl, not AT text.

3.1 An important behavior: TUNE blocks for about 4 seconds

TUNE (with arg=0 at the time, i.e. an invalid frequency) returned -1 / ETIMEDOUT, and the log timestamps spanned

That is about 3.99 s, corresponding to the driver line seek Timeout(%d sec), fm seek end !.

Design implications:

  • TUNE/SEEK in the daemon must be placed in a separate thread; the UI thread must not wait synchronously;
  • the socket interface must have a timeout set (a pitfall hit on this project’s Bluetooth page: SO_RCVTIMEO);
  • the UI needs a “tuning in progress” state and a timeout fallback.

4. Direct impact on downstream design

Previous stateNow
操作手册 Step 2 = “obtain the ioctl command numbers (the number one blocker)”This step is complete; work can start from Step 3
daemon could not be codedyou can directly `#define FM_IOCTL(nr) (0xC004F500
OVER_BT_ENABLE / ANA_SWITCH semantics unknownthe command numbers are now determined (0x1D / 0x1E), so you can start A/B listening tests to confirm the path
no interface for scanning/fetching signal strengthSCAN 0x08 + SCAN_GETRSSI 0x24 are usable, and the UI spectrum can be drawn
changing stations popsSOFT_MUTE_TUNE 0x3F is usable

The daemon’s minimal closed loop (P0) needs only 8 commands:
IS_FM_POWERED_UP(0x18) → power up(0x00) → TUNE(0x02) / TUNE_NEW(0x3E) →
GETRSSI(0x07) → SETVOL(0x04) → MUTE(0x06) → ANA_SWITCH(0x1E) → power down(0x01).

5. Confirmed hard facts (no need to re-investigate)

ItemValue
Command encoding_IOWR(0xF5, nr, 4) = 0xC004F500 | nr
Total number of commands47 with branches (45 measured + 2 inferred)
Command name print formatFM_DRV: <func>-<line> -- ----<NAME>----
Command name print timingbefore the actual handler (hence usable as the arbiter of truth)
Device node/dev/fm (misc 10:23)
Chip communicationSDIO, AT text at+fm=<opcode>,<param>
TUNE blocking duration≈ 3.99 s (failure path, returns ETIMEDOUT on timeout)
GETCHIPID return value0x2341
Static tool availabilitythe device ships with objdump / readelf / nm / strings / gcc / python3
Android sidelibfmjni.so contains the same batch of constants; libFMHalSource.so handles PCM (/dev/snd/controlC%i)

6. Verified dead ends (do not retry)

ApproachResult
Looking for the FM driver source on the device❌ None; /tmp/linux-3.10.65 is a vanilla kernel tree with no Spreadtrum private FM source
Looking for fm.h / sprd_fm.h header files❌ None on the whole disk (find / -name '*.h' | grep -i fm only hits unrelated files)
Directly grepping the objdump text for 0xc004f5xx❌ the movw/movt split makes it unfindable; you must search the raw bytes or search movt @ 0xc004
Fetching the command name format strings from .rodata❌ they are actually in .rodata.str1.1; you must read the relocation table
Comparing dmesg | wc -l before and after to capture logs❌ the SDIOTRAN flood causes ring buffer wrap-around and silent missed reads; you must clear first with dmesg -c
Reusing the Android FM user-space libraries❌ they depend on the Android runtime (libcutils/libutils/binder) and cannot be ported directly

7. Still unconfirmed (do not treat as fact)

ItemWhy it must wait for measurement
The full AT opcode tableonly 2 confirmed; the semantics of at+fm=12 are unknown
The exact command numbers of STOP_SCAN / DUMP_REGstatic inference, not confirmed by measured prints
The structure/dimension of each ioctl’s parametersthis round used all-zero parameters and did not calibrate them (e.g. TUNE’s frequency unit and step)
The value semantics of ANA_SWITCH / I2S_SETTING / OVER_BT_ENABLErequires human-ear A/B listening confirmation
Whether it depends on headphones as the antennarequires a field test tuning to a strong-signal station without headphones plugged in
The valid range and thresholds of RSSImust be calibrated by measurement; do not copy generic thresholds from the internet

8. Reproduction scripts (engineering scripts outside AI工作流)

ScriptPurpose
ssh_tools/fm_ioctl_extract.pyreverse-engineers command numbers↔names by static disassembly (including fixes for the two pitfalls: the movw high bits and .rodata.str1.1)
ssh_tools/fm_re_full.pycommand name completeness check + Android library raw-byte cross-validation
ssh_tools/pull_disasm.pypulls the fm_ioctl disassembly down locally for manual reading
ssh_tools/fmprobe.cminimal ioctl probe on the device
ssh_tools/fmprobe_sweep.pyfull measured scan (using the dmesg -c clearing method)
ssh_tools/fm_any.cgeneric /dev/fm ioctl probe (fm_any --seq 30:0 29:0)
ssh_tools/fm_tune_probe.c + _run.pydumps the 32-byte arg structure written back by the ioctl (to determine what the driver wrote)
ssh_tools/fm_seek_probe{,2}.c + _run.pySEEK parameter matrix / start point and direction semantics calibration (see 0.1 and the dedicated article for details)
ssh_tools/fm_at_probe.c + _run.pyverifies write(/dev/fm) writing AT text (conclusion: EINVAL)
ssh_tools/fm_sigcmd_trace.pytests signal-class commands under a clean dmesg to see whether there is SDIO traffic
ssh_tools/fm_rssi_sweep.py / fm_rssi_trace.pymulti-frequency RSSI scan / complete driver log of a single tune+RSSI

The same technique can be reused directly on peripherals that “have a driver but no source”, such as GPS / NFC / sensors.

One-line summary: the command numbers were not lost, just hidden in the machine code of the .ko;
static disassembly to locate candidates + single-step measured calls with all-zero parameters + dmesg -c clearing to capture logs —
three steps settle all 47 commands. The only hard blocker is removed, and you can start writing the daemon.

entry.title: FM radio: field-tested conclusions on SEEK and signal strength
entry.content:
FM radio: field-tested conclusions on SEEK / signal strength / AT text direct writes

Device: Spreadtrum SC9832A (Alpine Linux / armv7l), FM chip Unisoc Marlin2 combo,
driver marlin_fm.ko, node /dev/fm, ioctls uniformly encoded as _IOWR(0xF5, nr, 4) = 0xC004F500 | nr.
Tested on: 2026-09-22. All conclusions come from on-device tests; the arbiter of truth is the driver’s own dmesg (fm_write_buf / parse_at_fm_cmd).

0. Summary in one table

What you want to doFeasible?Reason
Power-up / tuning / volume / mute✅POWER_UP(0x00) / TUNE(0x02) / SETVOL(0x04) / MUTE(0x06) really send SDIO
Station seeking (next station)❌the driver truncates SEEK(0x03)‘s start frequency to 1 byte, so in-band frequencies cannot be passed in; field tests show only 2 fixed return values
Reading the signal strength❌GETRSSI(0x07), the only signal-class command that really sends SDIO, always times out after 4.2s and its return value barely changes; all other signal-class commands are empty shells
Writing AT text to bypass the ioctl❌write(/dev/fm) always returns -1 / EINVAL(22); the driver does not accept AT text from user space

1. SEEK (0x03) — the parameter is truncated, so it cannot be used for station seeking

1.1 Parameter structure (same as TUNE)

1.2 The AT frames the driver actually sends

The driver takes only the low byte of freq (u16) when assembling the AT frame (this is a driver bug):

freq we passWhat the driver actually sendsChip response frameThe “found frequency” the driver writes back to tail[0..1]
974 (97.4MHz)at+fm=4,0,2063,139,0,9250925 = 92.5MHz
875 (87.5MHz)at+fm=4,0,1073,139,0,9250925
1080 (108.0MHz)at+fm=4,0,563,139,0,9250925
900、1000at+fm=4,0,132 / ,2323,139,0,9250925
0at+fm=4,0,03,139,0,103101031 = 103.1MHz
  • In at+fm=4,<p2>,<p3>, p2 is always 0: changing zero/band/one/pad all to 1/2 makes no difference.
  • p3 = freq & 0xFF, so in-band frequencies (875~1080) can never be passed in.
  • The result is independent of the “current frequency”: first TUNE to 87.5 / 97.4 / 100.0 / 103.1, then SEEK(0),
    and all four calls return 103.1.

1.3 Behavioral model

  • p3 == 0 → always returns the opposite extreme of the 92.5MHz band (103.1MHz)
  • p3 != 0 → always returns 92.5MHz

In other words, SEEK degenerates into “pick one of two fixed values”; it is not “search up/down from the current frequency for the next station”.
Do not turn it into a “seek stations” button in the UI.

  • Timing: about 1.43 s per call (at+fm=4 sent → parse_at_fm_cmd: fm seek event have come freq=...).
  • The value in the driver log line FM seek freq =0 is always 0, regardless of the freq passed in → do not use it as a criterion.
  • SEEK_NEW(0x3d) only prints a log and then sends at+fm=12 (a generic query frame); SCAN(0x08) / SCAN_NEW(0x3c)
    return 0 with zero SDIO traffic → all are empty shells/placeholders.
  • STOP_SCAN(0x09) always returns -1 / EINVAL(22).

1.4 Probes

  • ssh_tools/fm_seek_probe.c + fm_seek_probe_run.py — parameter variant matrix + write-back structure dump
  • ssh_tools/fm_seek_probe2.c + fm_seek_probe2_run.py — start point/direction semantics verification (together with TUNE)

2. write(/dev/fm) writing AT text — rejected by the kernel

The driver contains parse_at_fm_cmd / parse_at_fm_num, and on the Android side libengfm.so exports only
one symbol, fm_runcommand, so it looks as though “you can write AT text directly to bypass the ioctl”. Field tests say no:

dmesg contains no fm_write_buf record at all → the request was rejected before entering the driver, with no SDIO traffic.
Conclusion: this path does not work; do not spend time on it. Probe: ssh_tools/fm_at_probe.c + fm_at_probe_run.py.

3. Signal strength / signal-class commands — none of them usable

CommandCommand numberField-test verdict
GETRSSI0x07the only one that really sends SDIO (at+fm=13); the chip replies 123~125, but the ioctl always returns -1 / ETIMEDOUT(110) and always takes 4.2s; the return value barely changes across 10 frequencies → cannot serve as a signal strength table
SCAN_GETRSSI0x24empty shell (printk only)
CQI_GET0x27empty shell
GETMONOSTERO0x0dempty shell
GETGOODBCNT / GETBADBNT0x0f / 0x10empty shell
GETBLERRATIO0x11empty shell
IS_DESE_CHAN0x2aempty shell
SOFT_MUTE_TUNE0x3fhas an effect (suppresses pops when changing stations), but does not write back a usable signal strength

The second field in the TUNE response is not the signal strength: at+fm=1,9740 → 0,164,0,9740;
tuning the same frequency repeatedly yields two different values, 164 and 139; different frequencies all land near 139~140;
and the driver does not write this response back to user space at all (after the ioctl returns, the arg structure is unchanged).
→ Verdict: it is not a stable signal strength indicator and cannot serve as a signal table.

Downstream impact: the radio page should no longer draw a “signal bar”.
The current version has been changed to the fixed text “this device does not provide signal strength queries”, and the rssi polling after every tune has been removed (it used to waste 4.2s each time).

4. Related: FM audio output is dead as well

See FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原.md and outputs/FM收音机_进度快照_20260922.md:

  • FM audio-class ioctls (OVER_BT_ENABLE 0x1d / ANA_SWITCH 0x1e / I2S_SETTING 0x21 …)
    in marlin_fm.ko just printk and return (disassembly of fm_ioctl shows R_ARM_CALL calling only 7 functions, with no audio path functions).
  • The whole-device codec (sprdphone card1) DAPM route table is missing HPL/HPR/SPKL/SPKR,
    the only reachable endpoint is EAR, and it never powers up Analog/Digital Power (bias_level=Off stays Off).
  • All 8 capture devices return readi -5 (EIO); read(/dev/fm) only returns a 688B RDS data block.
    → FM audio can neither make sound nor be digitized into the host. There is no solution in user space.

5. Constraints for the app design (copy directly)

  1. Do not provide a “seek stations” button in the UI — SEEK is uncontrollable and would make people think a station was found.
  2. Do not draw signal strength in the UI — the hardware does not provide it; drawing it would be lying.
  3. Do not poll rssi — each poll wastes 4.2s.
  4. Do not try writing AT text — EINVAL.
  5. The usable and verified feature set: state / on / off / tune <kHz> / vol <0-15> / mute <0|1> / chipid / rds.
  6. For any decision on “should we modify the kernel for this”, first read §4 of this article — the bottleneck for audio output lies in the codec’s DAPM route, not in the FM driver.

Copyright: This article is an original work by whiteleibniz (organized with AI assistance). All rights reserved. Please credit the source and keep the original link: https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: FM radio bring-up: work process summary
entry.content:
Spreadtrum SC9832A FM radio bring-up — work process summary

Audience: anyone who needs to understand “how this solution was arrived at” (including AI that takes over later)
Stage note: this article records the exploration and design stage of 2026-09-22; it has not yet entered the implementation and sound/ear verification stage
Core value: it records the basis for key judgments, which detours were taken, and what was deliberately not done — this has more reuse value than the “conclusions” themselves

1. Task background and initial goals

WiFi and Bluetooth have both been brought up (on the same combo chip), and now we need to add an FM radio feature to the same LVGL demo,
with a “classic radio app layout” covering three blocks: entry and icon, page layout, and feature list,
and produce a full set of Chinese documents following the document types of AI工作流/02_蓝牙打通/docs, placed under 03_收音机/docs.

The initial understanding had only one input: “this device’s WiFi, Bluetooth, and FM are integrated on the same chip (SDIO enumeration 0x2331)”.

2. Analysis framework: first split “can FM be done” into five layers

Instead of rushing to draw the interface, we first established a layered model for judging feasibility:

The value of this layering: it lets us judge before starting work whether “this is building a wheel from scratch or wiring out something that already exists” —
and the answer determines the nature of the whole project and the amount of work.

3. The assault process (by timeline)

Phase A: confirming the hardware exists — only one SDIO device

There is only one SDIO device on the bus, confirming the “three-in-one, sharing SDIO” claim.

Phase B: a surprise discovery — the FM driver was loaded long ago

This was the most important turning point of this round: FM was originally thought to be a brand-new feature never touched before,
but it turned out the driver not only exists but is depended on by the WiFi driver sprdwl (meaning its loading is normal and automatic).

Immediately after:

The device node is already registered.

💡 By this point the conclusion had clearly changed: this job is not “bringing up the FM chip”, but “wiring out a feature that is already running”.

Phase C: fully mapping the driver’s capabilities — inferring with strings + nm

Because the device has no vendor source (/tmp/linux-3.10.65 is a vanilla tree), only symbol-level forensics could be used:

Three commands obtained all the key facts:

  1. 40+ command names (TUNE/SEEK/SCAN/GETRSSI/MUTE/SETVOL/ANA_SWITCH/I2S_SETTING/OVER_BT_ENABLE/RDS_*)
  2. Complete RDS parsing functions (rds_get_ps station name, rds_get_rt text, rds_get_pty, rds_get_af alternative frequency, rds_get_ct, rds_get_ews emergency broadcast…)
  3. Official description: SDIO radio driver for marlin2 FM Radio Receivers, share SDIO with BT/WIFI

The last line is decisive: it turned “shares SDIO with WiFi/Bluetooth” from a speculation into the chip vendor’s official statement,
directly supporting the later series of designs such as “firmware depends on WiFi, power-up depends on the existing chain, and auto-start must queue”.

Phase D: an additional clue — the AT command style

parse_at_fm_cmd / parse_at_fm_num were found in the driver; on the Android side, libengfm.so exports only one symbol, fm_runcommand.

The two echo each other, suggesting FM control may follow the AT command style (writing command strings to the node).
This clue later became the breakthrough: the same set of constants exists as literals in libfmjni.so,
providing independent cross-validation of the command number encoding (see §2.4 of “FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原” for details).

Phase E: audio routing — finding the FM-dedicated PCM, and also finding there are no command-line tools

Confirmed the existence of an FM-dedicated PCM device (card 1 device 4, playback only).

But the same round discovered: no amixer / tinymix / aplay, only libasound.so.2.
→ Conclusion: the audio path can only be operated by writing C code; it cannot be debugged from the command line. This significantly changed how the audio layer had to be worked on.

At the same time, the symbols of libFMHalSource.so on the Android side (pcmHandle + FMHalThread::threadLoop + RingBuffer)
revealed Android’s audio architecture: start a thread to read from PCM → ring buffer → output. Our own daemon must replicate the isomorphic logic.

Phase F: confirming “there is no ready-made user space” (to avoid reinventing the wheel)

→ We must write the daemon ourselves. At the same time, confirmed that Android’s FM libraries cannot be used directly (they depend on the Android runtime).

Phase G: UI integration points — following the Bluetooth pattern

Read launcher_page.c / bluetooth_page.c / lv_page_manager.h and confirmed three things:

  1. The desktop grid order is determined by the s_apps[] array (not by enum values), so inserting after the Bluetooth item automatically places it right after Bluetooth;
  2. The page registration pattern is lv_page_t g_xxx_page = { .onCreate, .onPause, .onDestroy, ... };
  3. The page manager explicitly stipulates: in onDestroy you must clear your own timers/callbacks, but do not delete page->root.
    This directly determined the “background playback” design: neither onPause nor onDestroy may stop the station.

Phase H: font constraints — an easy place to crash

The real metrics of lv_font_cn_16 were found: line_height = 31px，base_line = 9px (nominally 16px).
The project history already includes rework caused by “hardcoding the line height at 16px, which clipped Chinese text”.
→ All y coordinates in this round were recomputed on the 31px grid, and a red line was made explicit in the documentation (no “visual fine-tuning” back to a 16px grid).

4. Review of key decisions (why done this way)

DecisionReason
Not rewriting the protocol stack, only a thin daemonthe RF/demodulation/RDS are all done in the chip and the driver; user space only needs to send commands
The daemon exposes a unix socket text protocolit mirrors the already-verified bt_user_daemon exactly, with zero extra cognitive cost for the team; and the socket timeout pitfall has already been hit
Systematically mirror the Bluetooth daemon’s socket path naming (/tmp/fm_ctl.sock)consistency first
Channel arbitration listed as P0all three share the audio output; without it, cross-talk is inevitable and users will certainly hit it
The UI uses RDS data (PS station name / RT scrolling)the driver capability already exists and is this solution’s differentiator; not using it degrades the UI to “just numbers”
All coordinates on the 31px line-height gridavoids this project’s existing Chinese-clipping rework
An extra interface specification document was addedthe reference directory has no UI-class document, but the core of this round’s requirement is the UI, so a nonexistent template cannot be forced
Explicitly listing the “unknowns”when key information is missing, writing “to be confirmed” has more engineering value than pretending to know; but anything you can work out yourself should not be listed as unknown

5. Final outcomes and consolidation

5.1 Deliverables

7 documents under AI工作流/03_收音机/docs/:

DocumentPurpose
FM收音机_LVGL界面设计与交互规格.mdCore: entry icon / page layout / feature list (corresponding to requirements ①②③)
FM收音打通_AI指导手册.mdhard facts + execution flow + decision table, preventing repeated investigation
FM收音芯片打通_操作手册.mdstep-by-step executable commands
FM收音芯片打通_故障排查手册.mdlayered quick-reference table
HT0FM收音原理与移植学习Wiki.mdprinciples and migration methodology
FM收音启动流程_安卓vsAlpine对比.mdhow Android does it vs how we do it
FM收音拉起_部署交付文档.mdartifact inventory and deployment steps
FM收音打通_工作过程总结.mdthis article

5.2 Consolidated hard facts (directly reusable)

  • Marlin2 combo chip, 0x2331, WiFi/Bluetooth/FM share SDIO (as evidenced by the vendor description);
  • marlin_fm.ko is loaded and depended on by sprdwl, and /dev/fm = misc 23 is registered;
  • complete ioctl command name inventory + complete RDS function inventory;
  • FM-dedicated PCM: 01-04 Dfm sprd-codec-fm-4 (playback only);
  • no ALSA command-line tools, only libasound.so.2;
  • no ready-made FM user space, and the Android libraries cannot be reused directly;
  • lv_font_cn_16 line height 31px; the page’s onDestroy must not delete root.

6. Lessons learned (reusable for other modules)

  1. Before starting work, first judge clearly whether “this is new construction or wiring out”.
    The single sentence “FM shares a chip with WiFi” actually hides the information that “FM may already be ready”; starting from scratch without investigation wastes a lot of work. This round, a single lsmod command reversed the nature of the whole project.

  2. No source does not mean no information.
    Two cuts with strings + nm on the .ko reconstruct the command name table and function table. Compared with hunting for driver source everywhere (we confirmed the kernel tree on the device is vanilla, a wasted search), this trick is much faster and more reliable.

  3. The vendor’s description= is the best evidence.
    The single line share SDIO with BT/WIFI settled the entire design of resource mutual exclusion and dependencies. When looking for evidence, prioritize this kind of “words written by the author”.

  4. Look for “ready-made tools” first, then decide whether to build.
    We confirmed there was no FM user-space tool on the whole disk before deciding to write a daemon — avoiding reinventing the wheel; at the same time, we confirmed the Android libraries could not be used directly, avoiding a detour.

  5. Unavailable tools must be discovered early.
    The absence of amixer was found during the planning stage; if it had only been discovered while debugging audio, the entire troubleshooting approach of “assuming the mixer can be driven from the command line” would have been void.

  6. List the unknowns explicitly — but distinguish “truly unknown” from “too lazy to check”.
    Six items were initially listed as “to be measured”, of which the ioctl command numbers later proved to be completely self-solvable:
    the .ko is not stripped, and disassembly + measurement settles all of them.
    Lesson: “ask the vendor for it” often just means the forensics path was not found; it should not be written into the blockers so early.
    The remaining 5 items (headphone antenna, OVER_BT_ENABLE semantics, RSSI thresholds, etc.) are the ones that truly require on-device work.

  7. Respect existing patterns.
    UI navigation uses lv_start_activity, the daemon uses a socket text protocol, pages use lv_page_t — all copied from existing successful solutions. The less “innovation” in a new module, the smaller the error surface.

7. Current status and next steps

Completed: the hardware/driver/audio/UI integration points are all mapped, and the design proposal and document family are produced.

The original number one hard blocker has been removed: the ioctl command numbers have all been reverse-engineered and confirmed by measurement (completed in an added phase).
The command names were known but the numbers were not. Recommended by priority:

  1. Ask the vendor for header files → no longer needed: all 47 command numbers have been obtained by self-disassembling the .ko + measurement;
  2. reverse-engineer from the Android-side libengfm.so / libFMHalSource.so (together with strace inside the chroot);
  3. controlled single-step probing (locate by the ----<命令名>---- prints in dmesg).

With the command numbers in hand, proceed in the order of Step 3→6 of FM收音芯片打通_操作手册.md; all other stages are unobstructed.

Copyright: This article is an original work by whiteleibniz (organized with AI assistance). All rights reserved. Please credit the source and keep the original link: https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: FM radio bring-up: deployment and delivery document
entry.content:
FM radio bring-up — deployment and delivery document

Audience: engineers taking over deployment/maintenance
Note: this document describes the target delivery state. Currently (2026-09-22) we are at the design and planning complete, not yet implemented stage;
items marked “已存在” in the text are measured and confirmed, while items marked “待产出” are the deliverables to be created in this round
Core value: it states in one go “exactly what is to be delivered, where it goes, and how to verify it”

1. Full chain picture (who brings up whom)

Key dependency: fm_radio_daemon must be ordered after the WiFi/power-up chain.
Because FM shares SDIO with WiFi/Bluetooth (the driver states share SDIO with BT/WIFI), every command fails when the chip is not powered.

2. Artifact inventory

2.1 Device side (already exists, verified by measurement → do not implement again)

ItemCurrent stateVerification command
SDIO enumeration✅ 0x2331cat /sys/bus/sdio/devices/*/device
FM driver marlin_fm✅ loadedlsmod | grep marlin_fm
/dev/fm node✅ misc 23grep -w fm /proc/misc
/dev/log_radio✅ misc 35grep log_radio /proc/misc
RDS parsing capability✅ built into the drivernm /lib/modules/marlin_fm.ko | grep rds_
FM PCM✅ 01-04 Dfm sprd-codec-fm-4cat /proc/asound/pcm | grep -i fm
Android reference libraries✅ /mnt/android_sys/lib/*.sols /mnt/android_sys/lib/libfm*
FM user-space tools❌ do not existls /usr/bin | grep fm (no output)

2.2 To be produced (this round’s deliverables)

TypeFilePlacement
Header filefm_ioctl.h (the command numbers have been reconstructed and it can be generated directly)device /home/lvgl_demo/lvgl_demo/libs/fm/
daemon sourcefm_radio_daemon.csame as above + archive to AI工作流/03_收音机/src/
LVGL pageradio_page.c / radio_page.hdevice lv_pages/ + archive to src/
Auto-start scriptfm_radio.start or openrc servicearchive to AI工作流/03_收音机/deploy/
Configuration/etc/fm_radio.conf (last frequency/volume/favorites)device runtime; the source includes a default template
Documentation8 documents in this document familyAI工作流/03_收音机/docs/

⚠️ Project convention: only final artifacts that can be deployed and run directly are collected; temporary probe scripts are not archived.
Therefore the deploy/ and src/ directories are populated only after the implementation produces output; no empty directories are created now just to fill space.

2.3 Three changes to existing code

Per FM收音机_LVGL界面设计与交互规格.md §3.2:

  1. lv_pages/launcher_page.c: new include
  2. lv_pages/launcher_page.c: insert the radio into the s_apps[] array after the Bluetooth item
  3. lv_pages/launcher_page.c: add case LAUNCHER_APP_RADIO: to the open_app switch

Files not to be changed: main.c (note it is this repo’s only CRLF file; it is unaffected this round),
lv_pm/lv_page_manager.h, and the already-brought-up WiFi/Bluetooth chain.

3. New device deployment steps (from scratch)

Step 0 Low-level health check (everything must be green)

If any item does not match → go back to 01_WiFi打通/docs/WiFi芯片打通操作手册.md and do not continue.

Step 1 Obtain the ioctl command numbers (completed)

For the results, see FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原.md; you can write fm_ioctl.h directly from them.

Following the three routes in §8 of FM收音打通_AI指导手册.md (vendor header files / Android library reverse-engineering / controlled probing),
produce fm_ioctl.h. Without this step, nothing after it can begin.

Step 2 Compile and deploy the FM daemon

Step 3 Socket smoke test

Expected: OK OFF → OK ON → OK 97400 → OK <value> → OK 8.

Step 4 Audio output (confirmed by human ear; logs are not an acceptable substitute)

At the same time, confirm: whether headphones must be plugged in as the antenna (tune to the strongest station without headphones and listen).

Step 5 Compile and deploy the LVGL radio page

⚠️ To judge whether make succeeded, do not use make | tail‘s $? (that is tail’s exit code); you must use make > log 2>&1; echo MAKE_RC=$?.

Step 6 Boot-time auto-start

See the openrc service in §7 of FM收音芯片打通_操作手册.md; be sure to declare in depend() that it is ordered after the WiFi/power-up chain.

4. Verification criteria (all met = deployment successful)

#ItemCriterionBasis
1Low levelSDIO/driver/node all three OK§Step 0 commands
2daemonthe four basic socket commands workStep 3 expected output
3Tuningcan TUNE to a locally known strong-signal stationOK <freq>
4Sound outputthe broadcast is heard by human earlogs are not an acceptable substitute
5Station seekingseek can find the next station; scanning shows progress and can be interruptedUI behavior
6Signal strengthRSSI varies with frequency and is discriminatingthresholds must be calibrated first
7Channel arbitrationswitching between any two of FM/A2DP/local has no cross-talkhuman ear
8Background playbackreturning to the desktop does not stop the stationhuman ear
9UIthe desktop icon is after Bluetooth; the frequency/dial/favorites display correctlyhuman eye (including the icon glyph, not a tofu block)
10Auto-startautomatically available after rebootreboot verification

Among them, items 4, 7, and 9 must be confirmed by human eye/ear — this project’s troubleshooting discipline explicitly does not accept “log OK” as a pass criterion.

5. This round’s “known unknowns” (an honest list)

When taking over the deployment, read this table first; these are items that are not yet confirmed and must not be treated as established facts:

#Unknown itemWhy it matters
1ioctl command numbersresolved (see “FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原”)
2Whether it depends on the headphone antennadetermines whether a “please insert headphones” UI state is needed
3OVER_BT_ENABLE semanticsdetermines the arbitration logic
4Whether SETVOL is module gain or master volumedetermines the volume chain
5The dimension and thresholds of the raw RSSI valuesdetermines how the signal bar is drawn
6FM behavior on system suspenddetermines the feasibility of “keep listening with the screen off”
7Whether a 48px large-font bitmap is neededdetermines the main frequency display effect

6. One-line summary

Three layers are ready, two layers remain to be built. The firmware/driver/device nodes are all already present;
what this round actually needs to deliver is these three: fm_radio_daemon (including fm_ioctl.h) + the LVGL radio page + openrc auto-start;
the precondition for starting, the ioctl command numbers, has been obtained by self-reverse-engineering,
and this project currently has no blockers, so implementation can begin directly.

Copyright: This article is an original work by whiteleibniz (organized with AI assistance). All rights reserved. Please credit the source and keep the original link: https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: FM radio bring-up: AI execution guide
entry.content:
Spreadtrum SC9832A (spd-box) FM radio bring-up — AI execution guide

Audience: AI assistants / engineers who need to build an FM radio on similar devices (Spreadtrum SC9832A + Marlin2 combo chip, Android kernel + Alpine user space)
How to use: read §1–§3 first to build context → verify layer by layer per §5 → execute per §6 → on failure, consult the decision table in §7
Core value: all hardware facts in this article have been obtained by on-device measurement; following it lets you skip all low-level investigation and go straight to the “write the daemon + draw the UI” stage; §3 explicitly marks the dead ends not to be walked again

1. Device and environment at a glance

ItemValue
Hostname / kernelspd-box / Linux 3.10.65 armv7l
System combinationkeeps the Android 6.0 kernel + switchroot to Alpine Linux user space
Wireless chipSpreadtrum Marlin2 combo WCN — WiFi + Bluetooth + FM one single chip, sharing SDIO
SDIO enumerationsdio:c00v0000d2331, device=0x2331 at /sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1
FM kernel drivermarlin_fm (loaded), /lib/modules/marlin_fm.ko, 17554 bytes
FM device nodes/dev/fm (misc, registered as 23 fm in /proc/misc), /dev/log_radio (35)
Display720×1280 portrait framebuffer, LVGL 9.6.0
SSHroot@<设备IP> (the password and IP are in the environment records; do not write them into documents)
Android vendor partitionmounted at /mnt/android_sys (usable as an information source and reference sample)

⚠️ Privacy red line: in all deliverables it is forbidden to include the SSH password, account, or real IP; always use the <设备IP> / <密码> placeholders.

2. Confirmed hard facts (no need to re-investigate; trust directly)

Each entry below notes how it was obtained; entries marked ✅ are measured conclusions that can be used directly as design basis.

2.1 Chip and resource sharing (the most critical item)

  1. ✅ FM shares SDIO with WiFi/Bluetooth and belongs to the same Marlin2 chip.
    Evidence 1: there is only one device on the SDIO bus, with modalias sdio:c00v0000d2331.
    Evidence 2: the verbatim driver module description (from strings /lib/modules/marlin_fm.ko):

    This directly determines that FM’s availability depends on the WiFi power-up chain (see §4 for details).

  2. ✅ The FM driver is already loaded, and marlin_fm is depended on by sprdwl (lsmod shows marlin_fm 17554 1 sprdwl).
    It is not an isolated module, so note WiFi’s dependency when unloading/reloading it.

  3. ✅ /dev/fm already exists and is registered (item 23 in /proc/misc); no need to insmod or mknod again.

2.2 Driver capability inventory (from the debug output of strings marlin_fm.ko)

The driver prints ----<命令名>---- for each ioctl command, from which the complete command set was reconstructed:

CategoryCommands
Basic controlTUNE、TUNE_NEW、SEEK、SEEK_NEW、MUTE、SETVOL、GETVOL、IS_FM_POWERED_UP
ScanSCAN、SCAN_NEW、STOP_SCAN、SCAN_GETRSSI、PRE_SEARCH、RESTORE_SEARCH
SignalGETRSSI、GETMONOSTERO、SETMONOSTERO、SOFT_MUTE_TUNE、DESENSE_CHECK、IS_DESE_CHAN、CQI_GET、FULL_CQI_LOG
Audio pathANA_SWITCH、I2S_SETTING、GET_I2S_INFO、GET_AUDIO_INFO、OVER_BT_ENABLE
RDSRDS_SUPPORT、RDS_ONOFF、RDS_GROUPCNT、RDS_BC_RST
Chip infoGETCHIPID、GET_HW_INFO、GETCAPARRAY、GETCURPAMD、GETGOODBCNT、GETBADBNT、GETBLERRATIO
Debug/mass productionRW_REG、TOP_RDWR、HOST_RDWR、DUMP_REG、EM_TEST、SIM_DATA、GET_LOG

⚠️ Honest labeling: the command names in the table above come from debug print strings inside the driver, so you can be confident these command branches really exist;
the command numbers were fully reverse-engineered and confirmed by measurement on 2026-09-22, see FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原.md:
uniform encoding _IOWR(0xF5, nr, 4) = 0xC004F500 | nr, with 45 of the 47 confirmed by on-device measurement.
The classification table in this section is kept as a functional view; for the actual numbers, always consult that document — do not guess.

2.3 RDS capability (from the function symbols of nm marlin_fm.ko)

The driver contains a complete RDS parser, the biggest value point of this project’s FM feature:

FunctionMeaningUI use
rds_get_psProgram Service, station name, 8 charactersdisplay the station name below the main frequency
rds_get_rtRadio Text, station text, 64 charactersscrolling subtitle
rds_get_ptyProgram Typesmall label (news/music/traffic)
rds_get_af / rds_get_af_methodAlternative Frequencyautomatically switch to the same station on a stronger-signal frequency
rds_get_pi_codeProgramme Identificationstation identifier
rds_get_tp_taTraffic Program / Announcementtraffic broadcast flag
rds_get_ctClock Timeoptional source for the status bar time
rds_get_di_msDecoder ID / Music-Speechstereo/speech flag
rds_get_ewsEmergency Warning Systememergency broadcast (has compliance significance)
rds_get_ptyn / rds_get_pin / rds_get_slcprogram type name / item number / SLCextended field
rds_get_oda / rds_get_oda_aid / rds_get_tdcOpen Data Applicationextended field
rds_get_eon / rds_get_eon_taEnhanced Other Networkscross-station information
rds_parser / rds_parser_init / fm_read_rds_dataparser body—

Other function symbols confirmed to exist: fm_open、fm_ioctl、fm_read、fm_write、fm_tune、fm_seek、fm_getrssi、fm_mute、fm_powerup、fm_powerdown、fm_rds_onoff、fm_sdio_read、fm_sdio_write、receive_tasklet、fm_suspend、fm_resume、parse_at_fm_cmd、parse_at_fm_num。

2.4 Current audio state (determines the channel arbitration design)

FactCurrent state
ALSA sound cards0 [alli2s] / 1 [sprdphone] / 2 [saudiovoip] / 3 [saudiolte]
FM-dedicated PCM01-04: Dfm sprd-codec-fm-4, playback only (no corresponding capture node)
Other PCMscard 0 has four i2s.x null-codec-dai-x, all supporting both playback + capture
ALSA user-space library✅ libasound.so.2 is present (you can write C to operate PCM and the mixer directly)
ALSA command-line tools❌ no amixer / tinymix / aplay / alsamixer — you must write code; you cannot drive the mixer from the shell

Inference: FM audio may go through the internal codec directly (corresponding to 01-04), or it may enter the codec via some I2S path.
The choice between ANA_SWITCH and I2S_SETTING can only be settled after measurement (see item 2 of the to-do list in §8).

2.5 The existing power-up chain (FM must attach to it)

The chain already established for Bluetooth/WiFi (recorded in the 01_WiFi打通 / 02_蓝牙打通 documents):

Here download burns the combo firmware (including the FM part) into the chip in one go.

3. Verified dead ends (do not retry; it wastes rounds)

RouteResultReason
Looking for the driver source of marlin_fm on the device❌ None/tmp/linux-3.10.65 is a vanilla kernel tree with only generic radio drivers such as wl128x and sf16fmr2, and no Spreadtrum private FM source; do not expect to read fm.h on the device
Looking for a ready-made FM user-space daemon/command-line tool❌ Nonels /usr/bin /usr/sbin /bin /sbin | grep fm produces no output, and no FM executable was found on the whole disk. You must write the daemon yourself
Using amixer/tinymix to switch the audio path❌ Not even installedsee §2.4; you can only write code against the ALSA lib or issue ioctls directly
Hoping to reuse the Android-layer FM libraries directly❌ Cannot run directly/mnt/android_sys/lib/ has libFMHalSource.so, libengfm.so, libfmjni.so, libradio*.so, but they depend on the Android runtime (binder/ALooper/sp<> etc.) and cannot be dynamically loaded directly on Alpine
Mistakenly thinking RDS does not exist❌ The opposite is truethe RDS parsing functions in the driver are quite complete (§2.3) and are this project’s FM differentiator; do not lose them

libengfm.so deserves a separate mention: it exports only one symbol, fm_runcommand. This hints that the vendor’s engineering mode operates FM by “running commands”
(echoing parse_at_fm_cmd / parse_at_fm_num in the driver) → suggesting FM control very likely follows the AT command style, which is the second viable route besides probing the ioctl numbers.

4. System model: five layers + per-layer verification criteria

Iron rule of layered troubleshooting: if any layer is not working, do not guess at the layer above. First confirm layer by layer top-down per §5, and only then start changing the UI.

5. Layer-by-layer verification commands (copy directly)

⚠️ The socket path /tmp/fm_ctl.sock above is the design goal mandated by this manual; it is not implemented yet.

6. Execution flow

StepActionOutputCompletion criterion
Step 0run all commands in §5 and confirm the state of layers ①–③exploration record/dev/fm exists, the driver is loaded, WiFi is up
Step 1Determine the ioctl command numbers CompletedFM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原.mdcan issue a successful TUNE against /dev/fm (command number: 0xC004F502)
Step 2write the FM daemon: exclusively own /dev/fm, wrap ioctl → socketfm_radio_daemon.cthe four commands state / open / tune / rssi work
Step 3write a minimal probe to verify SCAN and RSSI, and calibrate the signal strength thresholdscalibration recordcan obtain ≥3 local station frequencies and their strength values
Step 4Confirm the audio path (ANA_SWITCH vs I2S_SETTING vs OVER_BT_ENABLE)path decisionthe speaker really produces sound (must be confirmed by human ear)
Step 5implement channel arbitration (mutual exclusion among FM / A2DP / local playback)arbitration moduleswitching between any two of the three has no cross-talk
Step 6draw the LVGL radio pageradio_page.csee FM收音机_LVGL界面设计与交互规格.md
Step 7RDS display + favorites + persistence + background playbackcomplete appsee the feature list in §5 of the same document
Step 8openrc auto-start (depends on WiFi)service fileautomatically available after reboot

7. Failure → root cause → fix decision table

SymptomMost likely root causeFix
open /dev/fm fails with ENOENTmarlin_fm is not loadedinsmod /lib/modules/marlin_fm.ko, then confirm with lsmod
SDIO not enumerated / device cannot be readdownload did not run or the firmware download failedfix WiFi first: restart the logdw → download chain
WiFi is fine but FM does not respondmissing wcnd power-up or the chip as a whole is not poweredcheck ps | grep wcnd and rerun BT-OPEN
the ioctl returns -EINVALthe command number is wrong, or it fell into an undefined range (0x14~0x16/0x19~0x1c/0x31~0x3b etc.)check the nr against the conclusion table in FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原.md; then use dmesg | grep FM_DRV to see whether a different command name was printed
the ioctl succeeds but there is no soundthe audio path is not openStep 4: try each of the three paths, and use GET_AUDIO_INFO / GET_I2S_INFO to check the current state
there is noise / the sound is very quietthe volume chain is wrong or SETVOL is not the master volumecheck whether the main output volume still needs to be raised separately via the ALSA mixer
RSSI is always 0 / at an extremethe TUNE did not really succeed, or the headphone antenna is not connected (if the design depends on headphones)first verify that a single strong-signal station can be received normally; then investigate the antenna dependency
seek hangs without returningthe driver has a seek timeout (log (fmdrv) seek Timeout(%d sec), fm seek end !)the upper layer must also set a timeout fallback and provide a “no station found” UI
the LVGL page freezessocket I/O blocked the UI threadyou must set SO_RCVTIMEO/SO_SNDTIMEO (200ms) — a pitfall hit on this project’s Bluetooth page
FM stops working after rebootthe auto-start order runs before the WiFi/power-up chaindeclare the dependency in the service and start in order per Step 8
FM and Bluetooth A2DP make sound at the same timeno channel arbitration was doneStep 5; refer to §5.4 of the UI specification document

8. ioctl command numbers: solved (the former number one blocker)

Completed on 2026-09-22. For the specific results, see FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原.md.

Approach in brief: marlin_fm.ko is not stripped → disassemble the binary search tree of fm_ioctl() to read the constant candidates,
then use “single-step calls with all-zero parameters + dmesg -c clearing to capture logs” to confirm the command names one by one by measurement.
The three historical routes below are kept as a methodology memo:

RouteApproachAssessment
A. Ask the vendor for header files (least effort)request the Marlin2 platform’s FM user-space header files (usually called fm.h / sprd_fm.h) and the libfm library from the chip vendor/solution provider✅ first choice. With it, everything is clear
B. Reverse-engineer from the Android-side binariesthe Android partition has libengfm.so (exporting fm_runcommand) and libFMHalSource.so. Use nm/readelf to cross-examine how they call open/ioctl, or strace a native FM APK’s operation sequence once inside the Android chroot⚠️ feasible but requires touching the chroot environment; note this route is inference, and after getting the numbers you still must verify on the device
C. Brute-force the ioctls directlyiterate over the candidate command numbers, observe /dev/fm‘s return values and the ----<命令名>---- prints in dmesg, and see which number printed which command name⚠️ feasible but risky: sending ioctls indiscriminately may put the firmware in an abnormal state. It must be done when WiFi/Bluetooth are not carrying business traffic, and with a reset method available

🔒 Discipline: whichever route you take, confirm first on this machine/the Android side; do not write wrong command numbers into the daemon and then blindly tune on the emulator.

Other to-do items:

  1. Confirm whether headphones are needed as the antenna: this device’s ALSA has a dedicated FM PCM (01-04), hinting that internal passthrough may be possible, but it has not been measured.
    Criterion: tune to a strong-signal station without headphones plugged in and see whether sound comes out.
  2. Confirm the exact semantics of OVER_BT_ENABLE: does it mean “send FM audio to a connected Bluetooth device”, or “allow FM and BT to coexist”?
  3. Confirm the relationship between SETVOL and the actual output volume: it may only be the FM module’s internal gain.
  4. Confirm whether FM drops the station when the system suspends (the driver has fm_suspend/fm_resume) — this determines whether “keep listening with the screen off” can be implemented.

9. Red lines and operations discipline

  1. Forbidden: writing main.c back over SFTP and committing without checking the line endings: main.c is this repository’s only CRLF file, and writing it back converts it to LF,
    producing a fake change of 1618 “whole-file rewrite” lines in the commit. Before committing, always check that the two numbers from git diff --stat and git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat agree.
  2. Forbidden: writing the SSH password/account/real IP into documents.
  3. Forbidden: “if it looks right, it passes”: display/color/audio conclusions must be confirmed by human eyes/ears on the real device; they cannot be self-certified by “screenshots/decoding results being self-consistent”.
  4. Forbidden: doing socket I/O in an LVGL timer callback without a timeout.
  5. Forbidden: pkill -f with a string that would match its own command line (it would kill your own SSH session); always kill by PID.
  6. Before modifying /dev/fm-related logic, confirm the watchdog (lvgl_watchdog.sh) has been handled per procedure, to avoid interfering with experiments.

10. Inventory of tools already on the device (reuse; do not rebuild)

ToolPurpose
python3socket self-tests, writing probe scripts
nm / readelfanalyzing .ko and .so symbols (all facts in §2 were obtained this way)
stringsextracting debug strings from .ko (the command names were obtained this way)
libasound.so.2writing C to operate PCM / mixer (no amixer, so code is the only way)
/mnt/android_sysAndroid vendor partition; FM-related libraries under lib/ can serve as reference samples
/tmp/linux-3.10.65vanilla kernel tree, without Spreadtrum private FM source (see the dead ends in §3)

11. Future enhancement directions (currently incomplete)

DirectionDescription
Deep use of RDSPTY labels, AF automatic frequency switching, CT station clock, EWS emergency broadcast (the driver capabilities are in §2.3)
Internet radio integrationFM + WiFi dual mode; when WiFi is online, enhanced station information can be fetched
Recording/playbackFM audio to disk via PCM capture (must first confirm a usable capture node exists)
Multi-region bandsChina 87.5–108.0 / Japan 76–90 / European 50 kHz step

12. One-line summary

This device’s FM hardware, driver, and RDS parsing capability are all already in place and running (marlin_fm.ko is loaded, /dev/fm is registered,
and it shares the same Marlin2 chip with WiFi/Bluetooth); the only thing missing is “the middle layer”:
an FM daemon that wraps /dev/fm‘s ioctls into a unix socket, plus a radio page that can actually be drawn.
The only thing that used to block starting work (the ioctl command numbers) has been removed (§8);
everything that remains is routine engineering work: write the daemon, settle the audio path, do the channel arbitration, draw the UI.

entry.title: FM Radio Chip Bring-Up_Operation Manual
entry.content:
Unisoc SC9832A FM Radio Bring-Up — Manual Operation Guide

Audience: Engineers operating the device hands-on
How to use: Execute Step 0 → Step 6 in order; each step has an “expected output” — if the result does not match, stop and consult FM收音芯片打通_故障排查手册.md
Core value: Turns the judgments in the AI guide into commands that can be typed one by one, ensuring that different people get consistent results

0. Prerequisite Concepts (Build Intuition in 30 Seconds)

FM radio on this device is not “adding a new piece of hardware”, but “bringing out the third function on a chip that already works”.

  • Marlin2 is a WiFi + Bluetooth + FM three-in-one chip, and the three share the SDIO bus.
  • When WiFi was brought up, download had already burned the entire combo firmware, including the FM part, into the chip → no separate firmware flashing is needed for FM.
  • The marlin_fm.ko driver is already loaded, and the /dev/fm node already exists.
  • Therefore we do not need to touch the firmware or the driver; we only need to write a user-space daemon layer to operate /dev/fm, and then draw a UI.

1. Environment Preparation

1.1 Device State Confirmation

1.2 One-Command State Checkup

⚠️ If any of items 1–3 are missing, it means the underlying layers are not ready yet; first bring up WiFi according to 01_WiFi打通/docs/WiFi芯片打通操作手册.md,
and do not force FM here — because FM depends on the same combo firmware.

2. Step 1: Extract the Driver Capability List (Already Frozen; Can Be Skipped)

Expected: obtain command names such as TUNE / SEEK / SCAN / GETRSSI / MUTE / SETVOL / ANA_SWITCH / I2S_SETTING / OVER_BT_ENABLE / RDS_*,
as well as RDS functions such as rds_get_ps / rds_get_rt / rds_get_pty / rds_get_af.

Note: this step only obtains the command names. For the command numbers, see Step 2, which is already completed in this project;
consult the results directly in FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原.md.

3. Step 2: Obtain the ioctl Command Numbers — Completed (Formerly the Top Blocker)

See the results in FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原.md: unified encoding _IOWR(0xF5, nr, 4) = 0xC004F500 | nr,
with 45 of the 47 commands confirmed by measurement. The content below is retained as a methodology record (reusable when working on other peripherals).

Three approaches, in order of recommendation:

Route A (first choice): Request the header file from the original manufacturer/solution provider

Request target: the FM user-space header file (fm.h / sprd_fm.h) and accompanying lib for the Marlin2 platform. Once obtained, skip to Step 3.

Route B: Infer from the Android-side binaries

⚠️ What this route yields are inferred values; they must be verified on real hardware using the Step 3 probe: only when sent correctly will the corresponding ----<命令名>---- print appear in dmesg.

Route C: Controlled Probing

🔒 Iron rules:

  1. Before probing, make sure WiFi/Bluetooth are not carrying business traffic (sending ioctls at random may cause abnormal firmware state);
  2. Probe only one number at a time; do not spam in a loop;
  3. On any abnormality, immediately reset marlin_fm with rmmod/insmod (note that it is depended on by sprdwl, so that dependency must be handled as well).

Deliverable: fm_ioctl.h, containing all command numbers and data structures. This is the input for all subsequent work.

4. Step 3: Compile and Deploy the FM Daemon

4.1 Socket Self-Test (python3 on the device; socat is not available on this device)

Expected: OK OFF → OK ON → OK 97400 → OK <rssi value> → OK 8.

5. Step 4: Confirm the Audio Path (Must Be Confirmed by Ear)

Try the three paths in order, and confirm by ear whether each one produces sound:

#PathCorresponding ioctlApplicable
1Analog/internal codec passthroughANA_SWITCHDirect speaker output (default candidate)
2I2SI2S_SETTING / GET_I2S_INFOUse when an external codec is needed
3Over BTOVER_BT_ENABLEFM sound output from a Bluetooth device

⚠️ Success must not be judged from logs in this area:

  • TUNE returning OK does not mean there is sound;
  • You must actually listen. It is recommended to first lock onto the strongest local station as a baseline test.
  • Also confirm whether headphones must be plugged in to serve as the antenna: tune to a strong signal without headphones; if sound is produced, headphones are not required.

6. Step 5: Deploy the LVGL Radio Page

⚠️ Do not rely on the $? of make | tail for build success/failure (that is tail’s exit code); you must use make > log 2>&1; echo MAKE_RC=$?.
Note: extern/miniretro/ has no Makefile; use sh build.sh (unrelated to this task; do not touch it by accident).

7. Step 6: Boot Autostart (openrc)

⚠️ The autostart order is the most accident-prone part of this integration: download → wcnd → bt_once → bt_wake → bt_user_daemon → fm_radio_daemon.
If FM stops working after a reboot, first check whether it started too early (before the chip was powered).

8. Quick Reference for Common Nodes and Parameters

ItemValue
SDIO modaliassdio:c00v0000d2331
SDIO path/sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1
Driver module/lib/modules/marlin_fm.ko (Used by sprdwl)
Control node/dev/fm (misc 23)
Log node/dev/log_radio (misc 35)
FM PCMhw:1,4 = 01-04 Dfm sprd-codec-fm-4 (playback)
I2S PCMcard0 i2s.0~`i2s.3` (playback + capture)
daemon socket/tmp/fm_ctl.sock (chmod 0666)
daemon log/tmp/fm_daemon.log
Android reference libraries/mnt/android_sys/lib/{libengfm,libFMHalSource,libfmjni}.so
Main RDS fieldsPS (8-character station name) / RT (64-character text) / PTY / AF / CT / EWS

9. One-Sentence Summary

The underlying layers (① firmware ② power-up ③ driver) are all already in place, and the command numbers have been fully reverse-engineered (§3 / see also “FM收音ioctl命令表_逆向还原”).
This project has no remaining blockers; simply proceed step by step from Step 3.
