entry.title: GBA退出卡黑屏与FC被污染_前端分离
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_11 — GBA 退出卡黑屏，且 FC 被牵连（前端彻底分离）

项目内容
发现时间2026-09-23
修复时间2026-09-23
模块extern/miniretro/*（新增分离产物）、lv_pages/gba_game_page.c
涉及版本承接 bugfix_20260923_10 之后的现场
现象等级高（GBA 退出不可用，且把原本正常的 FC 一起带坏）

1. 问题现象

用户连续两轮反馈：

  1. 「退出逻辑还是有问题 还是卡黑屏」；
  2. 「把 GBA 的和 FC 的 miniretro 分开吧，FC 原来版本都是好用的，被 GBA 修改的污染了，
    导致 FC 的 miniretro 也不好用了，导致 FC 不能玩，退出莫名其妙。」

第 2 条是关键判断：两个游戏页共用一个前端二进制，改 GBA 必然波及 FC。用户的诉求
（物理隔离）比”继续在共用件上打补丁”更正确。

2. 影响范围

  • GBA 游戏页：退出后黑屏、退出键失效；
  • FC 游戏页：被同一份 miniretro 的改动连带影响，退出异常；
  • 根因层面：任何”多个页面共用一个可执行前端”的设计，都是这类跨模块污染的温床。

3. 根因分析

3.1 ★ 等待循环设了”跑满 N 秒就算退出”的上限（卡黑屏的直接原因）

gba_wait_thread 原来写成”等够一定时长就往下走”：

游戏正常跑满 3 秒，就满足”循环结束”这个条件，于是：

  1. hardware_keys_set_interceptor(NULL, NULL) 把按键拦截器摘掉 → 买单键不再被拦截 → 退不出游戏；
  2. app_runtime_set_lvgl_paused(false) 让 LVGL 恢复绘制 → 父进程抢回 fb0，与还在跑的游戏互相覆盖；
  3. 两者叠加 = 用户看到的「卡黑屏」，且只能重启。

这正是”FC 没问题、GBA 有问题”的分水岭：FC 页用的是阻塞式
while(waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) {...}（无上限），所以从来不误判。
GBA 页当初为了”快点恢复 UI”引入了上限，反而制造了 bug。

3.2 UI 恢复被绑在”子进程消失”上（把黑屏拉长）

本机内核回收 /dev/input/eventX 要几百毫秒，实测从发信号到收尸完成 ~455ms，
而画面在 ~40ms 就已交还。等收尸才恢复 UI，就白等了 400ms —— 这段时间屏幕全黑。

3.3 细节问题

  • gba_timer_cb 只 lv_obj_invalidate(lv_screen_active()) 一次，可能与 LVGL 恢复的
    时序错开而被吞掉（标志已消费、画面却没画回来）；
  • fb_restore() 调 FBIOPAN_DISPLAY 后不检查结果：若 yoffset 没真的归零，
    LVGL 会画在第 0 页而屏幕仍显示第 1 页 → 永久黑屏且完全静默，无法定位。

3.4 结构性根因：共用前端

FC 与 GBA 共用 extern/miniretro/miniretro。为 GBA 加的 双缓冲页翻转、pitch 寻址、
240×160 放行、音频重采样、退出信号处理 全都落在这一份共用产物上。FC 因此被反复牵连 ——
这是”改 A 坏 B”的必然结果，不是某一次改动没写好。

4. 修复方案

4.1 ★ 前端彻底分离（用户方案）

产物归属说明
extern/miniretro/miniretroFC 专用git checkout 恢复成仓库里的原始版本，此后永不重编、不被 GBA 改动触碰
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gbaGBA 专用含双缓冲/pitch/240×160/音频修正/退出修复
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.cGBA 源码
extern/miniretro/miniretro.cFC 源码已随二进制一并还原成原始版本
extern/miniretro/build.sh—**只编 miniretro_gba**，并在脚本头写明”不要再把产物写成 miniretro”

页面侧 gba_find_bin() 的首选路径改为 miniretro_gba，并保留 miniretro 作为兜底：

4.2 退出逻辑四项修复（只落在 GBA 页）

  1. 等待循环去掉时长上限，只认两个真实终止条件：

  2. 新增 exiting 标志：画面一交还就恢复 UI，不等收尸

  3. 恢复时连刷 3 帧，不依赖单次 invalidate：

  4. fb_restore() 校验翻页结果：只在 yoffset != 0 时才 pan，pan 后回读确认，
    不归零就打警告日志（把”永久黑屏且无任何线索”变成可定位）。

同时给等待线程加了”仍是我这一局的 pid”判断，避免上一局的线程醒来把新一局的状态清掉。

5. 验证方法与结果

5.1 分离结果校验（设备端）

项结果
miniretro 工作区 md5a95d9171d8d8b82a52c12ac84e68aaa2
git show HEAD:...miniretro md5a95d9171d8d8b82a52c12ac84e68aaa2（完全一致 = 已还原）
HEAD 版含 RELEASE_SIGNAL / on_quit_signal0 / 0（确认是纯 FC 版，不含 GBA 改动）
miniretro_gba md52b958d4f8fcec85b6f2668985848887b（与上者不同 = 真正分离）
体积miniretro 25648 B ／ miniretro_gba 35404 B
编译make -j2 RC=0，0 error

5.2 两个前端各自实跑（ssh_tools/split_verify.py）

前端核心画面（非黑像素比）退出码收尸耗时退出后 yoffset僵尸
FCminiretro（原版）fceumm0.600 ✓-15（被 SIGTERM 直接杀，原版行为）549 ms0 ✓无
GBAminiretro_gbamGBA0.380 ✓0（优雅退出）575 ms0 ✓无
  • FC 退出码 -15 符合”原版无信号处理”的预期；其页面侧在 120ms 后探测到进程已消失，
    直接恢复 UI —— 这正是用户记忆中”FC 原来好用”的表现。
  • GBA 侧 exiting 标志使 UI 在 ~125ms 即可恢复，收尸移到后台；yoffset 归零确认无黑屏隐患。
  • 恢复后 lvgl_demo ×1 + lvgl_watchdog ×1，单实例，无残留。

5.3 部署脚本的一处修正

gba_redeploy.py 用 ps -o pid,args | grep '<名>' 取 PID 来 kill，
而该命令自身的命令行含这个字符串 → 匹配到承载命令的 sh -c → 杀掉自己的 SSH 连接
（本次实测 ConnectionResetError）。已统一改为 ps -o pid,comm（承载 shell 的 comm 是 sh，
不会误伤），见 split_miniretro_gba.py / split_verify.py。

6. 回归风险

  • miniretro 已还原为原版：FC 侧要的任何未来改动都必须独立做，且不能再走
    “重编 miniretro” 这条路（build.sh 已只产 miniretro_gba）。若确需改 FC，
    应先 git checkout 一份到别的名字（如 miniretro_fc）再改，保持三者互不干扰。
  • **GBA 侧不再有”时长上限”**：等待线程在游戏运行期间会一直循环（每 5ms 一次，开销可忽略）。
    这是刻意选择 —— 宁可多转几次，也不能误判成”已退出”。
  • gba_reap_bg / onDestroy 两条收尸路径都可能对同一 pid waitpid，双方均已处理 ECHILD。
  • 本次未改渲染与音频链路，颜色、音质、帧率不应有变化。

7. 相关文件

文件说明
extern/miniretro/miniretroFC 专用前端，还原为 git 原版（25648 B）
extern/miniretro/miniretro.c同上，源码还原
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gbaGBA 专用前端（35404 B）
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.cGBA 源码（含退出修复）
extern/miniretro/build.sh改为只编 miniretro_gba，原子替换
lv_pages/gba_game_page.cgba_find_bin 优先 miniretro_gba；等待循环去上限；新增 exiting；连刷 3 帧
ssh_tools/split_miniretro_gba.py本次分离部署脚本（可复用）
ssh_tools/split_verify.py分离后双前端验证
bugfix_20260923_10上一轮回滚记录（其”UI 恢复等收尸”的做法由本次修正）

entry.title: GBA退出逻辑对齐FC
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_12 — GBA 退出逻辑改为与 FC 逐行一致（取消 GBA 专属分支）

项目内容
发现时间2026-09-23
修复时间2026-09-23
模块lv_pages/gba_game_page.c
涉及版本承接 bugfix_20260923_11 之后的现场（前端已分离）
现象等级中（无新故障，属”消除结构分歧”的收敛性修复）
触发方式用户明确要求：「你把 GBA 的改成 FC 的退出逻辑吧」

1. 问题现象

前端分离（bugfix_20260923_11）之后，GBA 与 FC 虽然各用一个二进制，但退出逻辑仍不是同一套：
GBA 页保留了一条 FC 页没有的”提前放行”路径（exiting 标志 + 后台收尸线程 + 画面连刷 3 帧）。

这条路径是 09→10→11 三轮故障中反复出问题的地方。用户据此判断”两边逻辑混在一起、退出莫名其妙”，
要求直接把 GBA 的退出逻辑改成 FC 那一套。

用户的判断是对的：FC 那套是唯一被实机长期验证过的退出路径，任何”改进版”目前都没有可信的验证基础。

2. 影响范围

  • lv_pages/gba_game_page.c：退出路径（gba_wait_thread / gba_exit_to_list / gba_timer_cb / 状态结构体）。
  • 不涉及 miniretro_gba（前端二进制不动），不涉及 FC 页（FC 页保持原样，一行未改）。
  • 结构层面：消除”同构组件之间的人为差异”——差异本身就是后续故障的藏身处。

3. 根因分析

3.1 修复前的四处差异（GBA 相对 FC 的额外复杂度）

#差异点FC 页GBA 页（修复前）
1等待判据阻塞 waitpid，只认”子进程真的消失”5ms 轮询，认 exiting 标志 或 子进程消失
2退出函数副作用只 SIGTERM → 120ms → SIGKILL追加 s_gba.exiting = true
3收尸兜底无（阻塞必然拿到尸）gba_reap_bg() 独立后台线程
4画面恢复lv_obj_invalidate() ×1invalidate() + for(3) lv_refr_now()

3.2 为什么这四处差异是风险

  • 第 1 处是 09/10/11 三轮卡死/卡黑屏的同一个病灶。只要等待判据里出现”标志位”或”时间上限”这类
    非硬事件，就存在”把仍在运行的游戏判成已退出”的可能，后果固定为两条：
    ① hardware_keys_set_interceptor(NULL) 摘掉按键拦截器 → 退出键失效，再也退不出游戏；
    ② app_runtime_set_lvgl_paused(false) 让 LVGL 抢回 fb0 → 与仍在运行的游戏互相覆盖。
    历史两版的差别只是”误判的触发条件不同”（时间上限 / 标志位被读到），本质同源。
  • 第 3、4 处是为第 1 处的时序问题打的补丁。提前放行意味着”标志已消费但子进程仍在碰 fb0”，
    于是不得不连刷 3 帧来抢画面、不得不另开线程收尸。改回硬事件判据后，这两个补丁不再有存在理由，
    留着反而是多余的失败面。
  • 结构性理由：FC 页这套逻辑经过长期实机验证；GBA 页却带着一条”只此一处”的路径。
    同一份设计意图在两处写法不同，未来任何一次修改都容易只改一边 —— 这正是 11 号文档里
    “共用二进制被改坏”那类问题的翻版，只是从”共享产物”变成了”共享语义、各自实现”。

3.3 代价的取舍（明确接受）

FC 那套的唯一代价是：恢复 UI 要等内核回收 evdev fd，实测发信号→收尸完成约 455ms
（其中子进程内部收尾 ~34ms，其余是内核固有开销）。09/10 两轮就是试图”省掉这几百毫秒”才出的故障。

本次明确选择承担这 ~400ms，换取”GBA 与 FC 行为逐行一致”。理由：

  • 455ms 的黑屏一闪在用户感受上属于”退出有一下停顿”，可接受；
  • 相比”偶发卡死、退出键失效、只能重启”，这个代价小得多；
  • 一致性带来的可验证性 > 几百毫秒的性能收益。

4. 修复方案

原则：GBA 页退出路径照抄 FC 页，不给任何专属分支。

4.1 gba_wait_thread() 改为阻塞 waitpid

安全性依据：上游 gba_exit_to_list() 保证 SIGTERM 后 120ms 必然补上 SIGKILL，
而 SIGKILL 不可捕获 ⇒ 子进程必然结束 ⇒ 阻塞的 waitpid 必然返回，不存在死等。

4.2 gba_exit_to_list() 去掉提前放行

4.3 删除 gba_reap_bg() 后台收尸线程

阻塞 waitpid 必然拿到尸，兜底线程没有存在意义。删除后同时消除”两处代码都去 child_pid
赋值”的竞态空间。

4.4 状态结构体去掉 exiting 字段

gba_state_t 的 exiting 及 gba_launch() 里对它的复位一并删除，字段布局回到与 fc_state_t 对齐。

4.5 gba_timer_cb() 画面恢复回到单次 invalidate

4.6 文件头注释重写

把”我们比 FC 更快”的叙述改成”刻意与 FC 完全一致，并说明为什么不再追求更快“，
同时把两轮失败方案（SIGUSR1 握手 / 时间上限）作为反例留在注释里，防止后来者再走一遍。

5. 验证方法与结果

5.1 代码一致性核对（本地）

  • grep -n "exiting\|reaped\|reap_bg\|lv_refr_now\|SIGUSR1\|RELEASE_SIGNAL" →
    仅命中注释内容，无任何代码残留；
  • gba_wait_thread() 与 fc_wait_thread() 逐行对照 → 结构、判据、恢复顺序、顺序注释全部相同，
    仅 s_gba / s_fc 前缀与缩进不同。

5.2 构建与部署（设备端）

ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.py（不带 --mini，只部署页面 + 编译 + 重启）：

检查项结果
make -j2MAKE_RC=0，error: 计数 = 0
二进制替换ATOMIC_OK（编到 .tmp 再 mv -f，原子）
部署前在跑的游戏无
重启后进程lvgl_demo ×1 + lvgl_watchdog ×1，单实例，无僵尸

5.3 实机功能验证（交由用户）

  1. 桌面 → GBA 游戏 → 选 ROM → 确认，进入游戏；
  2. 按买单键退出 → 预期约半秒黑屏一闪后回到游戏列表，退出键全程有效；
  3. 进入游戏后停留 5 秒以上再退出（重点：验证不再有”跑满 N 秒被误判”）→ 表现应与第 2 步相同；
  4. 再进一次并正常玩一段 → 退出，确认无残留黑屏、列表可继续操作；
  5. 对照 FC 游戏：进入 → 退出，行为应与 GBA 表现一致（同为”半秒黑屏一闪”）。

6. 回归风险

风险评估
退出比上一版慢约 400ms已明确接受，这是与 FC 对齐的必然代价，也是唯一被验证过的时序
单次 invalidate 是否够用FC 页同样只 invalidate 一次且长期正常；恢复时机现已与 FC 相同，判断为足够。若实机出现”退出后残留游戏画面”，则说明 GBA 侧 fb 清理与 FC 有差异，需从 miniretro_gba 的 fb_restore() 查，而不是再加连刷
阻塞 waitpid 会不会死等不会：SIGKILL 不可捕获，上游必然发出
pthread_create 失败的极端分支该分支（gba_launch 内）里是 waitpid(pid, NULL, 0) 且未先 kill，理论上会阻塞到游戏自行结束。FC 页存在完全相同写法，为保持逐行一致本次未改；属极低概率路径，如要修应两侧同时修
FC 页本次一行未改

7. 相关文件

文件说明
lv_pages/gba_game_page.c本次改动全部集中于此（退出路径 + 结构体 + 文件头注释）
lv_pages/fc_game_page.c参照基准，未改动
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gbaGBA 专用前端，未改动
ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.py部署脚本；本次顺带修正取 PID 方式（见下）
bugfix_20260923_11上一环：前端分离、卡黑屏根因

附：部署脚本的一处修正

gba_redeploy.py 原先用 ps -o pid,args | grep 'lvgl_demo' 取 PID 再 kill -9。
该命令经由 sh -c 执行，承载它的 shell 自身命令行里就含 lvgl_demo 字样 →
被 grep 匹配 → 杀掉自己 → SSH 连接被重置（上一轮部署时就断在这里）。
现改为 ps -o pid,comm | awk '$2=="lvgl_demo"{print $1}'：comm 是进程名（不含参数），
承载 shell 的 comm 是 sh，不会自匹配。miniretro 系列改用 $2 ~ /^miniretro/ 前缀匹配。

版权声明：本文为 whiteleibniz 原创文章（AI 协作整理），版权归 whiteleibniz 所有，转载请注明出处与原文链接：https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: GBA退出后卡死_页翻转残留
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_14 — GBA 退出后”卡死”（页翻转残留：屏幕定格在游戏画面）

  • 日期：2026-09-23
  • 现象：GBA 游戏退出后屏幕不黑（显示游戏画面），但界面永远回不来、按键像失灵，
    只能重启应用。用户描述为”不黑屏了，直接卡死”。偶发 —— 有时正常，有时必卡。
  • 影响面：lv_pages/gba_game_page.c、extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.c（GBA 前端）
  • 是否影响 FC：不影响（FC 用原版 miniretro，它从来不翻页）

1. 背景：两个驱动对”页”的理解不一致

设备 framebuffer 有 3 个虚拟页（yres_virtual=3840 = 3×1280）。

谁怎么用 fb0
LVGL（lv_linux_fbdev）只用 mmap 基址绘制 = 永远写第 0 页；vinfo.yoffset 在 init 时设 0 后再不改；源码里 FBIOPAN_DISPLAY 零命中
GBA 前端（miniretro_gba）用 FBIOPAN_DISPLAY 双缓冲页翻转消撕裂 → 前台在第 0/1 页之间来回切

关键推论：只要退出时前台停在第 1 页，LVGL 画什么都看不见 ——
因为 LVGL 永远往第 0 页写，而屏幕显示的是第 1 页。

2. 根因

  1. 前端每渲染一帧就翻一次页，**前台页是 0 还是 1 取决于”退出那一刻”**。
    实测抓帧：启动游戏后依次测到 yoffset=1280 → 0 → 1280 → 1280 → 1280（同一局游戏内）。
  2. 前端退出时本会在 fb_restore() 里翻回第 0 页（定点实测：SIGTERM 后 0.4s yoffset 由 1280 变 0），
    但父进程 gba_exit_to_list() 在 **SIGTERM 后 120ms 就补 SIGKILL**；
    而前端收尾里包含 core_deinit() —— 把 .sav 电池存档落盘到 SD 卡，写卡慢时远超 120ms。
  3. 一旦被 SIGKILL 打断 → 翻页没做 → 前台永久停在第 1 页 → 屏幕定格游戏画面 → “卡死”。

这解释了为什么它偶发：存档早就在页缓存里 → 收尾 <120ms → 正常；
真要写 SD 卡 → 被杀 → 卡死。

3. 证据

证据内容
源码lv_linux_fbdev.c:174 dsc->vinfo.yoffset = 0;（此后不改）、grep -n 'PAN' 零命中
抓帧图 shots/final/01..10：运行期 yoffset 在 0/1 间切换
定点实验单独跑 miniretro_gba：运行中 yoffset=1280 → SIGTERM 后 0.4s →0（说明前端收尾能翻页，问题只在”有没有机会走到”）
残留取证shots/guard/01：重启应用后抓到的”桌面”其实是页1 里的上一局游戏画面（yoffset=1280）—— 正是卡死的物质形态
排除项前端退出日志完整（收尾完成 t=30.8ms）、无僵尸、无崩溃循环、hardware_keys 的 EVIOCGRAB 幂等正常

4. 修复（三层兜底，全部”幂等 + 只在异常时才有动作”）

4.1 前端 miniretro_gba.c — fb_restore() 改为无条件翻回第 0 页

去掉”先读 yoffset、非 0 才翻”的分支：翻到第 0 页本身是幂等操作，
判断只会多一个可能出错的分支（虽然实测本驱动回读可靠，但没必要依赖）。
失败/翻不动时打印 ★ 翻回第0页失败，便于现场定位。

4.2 GBA 页 — 新增 gba_reset_fb_page()，父进程自己兜底翻页

打开 /dev/fb0，若 yoffset != 0 就 FBIOPAN_DISPLAY 到 0。
无论前端有没有被打死都成立 —— 这是治本的一层。在 3 处调用：

调用点作用
gba_wait_thread() 恢复段（set_lvgl_paused(false) 之前）游戏退出 → 恢复 UI 前先保证可见页 = 第 0 页
gba_on_destroy()页面离场时再兜一次
gba_on_create()进页面先归零（若上次异常留下页1 残留）

4.3 补刀时间 120ms → 600ms

给”落存档 + 翻页”留出时间。补刀必须保留（子进程真挂死时，没有 SIGKILL 会让阻塞的
waitpid 永不返回）。这 600ms 只花在按键线程里，不拖慢 UI 恢复。

4.4 恢复重绘后补一次 lv_refr_now(NULL)

只 invalidate 的话要等下一轮 lv_timer_handler 才真正出图；立即刷一帧，
消除”标志被消费、画面却没画回来”的窗口。

5. 验证

项结果
定点：前端运行中 / SIGTERM 后 yoffset1280 → 0 ✓
关键推论（运行期会在页1）实测同一局内多次采到 yoffset=1280 ✓
编译前端 RC=0、主程序 MAKE_RC=0 / ERR=0 ✓
部署原子替换 BIN_OK；设备源码 gba_reset_fb_page×6、前端”无条件翻回”×1 ✓
运行态lvgl_demo×1 + lvgl_watchdog×1；退出后 yoffset=0；无僵尸 ✓
正常路径兜底日志不出现（前端自己已翻回 0）→ 兜底是纯保险，不改变正常行为 ✓

6. 反模式记录（本次新增，已并入 skill）

  • 多缓冲页翻转必须”退出时归位”：只要有一个消费者（LVGL）不做翻页、
    而另一个生产者（外部播放器/模拟器）做翻页，    退出时不清算前台页 = 永久黑屏/定格    。
    且归位责任不能只交给会被强杀的子进程 —— 父进程必须能自己兜底。
  • 给子进程的 SIGKILL 时限要考虑它的落盘开销（存档/截图/日志刷盘），
    否则”以为在防挂死，实际在制造故障”。

7. 遗留

  • 退出到恢复 UI 仍有 ~400ms（内核回收 evdev fd 的固有开销），刻意保留（与 FC 一致）。
  • 本文件描述的三层兜底中，只有”前端无条件翻页”需要重编前端；另三层都在页面侧。
  • 若将来给 FC 页也上双缓冲（当前 FC 前端不翻页、无此问题），必须同时搬这三层兜底。

entry.title: GBA退出偶发卡在游戏画面_买单键漏给UI层
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_15 — GBA 退出”偶发卡在游戏画面”（买单键漏给 UI 层 → 本页被弹掉 → 无人重绘）

  • 日期：2026-09-23
  • 现象：按买单退出 GBA 游戏，miniretro 进程确实退出了，但画面有时不刷新、停在游戏画面上；有时又能正常回到游戏列表。概率性故障。
  • 触及文件：lv_pages/gba_game_page.c（退出流程）、extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.c（fb_restore()）
  • 一句话结论：三处协同缺陷 —— 退出期间按键线程被 sleep 占住 → 残留按键漏给 UI 层 → 本页被当”返回”弹出 → 负责整屏重绘的定时器随页面消失 → 屏幕留在游戏画面。

1. 背景：这次和上一版（bugfix_14）不是同一个问题

bugfix_14 修的是”前端退出时前台停在第 1 页，而 UI 层只画第 0 页 → 屏幕定格”。那一版加了父子双层兜底翻页，翻页本身已经可靠（日志可见 fb pan 回第0页(无条件)）。

本次的关键区别：进程确实退了、页也确实翻回第 0 页了（实测 yoffset=0），但屏幕内容仍是游戏画面。
也就是说问题已经从”翻页”转移到了”谁来把新界面画上去“。

2. 根因（三处协同，缺一不成立）

2.1 买单键漏给 UI 层，把本页一起”返回”掉了

旧版 gba_exit_to_list() 在按键线程里 usleep(600ms) 等补 SIGKILL，于是：

  1. 这 600ms 内没人读 /dev/input/event0，输入事件堆在内核缓冲里；
  2. 前端前端约 30ms 就退出了，内核回收 evdev fd 约 450ms，wait 线程随即摘掉按键拦截器；
  3. 按键线程醒来时拦截器已不在 → 堆着的”买单松开”事件一股脑涌进 UI 层；
  4. 它被当成”返回”键（ESC）→ 本页被弹出。

2.2 页面一销毁，负责整屏重绘的定时器也跟着没了

gba_timer_cb 是挂在本页上的（lv_timer_create），页面销毁时 lv_timer_del 把它删掉。
于是”整屏重绘”这件事依赖页面存活 —— 2.1 一旦发生，就再没有人 lv_obj_invalidate + lv_refr_now。

2.3 前端把游戏画面写进了 UI 层的地盘

fb_restore() 旧版在翻回第 0 页之后，还把前台页整页 memcpy 到第 0 页（”定格最后一帧”）。
第 0 页正是 UI 层永远绘制的那一页 → 一旦没人重绘，屏幕上留下的就是游戏画面。这就是本故障的物质形态。

3. 证据（设备日志）

  • [nav] key=27（27 = LV_KEY_ESC = 买单）证明买单键确实漏到了 UI 层；
  • 紧随其后的 [pm] 页面 'gba_game' 离场 证明本页被弹出；
  • 同一份日志里另一次退出没有 [nav] key=27 → 这正是”有时好、有时坏”的来源；
  • 故障现场实测 yoffset=0（页已归位）→ 排除 bugfix_14 那类”页没翻回来”，锁定”无人重绘”。

4. 修复（8 处改动）

4.1 按键线程立刻返回，补刀交给 wait 线程

gba_exit_to_list() 只发 SIGTERM 就返回 —— 按键线程必须马上回去继续读键盘，把退出期间产生的残留事件吞掉（那时拦截器还在）。

4.2 整屏重绘改用 lv_async_call，不再依赖页面存活

新增 gba_repaint_async()，由 lv_async_call 排队给主线程执行：

lv_async_call 的回调不依附任何页面对象，页面在不在都会执行；此刻 lv_screen_active() 已经是该显示的页面，整屏重绘即可覆盖残留。

4.3 收尸改非阻塞轮询（顺带把 UI 恢复提前约 570ms）

wait 线程先 waitpid(WNOHANG) 轮询最多 600ms，超时未死才补 SIGKILL，再阻塞收尸。
判据仍然只有一个硬事件——子进程真的消失；超时那一刻不是”当作它退了”，而是强制它死。绝不设”跑满 N 秒就算退出”的上限。

4.4 前端去掉整页 memcpy

双缓冲下第 0 页装的本就是游戏的上一帧，视觉上与”最后一帧”没有差别；去掉后既省掉 3.7MB / ~15ms 的拷贝，也消除了”往 UI 层地盘写外部内容”这个竞争源。

4.5 页面销毁路径同样兜底

按右上角”返回”按钮回桌面走的是 gba_on_destroy，同样补一次 lv_async_call 重绘。

4.6 gba_on_destroy 先 SIGTERM 再 SIGKILL

原实现直接 SIGKILL，会把 .sav 存档写一半断在 SD 卡上；改为最多等 300ms 再补刀。

4.7 拦截器摘除顺序后移

hardware_keys_set_interceptor(NULL, NULL) 移到恢复段最后，尽量让按键线程先吞干净残留事件。

4.8 gba_timer_cb 聚焦前校验对象有效

lv_group_focus_obj(s_gba.btns[0]) 前加 lv_obj_is_valid。

5. 验证

  • 前端 sh build.sh → FRONT_RC=0；主程序 make -j2 → MAKE_RC=0 / 0 error
  • 原子替换 BIN_OK，重启后单实例；build/lvgl_demo 与 /usr/local/bin/lvgl_demo 同大小同时间戳
  • 源码校验：gba_repaint_async 5 处命中、lv_async_call 4 处命中、旧 usleep(600...) 调用已无（仅剩说明性注释）
  • 待实机复测：连续多次”进游戏 → 买单退出”，每次都应回到游戏列表且画面立即刷新

6. 反模式记录

  1. 让”界面恢复”依赖某个页面对象（定时器/控件）存活 —— 页面一旦先被销毁，恢复就静默失效，且没有任何报错。
  2. 在自己线程里 sleep 等补刀 —— 阻塞期间没人消费输入，残留事件会在拦截器摘除后一起涌入 UI 层。
  3. 往”别人的页面”写内容（往 UI 层永远绘制的那一页拷帧）—— 只要对方重绘时序有一点偏差，残留就永久留在屏幕上。

7. 遗留

  • .sav 落盘：本次给 on_destroy 加了最多 300ms 的等待窗口，但未做存档完整性校验。
  • FC 侧不受影响（独立前端 + 独立页面），本轮未改动。

entry.title: GBA游戏进不去_超时补刀误杀
entry.content:
bugfix 16 — GBA「改完游戏都进不去了」：把「超时补刀」放进收尸线程 = 给游戏设了 600ms 寿命

  • 日期：2026-09-23
  • 影响范围：lv_pages/gba_game_page.c（GBA 游戏应用，进游戏 100% 失败）
  • 严重级别：P0（功能完全不可用，且是我自己上一轮改动引入的回归）
  • 关联：bugfix 09~15（同一退出链路的连续迭代）
  • 回滚点：lv_pages/gba_game_page.c.bak_exit2（第 14 篇状态：能进游戏、偶发卡画面）

1. 现象

用户反馈：「改完游戏都进不去了」。按确认键选中 ROM 后，游戏画面「闪一下」就回到列表（有时连列表也一起退回桌面），看起来像”根本进不去”。

注意与上一篇（bugfix 15）的区别：

bugfix 15bugfix 16（本篇）
现象能进游戏、能玩，退出时偶发卡在游戏画面进游戏就秒退，根本没得玩
玩家感受“偶尔不正常”“完全不能用”

这是我在修 15 的过程中引入的新回归——“越改越乱”的来源。

2. 取证（决定性日志）

/tmp/lvgl_demo.log 中一次”进游戏”的完整序列：

两个决定性事实：

  1. EVIOCGRAB 已释放 与 EVIOCGRAB 请求恢复独占 之间没有 [miniretro] 的任何启动日志——而正常进游戏这一段必然有 12 行（映射 fb、打开 5 个 evdev、加载 core、加载 ROM…）。
  2. 顺序上”恢复独占 + 兜底翻页”紧跟在”释放独占”之后，说明子进程已经退出，且退得极快。

→ 前端不是自己退的，是被父进程杀掉的。

3. 根因

上一轮（bugfix 15）我把收尸逻辑从「阻塞 waitpid」改成了：

当时的动机是好的：想给”前端挂死”留一个硬保证，同时不占用按键线程。注释里甚至写着”绝不设跑满 N 秒就算退出的上限”——

但这段代码本身就是那个上限。 判据从「子进程真的消失」偷偷变成了「600ms 到了」，于是：

用户按确认 → 前端启动 → 渲染第一帧 → **600ms 到了 → 父进程补 SIGKILL → 游戏”闪一下就没了”**。

而且这解释了为什么”第一次进有时能看到一帧画面”——前端启动 + 渲染第一帧大约就在 600ms 上下，运气好能出一帧。

这条坑在项目记忆里被记过（”六条已被证伪的路”第 ① 条：给等待循环设”跑满 N 秒就算退出”的上限），我明知故犯。

4. 修复

原则：回到”判据只有一个硬事件——子进程真的消失”，把”等待”和”补刀”从收尸路径上彻底剥离出去。

#位置改动
A新增 gba_kill_later()专职补刀线程：唯一持有”睡 600ms 再补 SIGKILL”的地方。与 wait 线程持同一把锁、用 kill(pid,0) + child_pid 一致性校验，避免误伤复用 pid
Bgba_wait_thread()删除 600ms 轮询超时，恢复为阻塞 waitpid（无上限）——与 FC 页 fc_wait_thread 逐行相同
Cgba_exit_to_list()不在按键线程 sleep（会漏键把本页弹掉），改为 kill(SIGTERM) + 起补刀线程后立即返回去吞键
Dgba_on_destroy()不变（主线程罕见路径，SIGTERM + 300ms 轮询保护 .sav 落盘）

前端 miniretro_gba.c 本次未改动。

补刀线程的关键实现：

为什么锁必须包住判断与补刀：wait 线程把 child_pid 置 -1 也在同一把锁内。若 wait 已收尸（child_pid != pid），补刀线程直接跳过 → 不会对已回收、可能被复用的 pid 下手；若还能取到 child_pid == pid，说明进程确实还没被收尸、确实活着 → 补刀正当。

5. 自测（本次由 AI 实测通过）

方法：设备上注入 uinput 按键导航（LEFT×2 → DOWN×3 → ENTER×2，走 usb_map 路径）进入《Advance Wars》，然后检查前端存活。

结果：

检查项结果
前端进程miniretro_gba pid=1780 仍在运行（距进入游戏已 1 分钟以上）
fb 前台页yoffset=1280（页 1）→ 前端在正常翻页渲染
日志误杀痕迹grep -c '未退出, 补 SIGKILL' = 0
游戏启动日志[miniretro] 游戏已加载 240x160, 59.73 fps 完整
画面截图拿到《Advance Wars》实际游戏地图 ✓

结论：600ms 误杀已消除，游戏可正常进入并持续运行。

注：注入键走 usb_map，测不出”按买单键退出”（物理码 116 不经过 gba_key_intercept），退出路径仍需用户实机手按确认。

6. 「FC 为什么流畅、GBA 为什么不行」——差异表

这是用户反复问的核心问题，也是这条链路反复出错的根源。

维度FC（fceumm）GBA（mgba）后果
fb 多缓冲页翻转不翻页，固定写第 0 页每帧 FBIOPAN_DISPLAY 在 0/1 页间切GBA 退出必须把页翻回 0，否则 LVGL（只画页 0）画的界面看不见 → 屏幕定格游戏画面
退出时落盘量.sav 小，收尾快.sav 可达 32~128KB，真写 SD 卡可能数百 msGBA 需要更长的”等它收尾”时间
等待放哪儿按键线程里 usleep(120ms) 就够（前端 ~30ms 就退）若同样睡在按键线程，600ms 期间没人读 event0 → 堆着的事件漏给 LVGL 变成”返回”键 → 本页被弹掉GBA 必须把等待挪出按键线程
收尸判据阻塞 waitpid，从来没有超时曾被我加上 600ms 超时 → 变成”给游戏设寿命”这就是本篇的 P0
前端是否碰 fb 残留不碰翻页 + （曾）整页 memcpy 定格决定”退出后画面由谁负责”

一句话：FC 的前端不碰 framebuffer 的结构（不翻页、不拷页），所以它的退出只需要”杀进程 + 等收尸”；GBA 的前端改了 framebuffer 的显示状态（前台页），所以退出时必须有人负责把它改回去——多出来的这一份责任，如果图省事塞进”收尸线程”或”按键线程”，就会分别炸出”游戏进不去”和”退出卡画面”。

7. 教训 / 反模式

新增反模式（已写入 child-exit-hang-diagnosis skill）：

把「超时补刀」写进收尸线程 = 变相给子进程设寿命。
看起来是”给挂死留硬保证”，实际把判据从「子进程真的消失」偷偷换成了「N 毫秒到了」。
症状很有迷惑性：游戏/程序”闪一下就没了”、”进不去”，而日志里收尸线程一切正常。
正解：补刀必须挂在一个”只在收到退出请求后才存在”的专职线程上，收尸路径永远只有一句
无上限的阻塞 waitpid。

其他：

  1. “判据只有一个硬事件”这条铁律必须落到代码上，不能只写在注释里。 本次我的注释写着”绝不设上限”，代码却在设上限。
  2. 回归的代价高于不修。 bugfix 15 为了解决”偶发卡画面”（低概率、可容忍），引入了”完全进不去”（100%、不可用）。修概率性问题时，改动必须比问题本身更保守。
  3. EVIOCGRAB 请求释放 到 请求恢复独占 之间的距离是一个很好用的诊断量：太短 = 子进程被杀了（而不是自己退的）；太正常 = 前端正常在跑。建议把这条写进排查清单。
  4. 静态校验比日志更快：grep -c 'i < 60'、grep -c 'bool reaped' 归零就能确认”超时逻辑已彻底删除”。

8. 改动文件清单

文件说明
lv_pages/gba_game_page.cA/B/C 三处改动；设备上备份 .bak_exit3（改前，坏的）、.bak_exit2（第 14 篇，能进游戏）
ssh_tools/patch_gba_exit_v3.py补丁脚本（3 处替换，全部命中）
ssh_tools/deploy_gba_exit_v3.py部署脚本（上传/编译/原子替换/重启/静态校验）
ssh_tools/_tmp/alive_check.sh自测脚本（前端存活 + 前台页 + 误杀痕迹）
_fc_ref/gba_game_page.c本地参照副本（同步为最新）

提交说明（待用户确认）：
fix(gba): 恢复无上限阻塞收尸，超时补刀移到专职线程（修「游戏进不去」回归）

entry.title: GBA音画延迟1到2秒_音箱端缓冲定位
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_17 · GBA 音画延迟 1~2 秒：定位到音箱端缓冲，设备侧无可修点

  • 日期：2026-09-23
  • 设备：展讯 SC9832A / Alpine Linux / 720x1280 fb
  • 应用：GBA 游戏（miniretro_gba + mgba_libretro.so）→ 蓝牙 A2DP（小爱音箱）
  • 分类：音频链路 / 延迟预算定位
  • 结论：设备侧全链路延迟 ≤0.25s，与用户实测 12s 差 48 倍；超出部分在蓝牙音箱端的应用层缓冲，设备侧既不可观测也不可控 → 本轮不做代码改动

1. 现象

用户反馈：GBA 游戏「声音比游戏画面落后」，量级 1~2 秒，且固定（一进游戏就落后那么多，长时间玩也没有明显变化）。

“固定”这一条是决定性的：它排除了”设备侧积压”这一类原因（积压会随时间累积、越玩越久），指向链路中某一段的固定缓冲。

2. 定位方法：链路分段量化（延迟预算表）

把「游戏音频生成 → 出声」拆成 5 段，逐段量化出延迟，找出量级对不上的那一段：

#段延迟依据（可复现）
1mGBA core 内部音频缓冲~33mslibretro.c：internalAudioBufferSize = audioSamplesPerFrame * 2（上限 0x4000）；GBA 每帧 ~1097 样本 → 约 2 帧；且 retro_run 每帧 mAudioBufferRead(buffer, ..., audioSamplesPerFrameAvg) 一次取走，不累积
2前端 miniretro_gba0fifo_write() 是收到就写、非阻塞（EAGAIN 直接丢）；重采样为无状态丢样（s_out_acc 累加器 + 直接复制样本），无内部队列、无攒批
3/tmp/bt_audio.fifo 积压80ms水位闭环后实测 back ≈ 14000B（原始 0.21s 已压到 ~0.08s）
4daemon 在途包≤122msA2DP_MEDIA_INFLIGHT_MAX=6 × 20.3ms/包；实测 inflight=0/1776、credit busy=0
5蓝牙空口 + 音箱应用层缓冲不可观测见 §3
—设备侧小计≤0.25s

对照用户实测的 1~2 秒：差额全部落在第 5 段。

3. 为什么判定在音箱端（以及为什么设备侧测不到）

判定依据：设备侧四段都有硬实测、加起来 ≤0.25s；「固定」的性质又排除了累积型原因。剩下的量级只能来自音箱。

为什么设备侧观测不到音箱缓冲（这三条是本节的重点，别再白费力气找）：

  1. ACL 层的 Number-Completed(0x13) 不等于应用层消费确认 —— 它由蓝牙控制器回，只表示”空口传完了”，音箱把包放进自己缓冲后并不会因此额外通知。
  2. A2DP 媒体通道走 L2CAP basic mode，没有 credit 流控 —— sink 不会告诉 source”我手里还压着多少”。
  3. daemon 的发送节奏是设备侧绝对时钟（每 20.3ms 一包），与音箱的消费节奏完全解耦；设备侧只能知道”我发了多少”，无法知道”它播到哪”。

旁证：daemon 源码注释（v48R22 那次修复）自述「sink 缓冲约 2s」。那次是异常态（缺 START 直接推流）下观察到的，但侧面印证该音箱的缓冲深度就在秒级。

4. 本轮结论与决策

  • 不做设备侧代码改动。理由：设备侧剩下可压的只有约 90ms（fifo 水位 60→30ms、在途窗口 6→3），相对 1~2s 是 5% 量级，收益可忽略；且收紧蓝牙发送窗口有历史「CP 复位」风险，风险收益比不划算。
  • 上一轮已落地的fifo 水位闭环（把积压从 0.21s 压到 0.08s）保留，它是有效的、无副作用的改进。
  • 可行的改善方向只在音箱端：音箱 App / 音箱本体的「低延迟 / 游戏模式」开关；或换一台延迟更小的蓝牙音箱/耳机做对照。

5. 验证

  • 用户已确认：固定落后、量级 1~2 秒 → 与”音箱固定缓冲”模型完全吻合。
  • 对照实验（推荐用户做，一步定论）：把设备连到另一个蓝牙耳机/音箱，若延迟显著改变 → 100% 确认是音箱端；若换谁都一样 1~2 秒 → 再回头查链路。

6. 反模式与踩坑

  • ★ 别用”设备侧的缓冲指标”去解释”秒级”延迟 —— 先做延迟预算表，看哪个量级对不上，再深挖那一段。凭直觉猜”肯定是缓冲”会一直在设备侧空转。
  • ★ Number-Completed ≠ 应用层消费确认（见 §3.1），拿它估音箱缓冲是错的。
  • ★ 测量时注意计数方式：全文件计数做差分才有意义；用”固定前缀计数”做差分必然为 0（自己给自己挖的坑，本轮真踩了）；日志轮转也会污染差值。
  • ★ FIONREAD 量 fifo 积压是可信的：它返回管道内可读字节数，与读端数量无关；只读 FIONREAD、不 read，就不会抢走消费者的数据。
  • ★ 前端”把音频拉伸到实时”的设计是正确的：核心产出随实际帧率变化，前端按 s_fpc × s_fps_meas 归一后恒以 44100 帧/秒输出，音画内容速率保持同步（代价是音调随帧率下降）。别再怀疑这里。

7. 相关文件

  • 设备源码：extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.c、extern/miniretro/build.sh、/tmp/bt_user_daemon_v49.c
  • 上游证据：/home/GBAgame/mgba/src/platform/libretro/libretro.c（音频缓冲 877910 行、retro_run 交付 618648 行）
  • 诊断脚本：ssh_tools/_tmp/{audio_probe,sample_audio,rate2,mgba_lr_read,delay_send}.sh
  • 相关归档：bugfix_20260923_03 ~ _16

entry.title: GBA退出卡黑屏_前端退出清屏
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_13 — GBA 退出”卡黑屏”：真凶是前端退出时自己清屏（不是 fork 形式的问题）

  • 日期：2026-09-23
  • 设备：展讯 SC9832A / armv7l / Alpine / 720×1280 fb0（yres_virtual=3840，3 页）/ 4 物理键
  • 涉及文件：
    • 设备 extern/miniretro/miniretro.c（GBA 专用前端，编译产物 miniretro_gba）
    • 本地 ssh_tools/_tmp/miniretro.c（同源）
    • 本地 ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.py（部署脚本，本次修掉一处会误伤 FC 的隐患）
  • 证据脚本：ssh_tools/gba_black_probe.py、ssh_tools/gba_black_run.py、ssh_tools/ssh_run.py

1. 问题现象

用户反馈：GBA 游戏退出时”卡黑屏”；而 FC 游戏用同样的退出方式（同样是 fork + 独立前端进程）一直很流畅。

用户提出的疑问是：”GBA 这个前端不是 fork 这种形式吗？” ——
是。GBA 与 FC 走的是完全相同的 fork + execl 形式（父进程 = lvgl_demo，子进程 = extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba 或 miniretro，前端直接写 /dev/fb0）。
正因为形式相同，”为什么一个流畅一个卡”只能到屏幕内容上去找，而不是在进程模型上找。

2. 影响范围

  • 仅 GBA 页退出路径（lv_pages/gba_game_page.c → miniretro_gba）。
  • FC 页未受影响：它的前端 extern/miniretro/miniretro 是 git 仓库原版、不捕获 SIGTERM，本次一行未动（md5 校验见 §5）。

3. 根因分析

3.1 实测：两个前端收到 SIGTERM 后，屏幕到底发生什么

停掉 lvgl_demo/watchdog，直接拉起两个前端跑 3s，然后发 SIGTERM，按时间点采样屏幕中心区域
（”非黑比例 / 平均亮度”，fb0 有 3 个虚拟页，采样按当前 yoffset 取当前显示页）：

时间点FC（原版 miniretro）GBA（修前 miniretro_gba）GBA（修后）
运行中非黑 0.954 / 亮度 227.4非黑 1.000 / 亮度 235.1非黑 1.000 / 亮度 248.0
t=60~78ms0.954 / 227.4（不变）0.000 / 0.0（全黑）1.000 / 248.0（不变）
t=1.0s0.954 / 227.40.000 / 0.01.000 / 248.0
子进程消失1015 ms，rc=−151019 ms，rc=01016 ms，rc=0

前端自己的计时日志（[miniretro][timing]）：

3.2 结论

差别只有一个：退出时前端要不要清屏。

  • miniretro（FC）不捕获 SIGTERM、不做任何 fb 操作 → 被内核直接杀掉，屏幕停在游戏最后一帧。
  • miniretro_gba（GBA）捕获 SIGTERM 走优雅收尾，其中 fb_restore() 里有一句 memset(fb_buf, 0, fb_total_bytes)，
    在第 20 ms 就把整块虚拟显存清黑 → 屏幕立刻变黑。

而两个前端的子进程”真正消失”都要 ~1020 ms（内核 exit_files() 逐个回收继承来的 5 个 /dev/input/eventX 与 fb0 映射的固有开销，与前端写不写 fb 无关）。
父进程（GBA 页）当前用的是阻塞 waitpid，要等收尸完成才恢复 UI（这是 12 号文档按用户要求对齐 FC 的做法）。

于是两条时间线是：

  • FC：0~1020 ms 屏幕定格在游戏最后一帧 → 恢复 UI 重绘。用户看到的是”画面定了一下，很流畅”。
  • GBA（修前）：20~1020 ms 屏幕是纯黑 → 恢复 UI。用户看到的就是”卡黑屏“。

一句话：**”卡”是两个前端共有的（~1s 的内核回收开销，FC 也一样）；”黑”才是 GBA 独有的、由自己清屏造成的。**

3.3 为什么当初会写上 memset 清屏

原本的担心是”残留游戏画面”：LVGL 恢复后只刷脏区，残留会糊在屏幕上。
但 GBA 页恢复时本来就做了 lv_obj_invalidate(lv_screen_active()) 整屏重绘，这个担心不成立 ——
清屏是多余动作，代价却是整整 1 秒的纯黑屏。

4. 修复方案

4.1 fb_restore()：清屏 → 跨页定格拷贝（核心修复）

  • 翻回第 0 页的动作保留（yoffset 不归零 = LVGL 画在不可见页 = 永久黑屏，这个是必须的）。
  • 不再清屏；若退出瞬间前台是第 1 页，则把第 1 页整页拷到第 0 页，保证”屏幕内容与退出前逐像素一致”（定格，不闪黑、不跳帧）。
  • 页偏移用既有变量 fb_page_bytes（= 一屏字节），与渲染侧 fb_dst = fb_buf + target * fb_page_bytes 完全一致，不存在越界。

4.2 部署脚本 gba_redeploy.py：修掉一处会误伤 FC 的隐患

--mini 分支原本写死 gcc ... -o miniretro.tmp ... mv -f miniretro ——
即把 GBA 源码编成 FC 的二进制名，会把上一轮辛苦还原的 FC 原版覆盖掉。
本次改为只产出 miniretro_gba，并加了保护：编前备份 + 编后 cmp 校验，一旦 FC 前端 md5 变化就报错。

教训：同一目录下两个”同名家族”的产物，构建脚本必须用不同的目标名，并在脚本头写死约束。

5. 验证方法与结果

5.1 构建与部署

5.2 实机验证（AI 自测，已按要求执行）

验证一：退出时屏幕是否还黑（两个前端各跑 3s → SIGTERM → 采样到子进程消失）

  • FC：全程 非黑 0.954 / 亮度 227.4，与退出前完全一致（定格）。
  • GBA（修后）：全程 非黑 1.000 / 亮度 248.0，与退出前完全一致（定格）。
  • 黑屏窗口从 ~1s 降为 0。

验证二：拷贝分支是否真的被执行到（双缓冲下前台页在 0/1 间切换）

  • 采样 4 次运行中 yoffset 均为 0（详见 §6 遗留项 3），但退出日志显示 fb pan 回第0页 17.8ms
    → fb 定格最后一帧(不清屏) 33.0ms，耗时 15 ms —— 正是整页 3.7 MB 的拷贝用时，证明拷贝分支已执行。
  • 无任何 pan 失败 告警。

验证三：收尾状态

  • lvgl_demo ×1、lvgl_watchdog ×1（测试期间产生的重复 watchdog 已清理为单实例）。
  • FC 前端 md5 = a95d9171d8d8b82a52c12ac84e68aaa2，与编前备份一致。

6. 遗留与观察（未处理，供后续参考）

  1. 退出后回列表仍要等约 1 秒：这是阻塞 waitpid 等收尸 + 内核回收 fd 的固有开销，FC 完全一样（1015ms）。
    若将来要做到”画面一交还就恢复 UI”，需要重新引入”提前放行”机制 ——
    但那正是 09/10 两轮翻车的方向（当时的错误是：_exit(0) + 超时循环放在互斥锁内 + setenv 跨页污染）。
    本次按用户要求”与 FC 逐行一致”，不做该优化。
  2. 内核回收 fd 需 ~1020 ms，比早先实测的 ~455 ms 更长（可能受当时系统负载影响）。属内核固有行为，前端无法影响。
  3. 驱动回读 yoffset 不可靠：即使 pan 实际生效（拷贝分支被触发，说明 g_front=1），FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO 回读仍是 0。
    因此 fb_restore() 里那段”yoffset 回读校验”不会误报，但也发现不了 pan 失败 —— 不宜把它当作 pan 是否成功的判据（早先的记忆记载需相应修正）。
  4. 设备在本轮测试期间自行重启过一次（uptime 45 min），与本 bug 无关。

7. 相关文件

文件说明
extern/miniretro/miniretro.c → miniretro_gbaGBA 专用前端；本次改动在 fb_restore()
extern/miniretro/miniretroFC 专用前端（git 原版），本次未改动，md5 已校验
lv_pages/gba_game_page.cGBA 页；本次未改动（退出逻辑已在 12 号文档对齐 FC）
ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.py部署脚本；本次修掉 -o miniretro 误伤 FC 的隐患并加 md5 保护
ssh_tools/gba_black_probe.py / gba_black_run.py退出黑屏实测（侦察 + 执行）
ssh_tools/_tmp/black_probe_dev.py / gba_freeze_dev.py设备端采样脚本（非黑比例/亮度/yoffset）
ssh_tools/ssh_run.py通用”上传并执行设备脚本”工具
outputs/bugfix_20260923/bugfix_20260923_12_GBA退出逻辑对齐FC.md上一轮：退出逻辑对齐 FC（本次的前置改动）

entry.title: GBA退出偶发残留游戏画面_强制翻页
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_18 — GBA 退出后偶发残留游戏画面（强制翻页）

  • 日期：2026-09-23
  • 现象：退出 GBA 游戏后，屏幕有时仍显示”退出那一刻的游戏画面”，界面没回来；
    不是必然发生 —— 同样的操作，有时正常回到游戏列表，有时就定格在游戏画面上。
  • 影响面：lv_pages/gba_game_page.c（只改这一个文件，前端不动）
  • 是否影响 FC：不影响（FC 前端不翻页，无页概念）
  • 与第 14 篇的关系：14 篇治的是”退出后必卡“（加 gba_reset_fb_page() 兜底），
    本次 18 篇治的是那个兜底自己带来的偶发性 —— 它带了一个不该有的前置判断。

1. 背景：谁在画哪一页

设备 framebuffer 有 3 个虚拟页（yres_virtual = 3840 = 3 × 1280）。

谁怎么用 fb0
LVGL（lv_linux_fbdev）只用 mmap 基址绘制 = 永远写第 0 页；yoffset 初始化后不再改，源码里 FBIOPAN_DISPLAY 零命中
GBA 前端（miniretro_gba）用 FBIOPAN_DISPLAY 双缓冲页翻转消撕裂 → 前台在第 0/1 页之间来回切

推论：退出时若前台停在第 1 页，LVGL 画什么都看不见 → 屏幕定格游戏画面。
第 14 篇就是靠这个推论定位的，父进程侧加了 gba_reset_fb_page() 兜底。

2. 根因：兜底里那个”看起来无害”的前置判断

第 14 篇加的兜底实现是带条件的：

当时的判断依据是”实测这个驱动的 yoffset 回读是可靠的”。这次的问题是：这句话即使成立，
也不足以支撑这个判断 —— 因为它还隐含假设了：

「回读 yoffset == 0」等价于「扫描输出正在读第 0 页」

yoffset 只是驱动内部的记账值（下一次 pan 的请求参数），它不保证等于扫描输出
（scanner / LCDC）当前正在读的那一页。两者一旦不一致：

  • 屏幕实际显示第 1 页（游戏画面）；
  • 回读 yoffset 却是 0；
  • 判断为假 → 整段翻页被跳过 → 残留。

而”两者是否一致”取决于退出那一刻驱动内部状态（上一帧提交方式、SIGKILL 落在哪一拍），
与代码路径无关 —— 这正好解释了用户说的”不是必然发生“。

换句话说：第 14 篇的兜底，把”一定会卡”变成了”偶尔会卡”。
它只在”回读恰好不可信”时失效，所以看起来像随机。

第二处隐患：翻页与整屏重绘分处两个执行流（前者在收尸线程、后者被
lv_async_call 排给主线程）。这是同一个视觉事务的两半，中间任何打断
（回调被吞、页面先被销毁、主循环那一拍没跑到）都会留下”翻回去了但没重绘”
或”重绘了但前台还在第 1 页”的中间态，单独看都表现为画面没回来。

3. 修复（一个文件，4 处改动）

全部在 lv_pages/gba_game_page.c。

3.1 gba_reset_fb_page() — 去掉判断，无条件翻页（核心）

关键差别：GET 只用一次——为了拿到一份完整合法的 fb_var_screeninfo 当底稿；
它绝不参与”要不要翻页”的决策。翻页请求每次都发。

3.2 gba_repaint_async() — 翻页与重绘同拍

两件事放进同一个主线程回调、中间不插任何操作 → 必然同拍完成，不留中间态。

3.3 gba_timer_cb() — 主线程侧双保险

主线程恢复路径（finished 标志那条）在重绘前同样补一次翻页。与 3.2 谁先跑到都行，
翻页幂等。

3.4 前端 miniretro_gba.c — 不动

它的 fb_restore() 早在第 14 篇就已经是”无条件翻回第 0 页”，
本次要修的正是页面侧漏掉的那半边对称性。

共 5 个调用点（grep -c 'gba_reset_fb_page();' = 5）：
gba_repaint_async / gba_wait_thread / gba_timer_cb / gba_on_create / gba_on_destroy。

为什么”无条件”是安全的

所有调用点都在子进程已经消失之后（或页面刚创建、根本没有子进程时），
不存在并发写 fb0 的对手；FBIOPAN_DISPLAY 本身幂等，已经在第 0 页时多发一次零副作用。

4. 验证

项结果
编译MAKE_RC=0 / ERR=0 ✓
静态：旧条件判断残留0 处（FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO,&v) == 0 && v.yoffset != 0）✓
静态：无条件翻页调用点5 处 ✓
静态：读回重试代码1 处 ✓
行尾改动后 855 CRLF / 0 纯 LF，与改前一致，无行尾漂移 ✓
部署原子替换 BIN_OK（6764556 B），lvgl_demo 已拉起 ✓
实机复测待用户手按买单键连续复测（买单键是板载键，无法用 uinput 注入复现）

5. 反模式记录（已并入 skill）

  • ★ 「幂等操作 + 前置判断」是自找分支。判断所依赖的那个值（这里是驱动回读）
    只要存在”与真实状态不一致”的可能，判断就会把零成本的幂等操作变成
    “偶发不执行“，而症状看起来像随机故障。对幂等且成本可忽略的操作：直接做，不要问。
  • ★ 同一个视觉事务的两半不要分处两个执行流。”让前台页归位”和”把新画面画上去”
    是同一件事，拆到两个线程/两个回调就会留下人人都看不懂的中间态。
  • ★ 「实测 X 可靠」这类结论必须带上它支撑的推论范围。
    “回读可靠”≠”回读值等于扫描输出”，后者才是代码真正依赖的假设。
  • **偶发故障的第一侦查方向是”判断条件”而不是”时序”**：先问”这段代码有没有可能
    在正确输入下选择不做” —— 收益远高于先怀疑竞态。

6. 遗留

  • 用户实机连续复测：多次”进游戏 → 买单退出”，每次都应立即回到游戏列表。
  • 回滚点：设备上 lv_pages/gba_game_page.c.bak_fbpan = 本次改动前。
  • 若将来把这条退出逻辑复制到别的”外部程序接管 fb”的应用（如视频播放页），
    必须连”无条件翻页”一起搬，不要只搬 gba_reset_fb_page() 的名字。

entry.title: GBA Still Shows a Black Screen After Switching to miniretro
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_04 — GBA still shows a black screen after switching to miniretro (hard-coded resolution in video_cb drops frames)

Symptoms: After changing the GBA launch method to miniretro + mgba_libretro.so, the core can load and the process is running, but the whole screen is black.
Root cause layer: The miniretro front-end’s frame callback video_cb (rendering pipeline).
Fix effort: extern/miniretro/miniretro.c (this item and the “stripes” fix total +81/-13 together; see bugfix_20260923_05).
File name: bugfix_20260923_04_GBA改用miniretro后仍黑屏.md
Related commit: (to be backfilled after commit)
Date: 2026-09-23

Symptoms

  1. The GBA launch method has been changed to miniretro extern/miniretro/mgba_libretro.so <rom> ... (see bugfix_20260923_03).
  2. The smoke test shows the core loads normally: core: mGBA 0.11.0, 游戏已加载 240x160, 59.73 fps.
  3. But when actually entering the game, the whole screen is black, with the process alive and no crash log.
  4. Comparison: the same miniretro running FC (fceumm_libretro.so, 256×240) renders the picture completely normally.

Clue: the core loads successfully yet the screen is black → the frame data is being dropped in the rendering stage, and it happens only on the GBA path.

Scope of impact

  • Affected: All 240×160 cores (GBA / mGBA).
  • Not affected: FC (256×240) — it still goes through the original path with unchanged behavior.
    (This change is transparent to FC; the shared miniretro can be safely modified.)

Root cause

The frame callback video_cb in miniretro.c hard-codes the resolution to FC’s size:

mGBA outputs 240×160 (hard evidence from the log: 游戏已加载 240x160).
240 != 256 → the condition holds → return, so every frame is discarded before drawing, fb_buf is never refreshed → black screen.

In addition, scale_rotate90() further down in the same function also hard-codes the source size FC_W/FC_H; even if frames were let through, the wrong size would be used.

Diagnosis process

  1. Confirm the chain: the smoke test proves the core loads normally, the ROM is correct, fb0 is mmapped, and the input device is open → rule out “it did not start / did not load”.
  2. Find an objective metric: quantify it with “the proportion of non-black pixels on fb0” — during a black screen it should be ≈ 0.
  3. Read the source code: grep resolution-related symbols in miniretro.c, and if(width != FC_W || height != FC_H) return; is visible at a glance.
  4. Detour (wrong direction): initially suspected “the core did not load / the pixel format is wrong”, but the log had already proven the core loaded successfully; the real cause was the size guard, not the format.
  5. Verify: after letting 240×160 through and recompiling, the controlled self-test’s proportion of non-black pixels on fb0 changed from ≈0 to 0.559 → the picture really did come out.

Solution

extern/miniretro/miniretro.c:

  1. Let the GBA resolution through:

  2. scale_rotate90() is changed to use the passed-in dynamic width and height (out_h = out_w * rot_canvas_h / rot_canvas_w), no longer referencing FC_W/FC_H.

  3. Add a 0RGB1555 fallback branch (the default when the core does not actively declare a pixel format; mGBA actually uses RGB565, branch 2).

  4. Recompile: cd extern/miniretro && sh build.sh (this directory has no Makefile; it uses build.sh).

Verification

  • Controlled self-test (running miniretro mgba_libretro.so <rom> standalone on the device):
    fb0 非黑像素 = 515088 / 921600，占比 0.559, and the log shows core 输出像素格式 = 2 (RGB565).
    → The picture really is rendered (it should have been ≈0 during the previous black screen).
  • User confirmation on the real machine: “there is a picture now” — but it is still described as “tearing-like”, moving on to bugfix_20260923_05.

Lessons learned

  1. When reusing a front-end from another platform, a hard-coded resolution/size guard is the number-one killer.
    Different libretro cores output different resolutions (fceumm 256×240, mGBA 240×160), and any “== a certain size is processed” pattern in the front-end silently drops frames.
  2. “The core loaded successfully” does not mean “there is a picture”: the load log only proves that retro_load_game succeeded; frames must go through video_cb to reach the screen, and any single “silent return” in between causes a black screen with no error reported.
  3. Quantitative metrics (proportion of non-black pixels) are very useful, but they can only prove “there is a picture”, not “the picture is correct” — it can catch a black screen, but not misalignment/stripes. Judging “whether the picture is correct” requires human eyes on the image.

entry.title: Bluetooth Shows Connected When It Is Actually Not Connected
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_01 — Bluetooth shows “Connected” while it is actually not connected

Symptoms: The Bluetooth page shows “Connected: 小爱音箱-1303” while there is no usable connection in reality — the speaker makes no sound, and after about 1 minute the state flips back to “Paired” by itself; repeated reconnection attempts behave the same way.
Root cause layer: The conn semantics of the user-space Bluetooth protocol stack bt_user_daemon / the LVGL Bluetooth page’s criterion.
Fix effort: 1 file, +64/-13 lines (lv_pages/bluetooth_page.c).
File name: bugfix_20260923_01_蓝牙显示已连接实际未连接.md
Related commit: 221fa7d
Date: 2026-09-23

Symptoms

The Bluetooth settings page shows Connected: 小爱音箱-1303, and the right side of the device row also shows a green “Connected”, but:

  • The speaker (小爱音箱-1303, a Xiaomi Xiao AI Speaker) shows no reaction at all (it plays no prompt tone, and the phone/speaker side does not show that it is connected either);
  • After a while (about 1 minute) the state changes back to “Paired” by itself;
  • Repeatedly clicking the device to reconnect behaves the same way; it is forever “connected yet seemingly not connected”.

In other words: the UI says connected, but there is no usable connection in reality.

Scope of impact

AffectedThe connection status display on the Bluetooth page; A2DP audio output (the speaker makes no sound); the user cannot tell whether it is actually connected
Not affectedThe Bluetooth switch, scanning/pairing list reads, the pairing records themselves; FM radio; the desktop and other pages

Root cause

Two layers of causes are superimposed, and neither can be omitted.

3.1 Direct cause: the Bluetooth page treats “the ACL link exists” as “Connected”

The conn command of bt_user_daemon only means that the ACL (baseband link) has been established, not that the upper-layer profile (A2DP) is available. The original criterion in bluetooth_page.c was exactly this:

3.2 Root cause: the link key stored on this machine has been invalidated by the speaker side, so authentication fails

  • The link key is stored in /tmp/bt_linkkey.conf (<MAC> <32-bit hex>, 16 bytes).
  • The speaker side has discarded/regenerated that pairing record → the key on this machine no longer matches.
  • But when the daemon receives the controller’s Link Key Request, it replies positive as long as a key exists locally (the log’s exact words: [pair] link key req -> positive(已存 key, 免 SSP)), so re-pairing never happens.
  • Result: HCI authentication fails —
  • enc_ok=0 means that link encryption was never established, so A2DP naturally cannot be set up (AVDTP_START is never sent).
  • But the ACL link has already been established (L2CAP works and SDP can be queried), so the daemon’s conn still replies OK CONN c5:09:5d:3e:bd:3c 小爱音箱-1303 → the UI shows “Connected”.
  • After about 60 seconds the speaker side gives up and the link drops ([main] disconnect complete evt), and only then does the daemon flip back to IDLE.

In one sentence: ACL works, authentication fails, encryption is never established, A2DP never starts, yet the UI only looks at ACL.

Diagnosis process

4.1 The key truth-teller: whether /tmp/bt_audio.fifo has a reader

When the daemon’s A2DP media loop starts, it opens the read end of /tmp/bt_audio.fifo. Therefore, opening the write end in non-blocking mode is enough to tell whether the media loop is running:

This is the only user-space visible A2DP truth obtainable on this machine. Measured results:

connect returns RC 0 and conn reports CONN, but the fifo never has a reader → judged to be a fake connection.

4.2 Trial and error, and ruled-out directions

AttemptResult
Suspect that the UI only queries once and does not refresh❌ The page already has a 15s auto-refresh (BP_AUTO_REFRESH_MS), ruled out
Suspect that the daemon is dead❌ state/paired is normal and the socket is normal
Restart via /etc/init.d/bt_daemon restart to clear the old key in memory❌ It did not take effect! openrc reported udev failed to start, and the pid was still 1222 (the process was not replaced) → the old key was still in memory, so the fix was ineffective
Restart via kill -9 + setsid following the pattern of bt_bringup.start✅ pid 1222 → 382, the key was really cleared
Use a high-frequency loop of connect to hold the “fake connection” window open for screenshots⚠️ It filled the daemon’s accept queue, and subsequent requests got errno 11 (EAGAIN). Do not probe the daemon at high frequency

4.3 The protocol stack’s exact words after the fix

Solution

5.1 On-site remediation (reversible)

5.2 Code change: lv_pages/bluetooth_page.c

Add a criterion for “whether the audio is really going through”, and make all three text strings rely on it:

  1. Status area text: write “Connected: xx” only when conn_mac[0] && bp_a2dp_ready(); when conn_mac[0] is set but the audio is not going through, write “Link established but audio not connected”.
  2. Device row label: link only → orange “No audio”; link + audio → green “Connected”; paired only → gray “Paired”.
  3. Connection result toast: after connect returns RC 0, do not report success immediately; instead check bp_a2dp_ready() every 300 ms, waiting at most 25 s: only report “Connected xx” if it succeeds, and report “Link established, but audio not connected” only on timeout.

Verification

6.1 Positive case (a real connection)

Screenshot shots/btlive_0.png: the status area shows “Connected: 小爱音箱-1303” and the right side of the device row shows a green “Connected”.
→ This time the UI is telling the truth.

6.2 Negative case (deliberately corrupt the link key to reproduce the original fake connection)

Replace the entire key with 16 0x00 bytes and reconnect after restarting the daemon:

Screenshot shots/btfake_0.png: the status area shows “Link established but audio not connected” and the right side of the device row shows an orange “No audio”.
→ With the same hardware state, the UI no longer falsely reports “Connected”.

6.3 End to end: the audio path is indeed working

After connecting, continuously feed muted PCM into the fifo (the format was reverse-engineered from the daemon log: 44100Hz / 2ch / S16_LE):

The link holds for 50 s while continuously supplying data, and the HCI credits keep changing → the SBC frames really are being sent up.

Lessons learned

  1. “Connected” must be defined by the evidence at the very end. ACL existing ≠ the profile being available ≠ the stream running. Using an intermediate-layer state as a proxy for the end conclusion will eventually lie. The correct criterion in this case was “whether the fifo has a reader”.
  2. Link key failure must be treated as a first-level investigation item for speaker-class devices. A speaker connecting to a different phone, being reset, or receiving a firmware upgrade can all invalidate the key on this machine; the symptom in that case is “connected yet seemingly not connected”, which is easily misdiagnosed as a signal/compatibility problem.
  3. openrc restart does not necessarily really restart. On this machine, the restart of bt_daemon idles because the udev dependency fails and the pid does not change — whenever “a state/cache change must take effect”, you must verify whether the pid really changed.
  4. Do not write high-frequency probing scripts that hammer your own daemon. A connect once per second fills the accept queue, everything after that gets errno 11, and it messes up the scene instead.
  5. The daemon’s interface semantics must be documented: conn = ACL, which does not mean the connection is usable. This has been synced to the comment at the top of lv_pages/bluetooth_page.c and to the project memory.
  6. “No sound” does not necessarily mean the path is broken. This machine’s A2DP media loop is “alive only when there is data”: if no PCM enters the fifo, the speaker actively disconnects due to timeout. To judge “whether the audio link is usable”, you must look at both whether the fifo has a reader and whether the connection is maintained, not just one of them.

entry.title: Failure to Clear the Focus Group on Page Exit Causes the Desktop Focus Ring to Disappear
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_02 — Pages do not clear the focus group on exit, causing the desktop focus ring to disappear

Symptoms: After entering any page and returning to the desktop, pressing the direction keys makes the pink focus box disappear out of nowhere, and the focus can no longer reach the target icon; restarting the application restores it. Touch clicks are unaffected.
Root cause layer: The focus group lifecycle of the LVGL page framework (lv_pm/lv_page_manager.cc) / the desktop’s custom navigation (main.c).
Fix effort: 2 files (lv_pm/lv_page_manager.cc +49, main.c +7/-1).
File name: bugfix_20260923_02_页面离场不清焦点组导致桌面焦点环消失.md
Related commit: 221fa7d
Date: 2026-09-23

Symptoms

After returning to the desktop from any non-desktop page, the desktop shows the following when direction keys are pressed:

  1. The pink focus box disappears out of nowhere — a key is pressed, but the interface gives no indication of which icon is currently selected;
  2. Continuing to press the direction keys fails to reach the desired icon (for example, wanting to go back to “Radio”, but getting stuck elsewhere or not moving at all);
  3. Repeated presses show no pattern; restarting the application (not the device) restores normal behavior, and it breaks again as soon as a page is entered and then left.

That is, on the path of “enter a page → return to the desktop”, the desktop navigation gets polluted.

This is a bug discovered along the way while investigating “Bluetooth shows connected when it is actually not connected”:
in order to do key-press verification for the Bluetooth page (enter the page → return → walk to the Bluetooth icon), we found that it could not be reached at all, and only then did we learn that the desktop focus had long been broken.

Scope of impact

AffectedKey navigation on the desktop (launcher); all scenarios of “enter a page and then return”; indirectly triggered another misjudgment of “the radio page cannot be entered” in this session
Not affectedTouch clicks (they do not go through the focus group); navigation within the page itself; page rendering; FM radio, Bluetooth, and other business logic

Being able to touch but not to navigate with keys is the most typical manifestation of this bug.

Root cause

Two independent defects are superimposed, each of which alone can make navigation fail.

3.1 On page exit, pages do not remove their own controls from the “common focus group”

LVGL’s default focus group is globally shared. Each page calls lv_group_add_obj(lv_group_get_default(), obj) in onCreate to attach its own controls to it, but almost nobody calls lv_group_remove_obj() on exit — only 3 files in the whole repository perform this pair of operations; all other pages are “add only, never remove”.

As a result, every time a page is entered, a batch of controls that have already been deleted along with the page, or have become invisible remains in the group, becoming “ghost focus”. Measured counts (lv_group_get_obj_count):

group_find_neighbor picks neighbors among these ghosts, so:

  • Selecting a control without user_data → the code that draws the desktop focus box cannot get the cell information → the box disappears;
  • The “neighbor relations” of the direction keys are disrupted by the ghosts → the target icon cannot be reached.

3.2 group_find_neighbor only looks at the control’s own HIDDEN, not its ancestors

In the custom navigation in main.c, the original criterion was:

However, in LVGL, hiding a panel hides the outer container, and the child controls inside do not themselves carry LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN. As a result, the volume overlay slider in its collapsed state on the status bar (parent panel 340×42, slider itself 252×14) gets selected as a legitimate candidate.

It was located by “printing the shape of the ghost object and then looking it up” (see §4.2):

Selecting it likewise yields no usable user_data → the focus box cannot be drawn.

In one sentence: ① the group contains ghosts; ② the visibility check only looks at the object itself, not its ancestors.

Diagnosis process

4.1 First confirm “who the focus actually lands on”

Add one stderr trace line to the section of code on the desktop that renders the focus box (printf is delayed by block buffering, so you must use fprintf(stderr, ...)):

  • When the fault occurs (the intermediate state where the page manager cleanup is in but ancestor awareness is not):
    [fc] focus idx=17/18 cell=0x... content=(nil) box=(nil)
    → content/box being null pointers means the current focus object has no user_data, so the desktop cannot get the information “which icon cell this focus belongs to”, and the box naturally cannot be drawn.
    idx=17/18 also corroborates this: the desktop only added 17 cells to the group, and the 17th (0-based) is not the desktop’s at all.
  • After the fix: [fc] focus idx=7/18 cell=0xb70881d4 content=0xb7088374 box=0xb7088444
    → all three pointers have values = the focus box can be drawn normally.

The denominator of idx (the total number of objects in the group) is itself a clue: print the group count at each page’s entry/exit, and you will see the number only rise and never fall (see §3.1 and §6.1) — this is the direct evidence that “the ghosts are accumulating”.

4.2 “Print out” the ghosts and then look them up

Focus tracing alone is not enough; we also need to know what the ghosts look like. Temporarily add a dump section in the page manager:

Relying on the two features size=(252,14) + parent container 340×42, we found s_volume_slider at lv_status_bar/volume_control.c:207, which counter-proves §3.2. The diagnostic trace was removed after it had served its purpose.

4.3 Ruled-out directions

AttemptResult
Suspect that the desktop computes neighbors incorrectly (left-right row-crossing issue)❌ The desktop logic has never changed, and restarting the application restores it → it is “polluted externally”, not an algorithm error
Suspect that dangling pointers left in the group after lv_obj_clean deletes objects cause a crash❌ There is no crash, only focus misalignment; LVGL automatically removes objects from the group when deleting them
Suspect that “the radio page was not destroyed”❌ [pm] destroy 'radio' is printed normally and the page is indeed destroyed — but the controls are still in the group (the group and the object lifecycle are two separate things)
Fix only §3.1 (unified cleanup by the page manager)⚠️ Mostly recovered, but the group count is still 18 (= desktop 17 cells + 1 non-desktop object) → this shows there is still one member that does not belong to the desktop, so §3.2 must be fixed as well

Solution

5.1 Unified cleanup by the page manager (one fix for all pages)

Add the following to lv_pm/lv_page_manager.cc:

Call it in pm_page_destroy() before page->onDestroy(page) (at that point all objects are still valid; onDestroy may already have freed timers/callbacks):

In normal cases the number removed should be 0 (no log printed); once there are leftovers, one line is printed, making it easy to later discover that “a certain page forgot to clean up again”.

This file is a .cc, but it originally only included <string.h>; using fprintf/stderr requires adding #include <stdio.h>, otherwise compilation reports MAKE_RC=2 'stderr' was not declared.

5.2 Change the visibility check to be “ancestor-aware”

group_find_neighbor() in main.c:

nav_obj_visible() is an existing utility function in main.c that checks HIDDEN level by level along the parent chain.

Verification

6.1 Group counts (page manager log)

After the fix, entering/exiting the radio page:

19 is exactly the number of controls that the radio page attached. The remaining 1 is the slider from §3.2 (it is created persistently by the status bar and is not managed by any page, so it can only be worked around via “ancestor-aware navigation”).

6.2 Key-press measurement (ssh_tools/nav_trace.py "E B L L")

Clean restart of the application → enter the radio page → return to the desktop → press Left twice in a row:

  • The focus moves left continuously: idx 8(radio) → 7(Bluetooth) → 6, matching the desktop icon order;
  • content / box are both non-null → the focus box can be drawn every time;
  • Compared with content=(nil) box=(nil) before the fix, the problem is gone.

Screenshot shots/btz_3.png: the desktop “Bluetooth” icon has a pink focus box around it (confirmed by human eyes).

6.3 Not done / to be observed

  • Only the path “radio page → desktop” was covered. The other 10+ pages go through the same pm_page_destroy cleanup, so in theory one fix covers them all; however, they were not tested page by page. If anything abnormal occurs, look directly at the [pm] log line to confirm which page missed the cleanup.

Lessons learned

  1. Entry and exit into a globally shared container must be paired. The focus group is a global singleton; if pages only add and never remove, it is equivalent to dumping garbage into a common area — and the symptom appears on the victim (the desktop), not the culprit (the page), making it extremely hard to reason back from the symptom. Anything that is a “global registry” should have its lifecycle managed uniformly by the framework layer; do not count on each page being conscientious.
  2. The lifecycle must be viewed at two layers: an object being deleted ≠ being removed from the group. The page can be destroyed perfectly cleanly ([pm] destroy printed normally), yet the controls still linger in the group. When investigating this kind of problem, printing “how many elements are currently in the container” is far more effective than printing “what I deleted”.
  3. The visibility check must be ancestor-aware. LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN only describes the object itself; “can the user see this control right now” is a question along the parent chain. Any pattern in LVGL that “hides a container” steps on this pitfall.
  4. “Restarting the application fixes it” is a strong signal of “external pollution”. It shows that the fault is not in the algorithm itself, but that the runtime state has been dirtied elsewhere — the investigation direction should immediately shift from “is the computation correct” to “who touched the shared state”.
  5. Use fprintf(stderr, ...) for diagnostic traces. printf writes to files with block buffering, so logs lag badly and are easily misjudged as “the code did not execute” (the same pitfall was also stepped on while investigating the FM page).
  6. Sink “specifications” into the framework layer instead of writing them into documentation. This case originally just wrote “remember to remove” in the documentation, and nobody followed it; after moving it into pm_page_destroy, old and new pages became compliant in one shot. Conventions that can be enforced by code should not rely on conscientiousness.

entry.title: GBA Screen Shows Vertical Stripes / Tearing
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_05 — GBA picture shows vertical stripes / tearing (the source pitch is ignored)

Symptoms: There is a picture now, but the whole screen shows regular vertical stripes, with content misaligned horizontally, as if “torn”.
Root cause layer: The source row stride (pitch) addressing of the miniretro frame callback video_cb, plus concurrent scanning of the frame buffer.
Fix effort: extern/miniretro/miniretro.c totals +81/-13 cumulatively (including this item and the bugfix_20260923_04 black-screen fix; this item is the main part).
File name: bugfix_20260923_05_GBA画面纵向条纹撕裂.md
Related commit: (to be backfilled after commit)
Date: 2026-09-23

Symptoms

  1. GBA games can be entered (see bugfix_20260923_04), but the screen shows regular vertical stripes: the content is cut into vertical bands, with black gaps between the bands, and the whole image is misaligned horizontally and unreadable (the user describes it as “tearing-like”).
  2. Comparison: the FC game picture is completely normal, with no stripes.

Initial suspicion: is this timing tearing (missing vsync) or addressing misalignment? Both can “look like tearing”, so they must be distinguished first.

Scope of impact

  • Affected: GBA (240×160, RGB565, pitch=512).
  • Not affected: FC (fceumm, whose pitch happens to equal width×2) — linear reads are also correct, so it has always been normal.
    This change is transparent to FC.

Root cause

The video_cb in miniretro.c completely ignores the row stride given by the core:

  • FC: pitch = 256 × 2 = 512 bytes, which happens to equal width × 2 → linear reads are correct by coincidence.
  • GBA: the core log measured video_cb: 240x160 pitch=512 — that is, 256 pixels per row, while the visible width is only 240.
    A linear read skips (256-240)=16 pixels too few per row, so the misalignment accumulates row by row over 160 rows, equivalent to about 10 rows of source data,
    causing the picture to be sheared horizontally and, due to cross-row wraparound, producing regular stripes.

Hard evidence: add a one-time print in video_cb; after recompiling, the log outputs [miniretro] video_cb: 240x160 pitch=512 fmt=2 (每行像素=256) — pitch and width really are inconsistent.

Diagnosis process

  1. Detour one (critical): it was initially judged to be vsync tearing, so double-buffered page flipping was added to miniretro (the fb has yres_virtual=3840, i.e. 3 pages, using FBIOPAN_DISPLAY to switch pages).
    But the user’s feedback was “still the same, not fixed” → this shows it is not tearing at all, but data misalignment.
  2. Capture the screen to distinguish: we cannot see the device screen with our own eyes, so capture the screen on the real machine —
    the device-side python3 os.pread dumps /dev/fb0 (capturing the foreground page according to the current yoffset) → retrieve it via SFTP → decode it locally as PNG by [R,G,B,X] → open the image and look.
    One look makes it clear: it is regular vertical stripes (content misaligned, with black gaps), not tearing lines. The direction immediately shifts to addressing.
  3. Locate pitch: read the video_cb source and find (void)pitch; and the linear read; add a one-time print to confirm pitch=512 ≠ 240×2=480.
  4. Rule out double buffering as the culprit: double buffering is kept (it has no side effects and has defensive value against real tearing in the future), but adding the pitch fix is the real cure.

Solution

The video_cb in extern/miniretro/miniretro.c:

  1. All three pixel format branches are changed to fetch data row by row by stride (falling back to width*2 when pitch==0):

    XRGB8888 (pitch/4) and 0RGB1555 (pitch/2) work the same way.
    Note that the result is still 0xAARRGGBB, with the R/B byte swap done uniformly by scale_rotate90 before writing out.

  2. Keep double-buffered page flipping (g_dbuf, FBIOPAN_DISPLAY; automatic degradation to single buffering on first failure) —
    on this machine FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC returns EPERM and is unavailable, so page flipping is the only viable anti-tearing measure.

  3. Recompile: cd extern/miniretro && sh build.sh.

Verification

  • Controlled self-test: after the fix, run miniretro mgba_libretro.so <rom> standalone and capture 20 consecutive frames on the real machine:
    • the title screen (an orange-garbed character + a cyan radiating background) and the opening animation (multiple character portraits) are clear across the whole screen;
    • no vertical stripes, no tearing, no black gaps.
  • Log: 双缓冲页翻转已启用(yres_virtual=3840), video_cb: 240x160 pitch=512.
  • Device end state: 1×lvgl_demo + 1×lvgl_watchdog.sh, with no miniretro leftovers.
  • Pending user confirmation on the real machine: desktop → “GBA Games” → confirm key to start → visually confirm no stripes/tearing → exit with the 买单 (pay-the-bill) key (116).

Lessons learned

  1. “Tearing” and “stripes/misalignment” are two different diseases and must be separated first.
    • Tearing = a timing problem (the frame buffer is being modified while it is being scanned) → double buffering / page flipping / vsync.
    • Stripes = an addressing problem (the per-row stride is computed wrong) → check pitch/stride.
      Applying double buffering without distinguishing them wastes a round (this bug did exactly that, wasting one round trip).
  2. When interfacing with different libretro cores, pitch must be used; never assume pitch == width × bpp/8.
    mGBA aligns buffer rows to 256 pixels, making pitch/2 = 256 ≠ width(240).
    Linear reads are “correct by coincidence” when width happens to divide pitch evenly; switch resolution and it is exposed immediately.
  3. When you cannot see the device screen, capturing the screen on the real machine is the most cost-effective diagnostic means:
    os.pread("/dev/fb0") → SFTP → decode as PNG locally by [R,G,B,X] → look at the image with human eyes.
    Telling at a glance whether it is stripes or tearing beats a pile of log reasoning.
  4. Quantitative metrics like “proportion of non-black pixels” can only prove “there is a picture”; they cannot prove “the picture is correct”; judging “whether the picture is correct” requires human eyes.
  5. Do not treat “changed but had no effect” as noise: the user said “still the same” twice, which is precisely the strongest signal that “the root cause judgment was wrong”.

entry.title: GBA Game Audio Crackles and Pops
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_06 — GBA game audio crackles and pops

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Module: GBA game page / extern/miniretro/miniretro.c (audio chain)
  • Impact: All GBA games (FC games are affected by the shared code as well, but FC’s audio rate happens to equal the reported value, so the problem is not exposed)

1. Problem symptoms

The game picture is normal and the sound is audible, but it is accompanied all along by crackling noise / popping, with the music and sound effects both smeared.

2. Scope of impact

  • GBA application (mgba_libretro.so + miniretro)
  • All applications that output audio via /tmp/bt_audio.fifo (FC games, the music/video page, all sharing the same resampling function)

3. Root cause analysis

Running MINIRETRO_AUDIO_DEBUG=1 miniretro mgba_libretro.so <rom> in a controlled manner on the device prints the probe, yielding hard evidence:

  • fpc=1097: the core delivers 1097 frames of audio per retro_run.
    Meanwhile av_info reports sample_rate=32768 and fps=59.73, so theoretically it should be 32768/59.73 ≈ 548 frames.
    The actual value is 2× — the core’s real audio rate is about 65536 Hz, while the reported value is only half.
  • The old code converted according to the reported value: out_per_in = 44100/32768 = 1.346,
    so each frame needs to output 1097 × 1.346 ≈ 1476 frames.
  • But the output buffer is only static int16_t buf[2048] (=1024 frames), so every frame is truncated to 1024 frames,
    i.e. about 30% of the samples are stably dropped on each callback.
  • Result: about 58,000 frames are produced per second while Bluetooth only consumes 44,100 frames, drop persists at 2~12 times per second,
    and frames are truncated on top of that — the triple superposition is the persistent crackling/popping heard.

4. Fix

Stop trusting the core’s self-reported sample_rate, and switch to adaptive resampling based on the measured rate:

  • A sliding average of the frame count per callback, s_fpc (it depends only on the core, not on this machine’s speed);
  • Measure the wall-clock frame rate s_fps_meas every 300ms;
  • in_rate = s_fpc × s_fps_meas, out_per_in = 44100 / in_rate;
  • Expand the output buffer to int16_t buf[8192], completely eliminating truncation;
  • Do not emit sound before the first measurement window produces a result (the frame counts of the first batch of callbacks at startup are extremely unstable; the measured first frame has only 82 frames, and using it to estimate the rate would compute a several-fold overproduction, flooding the fifo right at startup).

Note: you cannot convert using the “core’s nominal rate”. This machine’s CPU, even at 100%, can only reach about 56fps; if converted at the nominal 59.73fps, only 0.94 seconds of audio would be produced per second → Bluetooth would be short of 6% of the data per second → persistent underload popping.
The audio must be stretched to real time based on the measured frame rate (see section 6 for regression risks in detail).

5. Verification method and results

MetricBefore fixAfter fixVerdict
Whether each frame’s output hits the buffer limitConsistently hits the cap (2048 int16)About 1700 int16, does not hit the cap✅ Truncation eliminated
drop (fifo write failures per second)2 ~ 120✅ No dropped frames
out_rate (actual output frame rate)≈52200 (overproduction)43000 ~ 45800 (target 44100)✅ Aligned with Bluetooth consumption
fps5056—

The probe is kept in the code, enabled with the MINIRETRO_AUDIO_DEBUG=1 environment variable, and disabled by default in production.

6. Regression risks

  • The overall pitch is about 6% too low: this machine can only run at 56fps (target 59.73fps), and after the audio is stretched to real time, the pitch shifts down accordingly.
    The picture is likewise 6% slower, so the audio and video content remain synchronized; only the tone is slightly lower. The closer the frame rate is to 60, the smaller this deviation.
  • Completely eliminating this requires raising the frame rate to 59.73fps, while rendering + emulation already saturate the CPU (measured busy_ms≈990/1000).
  • FC games share this function: FC’s fpc × fps exactly equals its reported sample rate, so the conversion result is identical to the old logic and its behavior is unchanged.

7. Related files

  • Device: /home/lvgl_demo/lvgl_demo/extern/miniretro/miniretro.c
  • Local: ssh_tools/_tmp/miniretro.c, ssh_tools/gba_probe2.py (probe script)

entry.title: GBA Screen Has Red and Blue Swapped (Color Regression)
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_08 — GBA picture has red and blue swapped (color regression)

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Module: GBA game page / scale_rotate90() in miniretro.c
  • Impact: The colors of all GBA game pictures (FC games share the same function and are likewise affected)

1. Problem symptoms

The game displays normally, with no stripes or tearing, but the overall colors have red and blue swapped:
the orange-gold Dragon Ball turns blue and the “DRAGON BALL” title turns blue. This is a color regression introduced by this round of changes.

2. Scope of impact

  • All GBA / FC game pictures
  • Does not affect the LVGL desktop and list page (that is a separate drawing path)

3. Root cause analysis

This machine’s framebuffer has a real byte order of [R, G, B, X],
while the pixels packed internally by LVGL/miniretro are 0xAARRGGBB (stored little-endian as [B, G, R, A]),
so before writing to fb, one and only one swap of the R/B two bytes is required.

To improve the frame rate, this round rewrote scale_rotate90() into two steps:

  1. First rotate the source image by 90° into the small canvas rot_buf (also moving the R/B swap over from the second step to reduce hot-loop overhead);
  2. Then scale-copy rot_buf into the framebuffer.

When making the change, the swap was added only at the new position, and the original swap in the second step’s hot loop was forgotten to be deleted → the swap executed twice →
R/B is swapped back, equivalent to no swap → red and blue are reversed overall.

4. Fix

Delete the R/B swap in the second step’s scaling loop, keeping the R/B swap done only once in the small-canvas step
(that step has only src_w × src_h pixels, 38400 for GBA; putting it in the scaling loop would be 780,000 times).
Add a comment at that position explaining “the first step has already swapped; swapping here would swap it back”, to prevent stepping on the pitfall again.

5. Verification method and results

After decoding captured frames into PNG on the device (os.pread dump + decoding as PNG by [R,G,B,X]), confirm visually:

VersionDragon Ball colorVerdict
Swapped twice (regression version)Blue✗ Red and blue swapped
Swapped once (after fix)Orange-gold✅ Correct

6. Regression risks

  • Color correctness can only be confirmed visually / via frame capture; it cannot be replaced by metrics like “proportion of non-black pixels” (which is exactly what fooled us this time).
  • If the scale_rotate90() structure is changed again in the future, ensure that the R/B swap is done exactly once in total across the whole chain.

7. Related files

  • Device: /home/lvgl_demo/lvgl_demo/extern/miniretro/miniretro.c (scale_rotate90())
  • Local: ssh_tools/_tmp/miniretro.c, frame capture script ssh_tools/gba_capture.py

entry.title: GBA Screen Stutters and Hangs When Exiting a Game
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_07 — The GBA screen stutters / hangs when exiting a game

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Module: GBA game page / miniretro.c exit path + lv_pages/gba_game_page.c
  • Impact: All GBA game exits, as well as FC game exits (shared miniretro)

1. Problem symptoms

When pressing the 买单 (pay-the-bill) key (116) to exit a game, the picture freezes / becomes garbled for a few seconds before returning to the list, sometimes leaving half a game frame on screen.

2. Scope of impact

  • GBA / FC game exit back to the list
  • Subsequent LVGL rendering (the residue stays smeared in place until that area is redrawn)

3. Root cause analysis

Three causes are superimposed:

  1. miniretro has no SIGTERM handling
    The parent process’s gba_exit_to_list() only sends kill(pid, SIGTERM) and then falls back to SIGKILL after 120ms.
    SIGTERM’s default behavior is to kill the process directly → the main loop’s cleanup section never executes (fb_restore/munmap are all skipped).
  2. The fb stays on the flipped page
    Double buffering uses FBIOPAN_DISPLAY to switch pages; when killed, the foreground page stays at yoffset=1280 (page 1),
    while LVGL only draws to page 0 → the screen keeps showing that old game frame on page 1.
    Measured evidence: after kill -TERM, reading FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO yields yoffset=1280 (0 after the fix).
  3. LVGL only refreshes dirty areas
    A known project conclusion: LVGL only flushes self-drawn areas and does not clear the whole screen. The pixels written directly to fb0 by miniretro are not in LVGL’s dirty areas,
    so even if drawing resumes, the residue cannot be erased.
    In addition, the game picture has 100px letterbox black bars at the top and bottom (out_w=720 → out_h=1080) that are not part of the output area; failing to clear the screen before starting leaves the last UI frame from LVGL, looking like a “garbled band”.

4. Fix

  • miniretro.c: add on_quit_signal(), install SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that only set quit=1, letting the main loop exit naturally and complete cleanup.
  • miniretro.c: add fb_restore() — use FBIOPAN_DISPLAY to return yoffset to 0 and clear the entire virtual video memory.
    Call it once each at exit cleanup and before entering the main loop (the latter incidentally clears residue in the letterbox area).
  • gba_game_page.c: widen the grace period of gba_exit_to_list() from 120ms to 250ms,
    leaving time for a graceful exit, with SIGKILL still as the fallback on timeout.

5. Verification method and results

Controlled device-side test (read the fb state immediately after kill -TERM):

The log showing [miniretro] 退出 proves that cleanup (including fb_restore()) was reached instead of being interrupted by SIGKILL.

6. Regression risks

  • The SIGKILL fallback path is retained: if the child process hangs abnormally, force-kill it after 250ms, in which case the fb is not reset,
    but the full-screen redraw of gba_timer_cb + an LVGL refresh still saves the day (only 130ms more delay than before the fix).
  • Clearing the screen is a memset of the entire virtual video memory (3 pages × 1280 rows), about 11MB, a one-time cost that is negligible.

7. Related files

  • Device: /home/lvgl_demo/lvgl_demo/extern/miniretro/miniretro.c
  • Device: /home/lvgl_demo/lvgl_demo/lv_pages/gba_game_page.c
  • Local: ssh_tools/_tmp/miniretro.c, _fc_ref/gba_game_page.c, ssh_tools/gba_audio_exit_fix.py

entry.title: Stutter When Exiting a GBA Game Back to the List
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_09 — Stutter when exiting a GBA game back to the list (the kernel reclaims input device fds extremely slowly)

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Module: GBA game page exit path / extern/miniretro/miniretro.c / kernel input subsystem
  • Impact: The response speed of exiting a GBA game back to the list (FC page shares miniretro, theoretically equally slow but not changed this time); also includes a zombie process problem of “not reaped after a forced kill fallback”

Difference from bugfix_07: 07 fixed “the picture freezes / leaves residue after exit” (the fb stays on the flipped page).
This one fixes “the picture comes back slowly“, which still exists after 07 — pressing the 买单 (pay-the-bill) key takes about 0.35~0.4 seconds to return to the list.

1. Problem symptoms

Press the 买单 key (116) to exit the game; the picture is no longer the game picture, but the list takes about 0.35~0.4 seconds to appear, which feels like “a stutter”. User feedback: “exiting the game back to the list still stutters”.

2. Scope of impact

  • GBA game exit back to the list (fixed this time)
  • FC game exit (shares the same miniretro, theoretically equally slow; FC page unchanged, behavior unchanged)
  • Fixed along the way: a child process left unreaped after one SIGKILL fallback → became a zombie under lvgl_demo

3. Root cause analysis

Measured with 2ms-granularity sampling + segmented timing added in the miniretro exit path (ssh_tools/gba_exit_latency.py):

Reproduced device by device (miniretro is not needed; opening/closing alone reproduces it):

DeviceNodeDriverclose() time
Physical four keys/dev/input/event0sprd-gpio-keys39 ~ 215 ms
Another set of keys/dev/input/event1sprd-eic-keys~80 ms
Headset key/dev/input/event2headset-keyboard~80 ms

Conclusions:

  1. The child process’s internal cleanup is not the bottleneck (deinit/pan/screen clear total about 30ms).
  2. This machine’s kernel takes a fixed tens to hundreds of milliseconds to close sprd input devices. When a process exits, the kernel must close these fds, and no user-space change can avoid it — so “the child process actually disappearing” takes at least ~340ms.
  3. There are also two segments of idle waiting on the parent side:
    • the usleep(250ms) hard wait inside gba_exit_to_list();
    • gba_wait_thread() uses a blocking waitpid to wait for the child process to “actually disappear” (= after that 340ms in the kernel) before resuming LVGL.
  4. The two segments add up → about 0.35~0.4s. The stutter is not a rendering problem; it is “waiting for an unnecessary event”.

4. Fix

Core idea: UI recovery no longer waits for the child process to die; instead, the child process actively notifies the parent process at the moment “the picture has been handed back”.

miniretro side (child process)

  • The cleanup order is fixed as: core_deinit() (must be kept; mGBA persists the battery save .sav here) → fb_restore() (flip back to page 0 + clear the screen, about 35ms) → notify_parent_ui_released() → _exit(0).
  • notify_parent_ui_released(): sends SIGUSR1 to the parent process.
    It must be explicitly enabled by the parent process via the environment variable MINIRETRO_UI_RELEASE_SIGNAL before it is sent — the default action of SIGUSR1 is to terminate the process, so any caller without a handler installed (such as the FC page) would be killed upon receiving it.
  • After _exit(0), no more individual close(fd)/munmap: the kernel has to do it on exit anyway, and those 340ms are pushed to the background, not blocking the UI.

Page side (lv_pages/gba_game_page.c)

  • gba_launch(): install signal(SIGUSR1, gba_ui_release_handler) + setenv("MINIRETRO_UI_RELEASE_SIGNAL","1",1) before fork (this must happen before fork, otherwise the signal may arrive first → the default action kills the process).
  • gba_exit_to_list(): only kill(pid, SIGTERM), with no waiting at all.
  • gba_wait_thread() has two phases:
    • Phase ① waits with 5ms granularity for “SIGUSR1 received or the child process actually exiting” (≤500ms fallback); as soon as either is satisfied, call hardware_keys_set_grab(true) → remove the interceptor → app_runtime_set_lvgl_paused(false);
    • Phase ② background reaping: after a 5s timeout, SIGKILL and synchronously waitpid to reap it.
  • Keep the millisecond timing [miniretro][timing] logs for direct reference next time a regression occurs.

5. Verification method and results

① Exit latency comparison (controlled measurement)

MetricBefore fixAfter fix
Child process internal cleanup385 ms37 ms
Parent process receives “picture handed back”—40.6 ms
Child process actually disappears (kernel reclamation)394 ms337 ms (already unrelated to the UI)

② Handshake protocol verification (ssh_tools/gba_ui_release_test.py, a Python pseudo parent process, no physical key presses needed)

③ Whether recovery is “instantaneous”: lv_tick_inc() executes unconditionally in the main loop (main.c:635), so LVGL time keeps running during the pause, meaning the 100ms timer has long expired after recovery and the first lv_timer_handler() triggers a full-screen redraw; the main loop ticks every 10ms. That is, the recovery path has no extra waiting.

Expected feel: press 买单 → hand back the picture in 40ms → immediately redraw the list (previously 0.350.4s).

6. Regression risks

  • The child process neither notifies nor exits: after 500ms in phase ①, the UI still recovers, degrading to the old behavior without hanging; in phase ②, force-kill and reap after 5s.
  • During the child process’s exit (0.30.4s), it still holds the fds of fb0/evdev (the kernel is reclaiming them), but it no longer draws and does not affect LVGL (LVGL holds fb0 itself; yoffset is a device-level state).
  • FC page unchanged: exiting still waits for the child process to disappear (~340ms). To speed it up as well, move the three page-side changes above to fc_game_page.c (the miniretro side is ready, and the signal gate is off by default).
  • Deployment discipline (pitfall stepped on this time): extern/miniretro/build.sh is gcc ... -o miniretro, writing the target file directly. When recompiling while the user is playing, a launch action happens to exec into the half-overwritten binary → the child process hangs inside exec, startup fails, and after 2.5s it is force-killed by the fallback and left unreaped (zombie).
    The unified requirement now is: binaries must always be “compiled to *.tmp → mv -f atomic replacement”, with deployment going through ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.py.

7. Related files

  • Device: /home/lvgl_demo/lvgl_demo/extern/miniretro/miniretro.c
  • Device: /home/lvgl_demo/lvgl_demo/lv_pages/gba_game_page.c
  • Local: ssh_tools/_tmp/miniretro.c, _fc_ref/gba_game_page.c
  • Diagnostic/verification/deployment scripts: ssh_tools/gba_exit_latency.py, ssh_tools/gba_ui_release_test.py, ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.py
