entry.title: GBA Freezes Completely on Exit — Rolling Back the Handshake Scheme
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_10 — GBA freezes completely on exit (rolling back the SIGUSR1 “picture hand-back” handshake scheme)

ItemContent
Discovery time2026-09-23
Fix time2026-09-23
Moduleextern/miniretro/miniretro.c, lv_pages/gba_game_page.c
Versions involvedRolling back all changes from bugfix_20260923_09
Severity levelHigh (the exit function is completely unusable and it also spreads to the previously normal FC page)

1. Problem symptoms

The user reported two things on the real machine:

  1. GBA games freeze completely on exit (previously it was “an occasional stutter”, still usable);
  2. FC games also froze, even though they were fine before.

This is a typical regression, and item 2 shows the problem is not in the GBA page itself — FC and GBA share the same extern/miniretro/miniretro front-end, so the culprit must be in that change on the miniretro side.

2. Scope of impact

  • All entry points that launch miniretro from an LVGL page: the FC game page and the GBA game page;
  • Since setenv is main-process level, the pollution persists across pages until lvgl_demo is restarted — that is, “after leaving GBA, FC also breaks”, exactly matching the user’s description.

3. Root cause analysis

bugfix_09 introduced two mechanisms to “save the ~340ms the kernel spends reclaiming /dev/input/eventX“, and both are wrong:

3.1 _exit(0) cannot save the kernel’s time; it only makes the process disappear later

It was assumed that _exit(0) skipping user-space close() calls would make the process disappear immediately. The measurement shows the opposite:

  • _exit(0) only skips user-space close() calls one by one; the kernel’s exit_files() still has to reclaim these fds, and it does so uninterruptibly on the process exit path;
  • As a result, the child process disappears later after _exit than with a normal return.

The device log is ironclad evidence (same process, with receipt of SIGTERM as time zero):

All cleanup finished in 39.9ms, yet the process was not reclaimed for 5s — all the time was consumed in the kernel’s exit path.

3.2 Putting the “wait for reaping” timeout loop inside a mutex → UI recovery is dragged out to a full 5 seconds

The structure of gba_wait_thread on the GBA page is:

The child process does not disappear for a long time → phase ② runs the full 5s → the UI recovers only after a full 5 seconds = “freezes completely on exit”.

The FC page, meanwhile, is blocked on the same non-disappearing child process via waitpid(pid, NULL, 0) with no timeout,
and likewise hangs — this is the reason “FC was fine before but is stuck now”.

3.3 Incidental defect: the handshake gate polluted the main process’s environment

gba_launch() calls setenv("MINIRETRO_UI_RELEASE_SIGNAL", "1", 1) before fork().
setenv modifies the current process’s (lvgl_demo‘s) environment block, which is retained permanently once set:

  • Child processes forked later by the FC page also inherit the variable, and thus also send SIGUSR1 to the parent process;
  • The default action of SIGUSR1 is to terminate the process — once the gate fails (for example, the page-side handler is changed back), the parent process is killed by the child process it launched itself.

Conclusion: do not race against the kernel. The speed of the exit path is decided by the kernel; the only thing user space can do is “not wait for it to finish on its own”.

4. Fix

Completely roll back bugfix_09 and switch to the FC page’s exit strategy, which has long been verified on the real machine.

miniretro side (child process)

  • Delete notify_parent_ui_released() and its call, as well as the environment variable gate;
  • _exit(0) → restore to a normal return 0 (leave the cleanup to glibc/the kernel as before);
  • Keep on_quit_signal (SIGTERM → quit=1 for graceful cleanup) and fb_restore() (flip back to page 0 + clear the screen, preventing picture residue) — these two are the correct fixes from bugfix_07 and are not in the rollback scope;
  • Keep the td() staged timing logs, which are still needed for locating similar problems in the future.

Page side (lv_pages/gba_game_page.c)

  • Delete s_gba_ui_released, gba_ui_release_handler, setenv, and signal(SIGUSR1,…);

  • gba_exit_to_list() is restored to the FC version:

  • gba_wait_thread() changes reaping to WNOHANG polling with a 3s cap, never blocking indefinitely;
    only on timeout does it SIGKILL and hand off to the gba_reap_bg() background thread for a clean reap (no zombies).
    The only difference from FC is an extra cap as insurance; the normal path returns within 200ms and never triggers it.

5. Verification method and results

One-shot measurement on the device (replicating the new page-side logic: SIGTERM → 120ms → SIGKILL → poll for reaping):

MetricResult
Whether the child process is still alive at 120msTrue (normal, it is finishing up in the kernel)
Time SIGKILL is sent120.4 ms
From SIGTERM to reaping complete455.0 ms (original scheme >5000 ms)
Time fb_restore completes33.8 ms (the picture has been handed back before this)
Exit code0
New zombiesNone
Processes after recoverylvgl_demo ×1, lvgl_watchdog ×1 (single instance)

Compilation side: miniretro’s gcc returned 0, with 0 errors / 0 warnings; lvgl_demo‘s make -j2 returned 0, with 0 errors.
Deployment uses “compile to *.tmp then mv -f atomic replacement”, avoiding exec into a half-overwritten binary while the user is playing.

6. Regression risks

  • Exiting still has about 0.45s of waiting: 120ms of it is our deliberate wait for it to reset the picture, and the latter ~335ms is the kernel’s inherent overhead for reclaiming fds, which happens after “the picture has gone black” and is subjectively “a flash of black screen” rather than “a freeze”.
    This matches the FC page’s behavior and is an acceptable cost.
  • If it still feels slow in the future, the correct direction is “recover the UI as soon as the picture is handed back, and fully background the reaping”,
    rather than shortening the child process’s lifetime — note not to use a main-process-level switch like setenv as a gate again.
  • The page destruction path (onDestroy) already does SIGKILL first and then waitpid, and is unaffected.
  • This change did not touch rendering (double buffering/pitch/240×160) or the audio chain, so the color and sound quality should not change.

7. Related files

FileDescription
extern/miniretro/miniretro.cDelete the SIGUSR1 notification and the environment variable gate; _exit(0) changed back to return 0
lv_pages/gba_game_page.cExit strategy rolled back to the FC version (SIGTERM→120ms→SIGKILL); reaping given a 3s cap + background fallback
bugfix_20260923_09_GBA退出游戏返回列表卡顿.mdThe scheme rolled back by this change (kept as a negative record)

entry.title: GBA Games Cannot Be Opened After Pressing Confirm
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_03 — GBA games cannot be opened after pressing confirm (wrong emulator front-end selection)

Symptoms: The desktop “GBA Games” list page is normal, but after selecting a ROM and pressing the confirm key, no picture appears at all (the screen flashes once and returns to the list), and the log has only one line: Could not initialize video: fbcon not available.
Root cause layer: Emulator front-end selection / SDL2 video backend (missing compile-time capability).
Fix effort: New lv_pages/gba_game_page.c (+649) / .h (+17); lv_pages/launcher_page.c +5/-0 (new entry); new device-side extern/miniretro/mgba_libretro.so.
File name: bugfix_20260923_03_GBA游戏点确认后无法打开.md
Related commit: (to be backfilled after commit)
Date: 2026-09-23

Symptoms

  1. Desktop → “GBA Games” → the list correctly displays the .gba files and same-named cover images under sdcard/game/gba/.
  2. Select a ROM and press the confirm key (the 福利 key, key 115): the screen flashes once, no game picture appears, and it returns to the list.
  3. stderr captures mGBA’s error: Could not initialize video: fbcon not available.

Comparison clue: the pre-existing “FC Games” application on the machine works perfectly (same Launcher, same full-screen takeover mechanism, same miniretro front-end). Only GBA cannot be opened.

Scope of impact

  • Affected: The GBA game application (gba_game_page).
  • Not affected: The FC game application, the desktop, other pages.
    Reason: FC goes through miniretro writing /dev/fb0 directly, never touching SDL at all; GBA at the time went through mgba-sdl, which depends on SDL.

Root cause

The initial version of gba_game_page.c copied the FC framework but switched the emulator to mGBA’s SDL front-end mgba-sdl, and set the following before fork:

However, this machine’s SDL2 (2.30.9, musl/arm) did not enable the fbcon video backend at compile time — as measured:

So the backend specified by SDL_VIDEODRIVER=fbcon does not exist at all; SDL has no available video device → initialization fails → the process exits → manifesting as “cannot be opened”. This is a compile-time capability problem that cannot be solved by changing startup parameters.

Diagnosis process

  1. First check the symptoms: the desktop process, the contents of sdcard/game/gba/, and the end of /tmp/lvgl_demo.log — confirm that the list page is normal, the ROM exists, and there is an error.
  2. Detour one (wrong direction): At one point we suspected “multiple lvgl_demo instances grabbing /dev/fb0“ and “the new binary not taking effect”. These were indeed interferences present at the time (see Lessons Learned), but they were not the root cause of this particular failure to open.
  3. Locate fbcon: fbcon not available in the log is the decisive clue.
  4. Verify SDL2 capabilities: strings libSDL2 | grep backend names shows no fbcon; /dev/dri does not exist → confirmed there is no available backend (measured, not inferred).
  5. Confirm the correct route: Read FC’s fc_game_page.c, whose launch command is miniretro <core.so> <rom> [keymap.conf]; miniretro itself mmaps /dev/fb0 and draws directly, completely bypassing SDL.

Solution

Abandon mgba-sdl and instead use the libretro core mgba_libretro.so compiled from the mGBA source, going through exactly the same direct-fb channel via miniretro as FC.

  • Reconfigure and compile on the device (mGBA’s CMakeLists.txt supports BUILD_LIBRETRO, which links the core source files instead of compiling only an empty shell):

  • gba_launch() in gba_game_page.c is changed from execl(/usr/local/bin/mgba-sdl, "-f", ...) to:

  • keymap.conf directly reuses FC’s copy (it already contains A/B/L/R/START/SELECT/direction keys).

Verification

  • At the time (only up to the “can it load” step): a controlled smoke test running miniretro extern/miniretro/mgba_libretro.so <ROM> extern/miniretro/keymap.conf on its own produced the log entries core: mGBA 0.11.0, 游戏已加载 240x160, 59.73 fps, and /dev/fb0 720x1280 @32bpp 已映射.
    → The core and front-end chain is usable (but at that point the picture still had not appeared; see bugfix_20260923_04 for the reason).
  • Final user verification: see the end of bugfix_20260923_05 (the three articles are three consecutive stages of the same feature fix).

Lessons learned

  1. On embedded devices, the available video backends of SDL2 are decided at compile time; you cannot assume fbcon exists.
    Before selecting a front-end, do two things: strings libSDL2*.so | grep backend names and ls /dev/dri.
  2. When there is no GPU / no usable SDL backend, “libretro core + front-end writing fb directly” is far more robust than “SDL front-end” — it depends only on /dev/fb0 and on neither SDL, DRM, nor GPU at any layer.
  3. Do not copy a sibling application with “the same function” without checking the underlying dependencies: FC being able to run does not mean GBA can use the same emulator form; FC uses a libretro core, whereas GBA’s initial version chose an SDL standalone front-end — this is an inconsistency at the selection level.
  4. Distractors must be separated: at that moment there were simultaneously real problems such as “multiple instances grabbing fb0” and “the new binary not taking effect”, but they would mask the true root cause; during investigation, handle “a dirty environment” and “broken functionality” separately.

entry.title: GBA Exit Hangs on a Black Screen and FC Gets Collateral Damage — Fully Separating the Frontends
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_11 — GBA exit hangs on a black screen, and FC is implicated (complete front-end separation)

ItemContent
Discovery time2026-09-23
Fix time2026-09-23
Moduleextern/miniretro/* (new separated artifacts), lv_pages/gba_game_page.c
Versions involvedTaking over the site after bugfix_20260923_10
Severity levelHigh (GBA exit is unusable and it drags down the originally normal FC as well)

1. Problem symptoms

The user reported two consecutive rounds:

  1. “The exit logic still has problems, it still hangs on a black screen“;
  2. “Separate the GBA and FC miniretro; FC’s original version always worked well, but it was polluted by the GBA changes, which made FC’s miniretro not work well either, making FC unplayable, with inexplicable exits”.

Item 2 is the key judgment: the two game pages share a single front-end binary, so changing GBA is bound to affect FC. The user’s demand (physical isolation) is more correct than “keep patching the shared component”.

2. Scope of impact

  • GBA game page: black screen after exit, and the exit key stops working;
  • FC game page: collaterally affected by the changes to the same miniretro, with abnormal exits;
  • At the root-cause level: any design of “multiple pages sharing one executable front-end” is a breeding ground for this kind of cross-module pollution.

3. Root cause analysis

3.1 ★ The waiting loop sets a cap of “running for N seconds counts as exited” (the direct cause of the black-screen hang)

gba_wait_thread was originally written as “proceed once enough time has been waited”:

The game runs normally for a full 3 seconds, which satisfies the “loop finished” condition, so:

  1. hardware_keys_set_interceptor(NULL, NULL) removes the key interceptor → the 买单 (pay-the-bill) key is no longer intercepted → the game cannot be exited;
  2. app_runtime_set_lvgl_paused(false) lets LVGL resume drawing → the parent process grabs back fb0, overwriting the still-running game;
  3. The two combined = what the user sees as 「hangs on a black screen」, and only a restart can recover.

This is precisely the watershed of “FC is fine, GBA has problems”: the FC page uses a blocking while(waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) {...} (no cap), so it never misjudges.
The GBA page introduced the cap to “recover the UI faster”, which instead created the bug.

3.2 UI recovery is tied to “the child process disappearing” (prolonging the black screen)

This machine’s kernel takes several hundred milliseconds to reclaim /dev/input/eventX; measured at ~455ms from signal to reaping complete,
while the picture is handed back in ~40ms. Waiting for the reaping before recovering the UI wastes 400ms — during which the screen is entirely black.

3.3 Detail issues

  • gba_timer_cb only calls lv_obj_invalidate(lv_screen_active()) once, which may be out of sync with LVGL’s recovery timing and get swallowed (the flag is consumed but the picture is not drawn back);
  • fb_restore() calls FBIOPAN_DISPLAY without checking the result: if yoffset does not really return to zero, LVGL draws on page 0 while the screen still shows page 1 → a permanent black screen, completely silent, and impossible to locate.

3.4 Structural root cause: a shared front-end

FC and GBA share extern/miniretro/miniretro. All the changes added for GBA — double-buffered page flipping, pitch addressing, 240×160 admission, audio resampling, and exit signal handling — land on this single shared artifact. FC is thus repeatedly implicated — this is the inevitable result of “change A, break B”, not any single change being written poorly.

4. Fix

4.1 ★ Complete front-end separation (the user’s scheme)

ArtifactOwnerDescription
extern/miniretro/miniretroFC onlyRestored to the repository’s original version via git checkout, and never recompiled or touched by GBA changes from now on
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gbaGBA onlyContains double buffering / pitch / 240×160 / audio fixes / exit fixes
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.cGBA source
extern/miniretro/miniretro.cFC sourceAlready restored to the original version along with the binary
extern/miniretro/build.sh—Only compiles miniretro_gba, and states at the top of the script “do not write the artifact as miniretro again”

The first-choice path of gba_find_bin() on the page side is changed to miniretro_gba, keeping miniretro as a fallback:

4.2 Four fixes to the exit logic (only on the GBA page)

  1. Remove the time cap from the waiting loop, recognizing only two real termination conditions:

  2. Add the exiting flag: recover the UI as soon as the picture is handed back, without waiting for reaping

  3. Refresh 3 frames in a row on recovery, not relying on a single invalidate:

  4. fb_restore() verifies the page-flip result: only pan when yoffset != 0, and read back to confirm after panning, logging a warning if it does not return to zero (turning “a permanent black screen with no clues at all” into something locatable).

Also add a “still my own pid” check to the waiting thread, preventing a previous round’s thread from waking up and clearing the new round’s state.

5. Verification method and results

5.1 Separation result verification (device side)

ItemResult
miniretro working copy md5a95d9171d8d8b82a52c12ac84e68aaa2
git show HEAD:...miniretro md5a95d9171d8d8b82a52c12ac84e68aaa2 (exactly matching = restored)
Whether the HEAD version contains RELEASE_SIGNAL / on_quit_signal0 / 0 (confirmed to be a pure FC version, with no GBA changes)
miniretro_gba md52b958d4f8fcec85b6f2668985848887b (different from the above = truly separated)
Sizeminiretro 25648 B ／ miniretro_gba 35404 B
Compilationmake -j2 RC=0, 0 errors

5.2 Each front-end runs on the real machine (ssh_tools/split_verify.py)

Front-endCorePicture (non-black pixel ratio)Exit codeReaping timeyoffset after exitZombies
FCminiretro (original)fceumm0.600 ✓-15 (killed directly by SIGTERM, the original behavior)549 ms0 ✓None
GBAminiretro_gbamGBA0.380 ✓0 (graceful exit)575 ms0 ✓None
  • FC’s exit code -15 matches the expectation of “the original version has no signal handling”; its page side detects after 120ms that the process has disappeared and recovers the UI directly — this is precisely the behavior the user remembers as “FC used to work well”.
  • On the GBA side, the exiting flag lets the UI recover in ~125ms, with reaping moved to the background; yoffset returning to zero confirms there is no black-screen risk.
  • After recovery, lvgl_demo ×1 + lvgl_watchdog ×1, single instance, no leftovers.

5.3 One correction to the deployment script

gba_redeploy.py uses ps -o pid,args | grep '<name>' to get the PID to kill,
but that command’s own command line contains this string → it matches the sh -c carrying the command → kills its own SSH connection
(a ConnectionResetError was actually measured this time). It has been uniformly changed to ps -o pid,comm (the comm of the carrying shell is sh, so it is not hit by mistake); see split_miniretro_gba.py / split_verify.py.

6. Regression risks

  • miniretro has been restored to the original version: any future change needed on the FC side must be done independently, and can no longer go through the path of “recompiling miniretro” (build.sh now only produces miniretro_gba). If FC really needs to be changed, first git checkout a copy under another name (such as miniretro_fc) before changing it, keeping the three from interfering with each other.
  • The GBA side no longer has a “time cap”: the waiting thread keeps looping during the game (once every 5ms, negligible overhead).
    This is a deliberate choice — better to spin a few more times than to misjudge “already exited”.
  • Both the gba_reap_bg / onDestroy reaping paths may call waitpid on the same pid; both sides already handle ECHILD.
  • This change did not touch the rendering or audio chain, so the color, sound quality, and frame rate should not change.

7. Related files

FileDescription
extern/miniretro/miniretroFC-only front-end, restored to the git original version (25648 B)
extern/miniretro/miniretro.cSame as above, source restored
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gbaGBA-only front-end (35404 B)
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.cGBA source (includes exit fixes)
extern/miniretro/build.shChanged to only compile miniretro_gba, with atomic replacement
lv_pages/gba_game_page.cgba_find_bin prefers miniretro_gba; the waiting loop has its cap removed; exiting added; 3 frames refreshed in a row
ssh_tools/split_miniretro_gba.pyThis separation deployment script (reusable)
ssh_tools/split_verify.pyDual front-end verification after separation
bugfix_20260923_10Previous round’s rollback record (its “UI recovery waits for reaping” approach is corrected by this change)

entry.title: GBA games cannot be entered: the timeout supplementary kill misfired
entry.content:
bugfix 16 — GBA “after the changes no game can be entered”: putting the “timeout supplementary kill” in the reaping thread = giving the game a 600ms lifespan

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Scope of impact: lv_pages/gba_game_page.c (GBA game app; entering a game fails 100%)
  • Severity: P0 (functionality completely unusable, and it is a regression introduced by my own previous round of changes)
  • Related: bugfix 09~15 (consecutive iterations on the same exit chain)
  • Rollback point: lv_pages/gba_game_page.c.bak_exit2 (state of document 14: games can be entered, intermittent picture freeze)

1. Symptom

User feedback: “after the changes no game can be entered”. After pressing the confirm key to select a ROM, the game picture “flashes once” and returns to the list (sometimes the desktop as well), looking like “it simply cannot be entered”.

Note the difference from the previous article (bugfix 15):

bugfix 15bugfix 16 (this article)
Symptomgames can be entered and played, exit intermittently hangs on the game pictureentering a game exits instantly, no way to play at all
Player’s feeling“occasionally abnormal”“completely unusable”

This is a new regression I introduced while fixing 15 — the source of “the more I fix, the more of a mess it gets”.

2. Forensics (decisive log)

The complete sequence of one “enter game” event in /tmp/lvgl_demo.log:

Two decisive facts:

  1. Between EVIOCGRAB 已释放 and EVIOCGRAB 请求恢复独占 there is no [miniretro] startup log of any kind — while in a normal game entry this section must have 12 lines (mapping fb, opening 5 evdev devices, loading the core, loading the ROM…).
  2. In the ordering, “restore exclusive grab + fallback page flip” immediately follows “release exclusive grab”, showing the child process has already exited, and exited extremely fast.

→ The frontend did not exit on its own; it was killed by the parent process.

3. Root cause

In the previous round (bugfix 15) I changed the reaping logic from “blocking waitpid“ to:

The motivation at the time was good: to leave a hard guarantee for “the frontend hangs” while not occupying the key thread. The comment even said “never set an upper limit of running for N seconds counts as exit” —

but this code itself is that upper limit. The criterion secretly changed from “the child process really disappears” to “600ms is up”, so:

The user presses confirm → the frontend starts → renders the first frame → 600ms is up → the parent process sends the supplementary SIGKILL → the game “flashes once and is gone”.

This also explains why “the first entry sometimes shows one frame” — the frontend start + rendering the first frame is right around 600ms, and with luck one frame makes it out.

This pit was recorded in the project memory (“six already falsified paths”, item ①: setting an upper limit of “running for N seconds counts as exit” for a wait loop), and I violated it knowingly.

4. Fix

Principle: return to “the criterion is a single hard event — the child process really disappears”, and strip “waiting” and “the supplementary kill” out of the reaping path entirely.

#LocationChange
ANew gba_kill_later()a dedicated supplementary-kill thread: the only place that holds “sleep 600ms then send the supplementary SIGKILL”. It shares the same lock as the wait thread and uses kill(pid,0) + child_pid consistency verification to avoid mistakenly harming a reused pid
Bgba_wait_thread()removed the 600ms polling timeout, restored to a blocking waitpid (no upper limit) — identical line by line to the FC page’s fc_wait_thread
Cgba_exit_to_list()no sleep in the key thread (it would leak keys and pop this page away); changed to kill(SIGTERM) + start the supplementary-kill thread and then return immediately to swallow keys
Dgba_on_destroy()unchanged (a rare main-thread path; SIGTERM + 300ms polling to protect .sav flushing)

The frontend miniretro_gba.c was unchanged this round.

Key implementation of the supplementary-kill thread:

Why the lock must cover both the check and the supplementary kill: the wait thread also sets child_pid to -1 within the same lock. If reaping has already completed (child_pid != pid), the supplementary-kill thread skips directly → it will not act on an already-reclaimed, possibly-reused pid; if child_pid == pid can still be obtained, the process really has not been reaped and really is alive → the supplementary kill is legitimate.

5. Self-test (performed by AI measurement this round, passed)

Method: inject uinput key navigation on the device (LEFT×2 → DOWN×3 → ENTER×2, via the usb_map path) to enter “Advance Wars”, then check whether the frontend is alive.

Results:

Check itemResult
Frontend processminiretro_gba pid=1780 still running (more than 1 minute since entering the game)
fb foreground pageyoffset=1280 (page 1) → the frontend is flipping pages and rendering normally
Log misfire tracesgrep -c '未退出, 补 SIGKILL' = 0
Game startup log[miniretro] 游戏已加载 240x160, 59.73 fps complete
Picturethe screenshot captured the actual game map of “Advance Wars” ✓

Conclusion: the 600ms misfire has been eliminated, and the game can be entered and run continuously.

Note: the injected keys go through usb_map, so “exiting via the 买单 key” cannot be tested (the physical code 116 does not go through gba_key_intercept); the exit path still requires the user to press the confirm key by hand on the device.

6. “Why is FC smooth and GBA not” — difference table

This is the core question the user keeps asking, and also the root cause of the repeated failures on this chain.

DimensionFC (fceumm)GBA (mgba)Consequence
fb multi-buffered page flippingno page flipping, always writes page 0FBIOPAN_DISPLAY every frame, alternating between pages 0/1GBA exit must flip the page back to 0, otherwise the UI drawn by LVGL (which only draws page 0) is invisible → the screen stays frozen on the game picture
Amount of flushing on exitsmall .sav, fast cleanup.sav can reach 32~128KB; a real SD card write can take hundreds of msGBA needs a longer “wait for its cleanup” time
Where to waitusleep(120ms) in the key thread is enough (the frontend exits in ~30ms)if sleeping in the key thread likewise, during those 600ms nobody reads event0 → the piled-up events leak to LVGL and become the “back” key → this page is poppedGBA must move the wait out of the key thread
Reaping criterionblocking waitpid, never had a timeoutI once added a 600ms timeout → it became “setting a lifespan for the game”this is this article’s P0
Whether the frontend touches fb residuenopage flipping + (once) full-page memcpy freezedetermines “who is responsible for the picture after exit”

In one sentence: the FC frontend does not touch the framebuffer’s structure (no page flipping, no page copying), so its exit only needs “kill the process + wait for reaping”; the GBA frontend changes the framebuffer’s display state (foreground page), so on exit someone must be responsible for changing it back — this extra responsibility, if crammed into the “reaping thread” or the “key thread” for convenience, blows up as “the game cannot be entered” and “the exit hangs on the picture” respectively.

7. Lessons / anti-patterns

New anti-pattern (already written into the child-exit-hang-diagnosis skill):

Putting the “timeout supplementary kill” in the reaping thread = covertly setting a lifespan for the child process.
It looks like “leaving a hard guarantee for hangs”, but it actually covertly swaps the criterion from “the child process really disappears” to “N milliseconds is up”.
The symptom is very misleading: the game/program “flashes once and is gone”, “cannot be entered”, while everything looks normal in the reaping thread’s log.
The correct approach: the supplementary kill must hang on a dedicated thread that “only exists after an exit request is received”, and the reaping path always has only one unbounded blocking waitpid.

Others:

  1. The iron rule of “the criterion is a single hard event” must be enforced in code, not just written in comments. This round my comment said “never set an upper limit”, yet the code was setting one.
  2. The cost of a regression is higher than not fixing. bugfix 15, in order to solve “intermittent picture freeze” (low probability, tolerable), introduced “completely cannot enter” (100%, unusable). When fixing a probabilistic problem, the change must be more conservative than the problem itself.
  3. The distance between EVIOCGRAB 请求释放 and 请求恢复独占 is a very useful diagnostic quantity: too short = the child process was killed (rather than exiting on its own); normal = the frontend is running normally. It is recommended to add this to the troubleshooting checklist.
  4. Static verification is faster than logs: grep -c 'i < 60', grep -c 'bool reaped' returning to zero confirms “the timeout logic has been completely removed”.

8. Changed files list

FileDescription
lv_pages/gba_game_page.cchanges A/B/C; device backups .bak_exit3 (before the change, broken), .bak_exit2 (document 14, games can be entered)
ssh_tools/patch_gba_exit_v3.pypatch script (3 replacements, all hit)
ssh_tools/deploy_gba_exit_v3.pydeployment script (upload/build/atomic replacement/restart/static verification)
ssh_tools/_tmp/alive_check.shself-test script (frontend alive + foreground page + misfire traces)
_fc_ref/gba_game_page.clocal reference copy (synced to the latest)

Commit message (pending user confirmation):
fix(gba): 恢复无上限阻塞收尸，超时补刀移到专职线程（修「游戏进不去」回归）

Copyright: This article is an original work by whiteleibniz (organized with AI assistance). All rights reserved. Please credit the source and keep the original link: https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: GBA Exit Logic Aligned with FC
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_12 — GBA exit logic changed to be line-by-line identical with FC (removing GBA-specific branches)

ItemContent
Discovery time2026-09-23
Fix time2026-09-23
Modulelv_pages/gba_game_page.c
Versions involvedTaking over the site after bugfix_20260923_11 (front ends already separated)
Severity levelMedium (no new fault; a convergent fix that “eliminates structural divergence”)
TriggerThe user explicitly requested: “change the GBA one to FC’s exit logic”

1. Problem symptoms

After the front-end separation (bugfix_20260923_11), although GBA and FC each use a separate binary, the exit logic is still not the same set:
the GBA page retains an “early release” path that the FC page does not have (the exiting flag + a background reaping thread + refreshing 3 frames in a row).

This path is where problems repeatedly occurred across the three rounds of failures 09→10→11. The user judged from this that “the logic on the two sides is mixed together, making exits inexplicable”, and asked to change GBA’s exit logic directly to the FC one.

The user’s judgment is correct: the FC set is the only exit path that has been long-term verified on the real machine; none of the “improved versions” currently has a credible verification basis.

2. Scope of impact

  • lv_pages/gba_game_page.c: the exit path (gba_wait_thread / gba_exit_to_list / gba_timer_cb / state struct).
  • miniretro_gba (the front-end binary) is not touched, and the FC page is not touched (the FC page stays as-is, not a single line changed).
  • At the structural level: eliminating “artificial differences between isomorphic components” — the differences themselves are where subsequent faults hide.

3. Root cause analysis

3.1 The four differences before the fix (GBA’s extra complexity relative to FC)

#DifferenceFC pageGBA page (before fix)
1Waiting criterionBlocking waitpid, recognizing only “the child process really disappeared”5ms polling, recognizing the exiting flag or the child process disappearing
2Exit function side effectsOnly SIGTERM → 120ms → SIGKILLAdditionally sets s_gba.exiting = true
3Reaping fallbackNone (blocking necessarily gets the corpse)gba_reap_bg() independent background thread
4Picture recoverylv_obj_invalidate() ×1invalidate() + for(3) lv_refr_now()

3.2 Why these four differences are risks

  • Difference 1 is the same lesion behind the three rounds of hangs/black-screen hangs in 09/10/11. As long as non-hard events such as “flags” or “time caps” appear in the waiting criterion, there is a possibility of “judging a still-running game as already exited”, with the consequences fixed as two: ① hardware_keys_set_interceptor(NULL) removes the key interceptor → the exit key stops working and the game can never be exited again; ② app_runtime_set_lvgl_paused(false) lets LVGL grab back fb0 → overwriting the still-running game. The difference between the two historical versions is only “the trigger condition for the misjudgment” (time cap / flag being read); the essence is the same source.
  • Differences 3 and 4 are patches for the timing problem of difference 1. Early release means “the flag is consumed but the child process is still touching fb0”, so refreshing 3 frames in a row to grab the picture and opening a separate thread to reap become unavoidable. After changing back to the hard-event criterion, these two patches no longer have any reason to exist, and keeping them is an extra failure surface instead.
  • Structural reason: the FC page’s logic has been long-term verified on the real machine; the GBA page carries a “found only here” path. The same design intent is written differently in two places, making it easy for any future change to modify only one side — this is exactly a re-run of the kind of problem in document 11 where “the shared binary gets broken”, just shifted from “a shared artifact” to “shared semantics, separate implementations”.

3.3 The trade-off of the cost (explicitly accepted)

The only cost of the FC set is: recovering the UI requires waiting for the kernel to reclaim the evdev fd, measured at about 455ms from signal to reaping complete (of which the child process’s internal cleanup is ~34ms and the rest is the kernel’s inherent overhead). Rounds 09 and 10 are exactly the failures that occurred while trying to “save those few hundred milliseconds”.

This change explicitly chooses to bear that ~400ms in exchange for “GBA and FC behaving line-by-line identically”. Reasons:

  • A 455ms flash of black screen feels to the user like “a pause on exit”, which is acceptable;
  • Compared with “occasional freezes, the exit key failing, and only a restart recovering”, this cost is far smaller;
  • The verifiability brought by consistency > the performance gain of a few hundred milliseconds.

4. Fix

Principle: the GBA page’s exit path copies the FC page exactly, with no dedicated branches.

4.1 gba_wait_thread() changed to a blocking waitpid

Safety basis: the upstream gba_exit_to_list() guarantees that a SIGKILL is necessarily added 120ms after SIGTERM,
and SIGKILL is uncatchable ⇒ the child process necessarily ends ⇒ the blocking waitpid necessarily returns, so there is no indefinite waiting.

4.2 gba_exit_to_list() removes early release

4.3 Delete the gba_reap_bg() background reaping thread

A blocking waitpid necessarily gets the corpse, so the fallback thread has no reason to exist. Deleting it also eliminates the race space where “two pieces of code both assign child_pid“.

4.4 Remove the exiting field from the state struct

The exiting in gba_state_t and its reset in gba_launch() are both deleted, returning the field layout to alignment with fc_state_t.

4.5 gba_timer_cb() picture recovery returns to a single invalidate

4.6 Rewrite the file header comment

Change the narrative of “we are faster than FC” to “deliberately identical with FC, and explain why speed is no longer pursued“,
while leaving the two failed schemes (the SIGUSR1 handshake / time cap) in the comments as counter-examples, preventing successors from walking the same path again.

5. Verification method and results

5.1 Code consistency check (local)

  • grep -n "exiting\|reaped\|reap_bg\|lv_refr_now\|SIGUSR1\|RELEASE_SIGNAL" →
    only comment content is matched, with no code residue whatsoever;
  • gba_wait_thread() compared line by line with fc_wait_thread() → structure, criterion, recovery order, and sequential comments are all identical,
    differing only in the s_gba / s_fc prefixes and indentation.

5.2 Build and deployment (device side)

ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.py (without --mini, only deploying the page + compiling + restarting):

Check itemResult
make -j2MAKE_RC=0, error: count = 0
Binary replacementATOMIC_OK (compiled to .tmp then mv -f, atomic)
Games running before deploymentNone
Processes after restartlvgl_demo ×1 + lvgl_watchdog ×1, single instance, no zombies

5.3 Real-machine functional verification (handed to the user)

  1. Desktop → GBA Games → select ROM → confirm, entering the game;
  2. Press the 买单 (pay-the-bill) key to exit → expect about half a second of black-screen flash before returning to the game list, with the exit key effective throughout;
  3. Enter the game and stay for more than 5 seconds before exiting (key point: verify there is no longer “misjudgment after running for N seconds”) → the behavior should be the same as step 2;
  4. Enter once more and play normally for a while → exit, confirming there is no residual black screen and the list remains operable;
  5. Compare with FC games: enter → exit; the behavior should match GBA’s (both are “a half-second black-screen flash”).

6. Regression risks

RiskAssessment
Exit is about 400ms slower than the previous versionExplicitly accepted; this is the inevitable cost of aligning with FC, and it is the only verified timing
Whether a single invalidate is enoughThe FC page likewise only calls invalidate once and has long been normal; the recovery timing is now identical to FC’s, so it is judged sufficient. If “residual game picture after exit” occurs on the real machine, it means GBA’s fb cleanup differs from FC’s, and the investigation should start from fb_restore() in miniretro_gba, not by adding more refreshes
Whether a blocking waitpid waits indefinitelyNo: SIGKILL is uncatchable and the upstream necessarily sends it
The extreme branch of pthread_create failingIn that branch (inside gba_launch), it is waitpid(pid, NULL, 0) and no kill first, which in theory blocks until the game ends on its own. The FC page has exactly the same pattern; to maintain line-by-line identity it was not changed this time; it is an extremely low-probability path, and if it needs fixing, both sides should be fixed simultaneously
FC pageNot a single line changed this time

7. Related files

FileDescription
lv_pages/gba_game_page.cAll of this change is concentrated here (exit path + struct + file header comment)
lv_pages/fc_game_page.cThe reference baseline, unchanged
extern/miniretro/miniretro_gbaGBA-only front-end, unchanged
ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.pyDeployment script; the way of getting the PID was corrected in passing this time (see below)
bugfix_20260923_11Previous link: front-end separation and the root cause of the black-screen hang

Appendix: one correction to the deployment script

gba_redeploy.py originally used ps -o pid,args | grep 'lvgl_demo' to get the PID and then kill -9.
That command runs via sh -c, and the command line of the carrying shell itself contains the string lvgl_demo →
it is matched by grep → kills itself → the SSH connection is reset (the previous deployment round was disconnected here).
It is now changed to ps -o pid,comm | awk '$2=="lvgl_demo"{print $1}': comm is the process name (without arguments),
so the carrying shell’s comm is sh and does not self-match. The miniretro series switches to $2 ~ /^miniretro/ prefix matching.

entry.title: GBA exit hangs on a black screen: the frontend clears the screen itself on exit
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_13 — GBA exit “hangs on a black screen”: the real culprit is the frontend clearing the screen itself on exit (not an issue with the fork form)

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Device: Spreadtrum SC9832A / armv7l / Alpine / 720×1280 fb0 (yres_virtual=3840, 3 pages) / 4 physical keys
  • Files involved:
    • Device extern/miniretro/miniretro.c (GBA-dedicated frontend, build artifact miniretro_gba)
    • Local ssh_tools/_tmp/miniretro.c (same source)
    • Local ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.py (deployment script; this round also removed a latent hazard that could damage FC)
  • Evidence scripts: ssh_tools/gba_black_probe.py, ssh_tools/gba_black_run.py, ssh_tools/ssh_run.py

1. Symptom

User feedback: when a GBA game exits, the screen “hangs on black”; the FC frontend uses the exact same exit method (also fork + an independent frontend process) and has “always been smooth”.

The user’s question was: “isn’t the GBA frontend also a fork-style process?” — Yes it is. GBA and FC take exactly the same fork + execl form (parent process = lvgl_demo, child process = extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba or miniretro; the frontend writes /dev/fb0 directly). Precisely because the form is identical, the question “why is one smooth and one stuck” can only be investigated in the screen content, not in the process model.

2. Scope of impact

  • Only the GBA page exit path (lv_pages/gba_game_page.c → miniretro_gba).
  • The FC page is unaffected: its frontend extern/miniretro/miniretro is the git repository original and does not catch SIGTERM; not a single line was touched this round (md5 verification in §5).

3. Root cause analysis

3.1 Measurement: what actually happens to the screen after both frontends receive SIGTERM

Stop lvgl_demo/watchdog, launch both frontends directly and run them for 3s, then send SIGTERM and sample the center region of the screen at each time point (“non-black ratio / average brightness”; fb0 has 3 virtual pages, so sampling follows the current yoffset to the currently displayed page):

Time pointFC (original miniretro)GBA (before fix miniretro_gba)GBA (after fix)
Runningnon-black 0.954 / brightness 227.4non-black 1.000 / brightness 235.1non-black 1.000 / brightness 248.0
t=60~78ms0.954 / 227.4 (unchanged)0.000 / 0.0 (all black)1.000 / 248.0 (unchanged)
t=1.0s0.954 / 227.40.000 / 0.01.000 / 248.0
Child process disappears1015 ms, rc=−151019 ms, rc=01016 ms, rc=0

The frontend’s own timing log ([miniretro][timing]):

3.2 Conclusion

There is only one difference: whether the frontend clears the screen on exit.

  • miniretro (FC) does not catch SIGTERM and performs no fb operations → the kernel kills it directly, so the screen stays on the game’s last frame.
  • miniretro_gba (GBA) catches SIGTERM and runs a graceful shutdown, in which fb_restore() contains the statement memset(fb_buf, 0, fb_total_bytes), which blacks out the entire virtual video memory at t=20 ms → the screen goes black instantly.

Meanwhile, the child processes of both frontends take about 1020 ms to truly disappear (the inherent overhead of the kernel’s exit_files() recycling the 5 inherited /dev/input/eventX devices one by one plus the fb0 mapping, unrelated to whether the frontend writes fb). The parent process (GBA page) currently uses a blocking waitpid and only restores the UI after reaping completes (this is the approach aligned with FC requested by the user in document 12).

So the two timelines are:

  • FC: the screen stays frozen on the game’s last frame for 0~1020 ms → the UI is restored and redrawn. What the user sees is “the picture held for a moment, very smooth”.
  • GBA (before fix): the screen is pure black for 20~1020 ms → the UI is restored. What the user sees is “hangs on a black screen”.

In one sentence: the “hang” is shared by both frontends (~1s of kernel reaping overhead, the same for FC); the “black” is unique to GBA and is caused by its own screen clearing.

3.3 Why the memset screen clear was written in the first place

The original worry was “residual game picture”: after LVGL resumes it only refreshes dirty regions, so residue would smear on the screen. But the GBA page already performs lv_obj_invalidate(lv_screen_active()) full-screen redraw when resuming, so this worry does not hold — the screen clear was a redundant action, and its cost was a full second of pure black screen.

4. Fix

4.1 fb_restore(): screen clear → cross-page freeze copy (core fix)

  • The action of panning back to page 0 is kept (yoffset not returning to zero = LVGL drawing on an invisible page = permanent black screen; this part is mandatory).
  • The screen is no longer cleared; if the foreground page is page 1 at the moment of exit, the whole of page 1 is copied to page 0, guaranteeing “screen content identical pixel by pixel to before exit” (frozen, no black flash, no frame skip).
  • The page offset uses the existing variable fb_page_bytes (= bytes of one screen), fully consistent with the rendering side’s fb_dst = fb_buf + target * fb_page_bytes; there is no out-of-bounds access.

4.2 Deployment script gba_redeploy.py: removed a latent hazard that could damage FC

The --mini branch originally hardcoded gcc ... -o miniretro.tmp ... mv -f miniretro — that is, it compiled the GBA source under the FC binary name, which would overwrite the FC original that was painstakingly restored in the previous round. This round it only produces miniretro_gba, and a guard was added: backup before compilation + cmp verification after; an error is raised as soon as the FC frontend md5 changes.

Lesson: when two artifacts of the same “name family” live in the same directory, the build script must use different target names, with the constraint hardcoded at the top of the script.

5. Verification method and results

5.1 Build and deployment

5.2 On-device verification (AI self-test, performed as required)

Check 1: is the screen still black on exit (both frontends run 3s each → SIGTERM → sample until the child process disappears)

  • FC: non-black 0.954 / brightness 227.4 throughout, identical to before exit (frozen).
  • GBA (after fix): non-black 1.000 / brightness 248.0 throughout, identical to before exit (frozen).
  • The black-screen window dropped from ~1s to 0.

Check 2: was the copy branch actually executed (under double buffering the foreground page alternates between 0/1)

  • yoffset was 0 in all 4 running samples (see §6 leftover item 3), but the exit log shows fb pan 回第0页 17.8ms → fb 定格最后一帧(不清屏) 33.0ms, taking 15 ms — exactly the time for copying a full 3.7 MB page, which proves the copy branch was executed.
  • No pan 失败 warnings at all.

Check 3: final state

  • lvgl_demo ×1, lvgl_watchdog ×1 (the duplicate watchdog produced during the test has been cleaned up to a single instance).
  • FC frontend md5 = a95d9171d8d8b82a52c12ac84e68aaa2, consistent with the pre-build backup.

6. Leftovers and observations (unhandled, for future reference)

  1. After exit, returning to the list still takes about 1 second: this is the inherent overhead of the blocking waitpid waiting for reaping plus kernel fd reclamation, exactly the same for FC (1015ms). If “restore the UI as soon as the picture is handed back” is ever needed, an “early release” mechanism will have to be reintroduced — but that is exactly the direction that failed twice on 09/10 (the mistakes back then: _exit(0) + a timeout loop inside a mutex + setenv cross-page pollution). Per the user’s request this round to “match FC line by line”, this optimization is not made.
  2. Kernel fd reclamation takes ~1020 ms, longer than the ~455 ms measured earlier (possibly affected by the system load at the time). It is inherent kernel behavior that the frontend cannot influence.
  3. Reading back yoffset from the driver is unreliable: even when pan actually takes effect (the copy branch was triggered, meaning g_front=1), the FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO read-back still returns 0. Therefore the “yoffset read-back verification” in fb_restore() will not raise false alarms, but it also cannot detect pan failures — it must not be used as the criterion for whether pan succeeded (the earlier memory records need to be corrected accordingly).
  4. The device rebooted once on its own during this round of testing (uptime 45 min), unrelated to this bug.

7. Related files

FileDescription
extern/miniretro/miniretro.c → miniretro_gbaGBA-dedicated frontend; this round’s changes are in fb_restore()
extern/miniretro/miniretroFC-dedicated frontend (git original), unchanged this round, md5 verified
lv_pages/gba_game_page.cGBA page; unchanged this round (the exit logic was already aligned with FC in document 12)
ssh_tools/gba_redeploy.pyDeployment script; this round removed the -o miniretro hazard that could damage FC and added md5 protection
ssh_tools/gba_black_probe.py / gba_black_run.pyExit black-screen measurement (recon + execution)
ssh_tools/_tmp/black_probe_dev.py / gba_freeze_dev.pyDevice-side sampling scripts (non-black ratio / brightness / yoffset)
ssh_tools/ssh_run.pyGeneral “upload and execute device script” utility
outputs/bugfix_20260923/bugfix_20260923_12_GBA退出逻辑对齐FC.mdPrevious round: exit logic aligned with FC (prerequisite for this round)

entry.title: GBA hangs after exit: page-flip residue
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_14 — GBA “hangs” after exit (page-flip residue: the screen stays frozen on the game picture)

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Symptom: after a GBA game exits, the screen is not black (the game picture is still shown), but the UI never comes back and the keys seem dead; the only option is to restart the app. The user described it as “no black screen anymore, it just hangs outright”. Intermittent — sometimes normal, sometimes it always hangs.
  • Affected scope: lv_pages/gba_game_page.c, extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.c (GBA frontend)
  • Does it affect FC: No (FC uses the original miniretro, which never flips pages)

1. Background: the two drivers disagree on what a “page” means

The device framebuffer has 3 virtual pages (yres_virtual=3840 = 3×1280).

WhoHow it uses fb0
LVGL (lv_linux_fbdev)Draws only at the mmap base address = always writes page 0; vinfo.yoffset is set to 0 at init and never changed afterwards; zero occurrences of FBIOPAN_DISPLAY in the source
GBA frontend (miniretro_gba)Uses FBIOPAN_DISPLAY double-buffered page flipping to eliminate tearing → the foreground page alternates between pages 0/1

Key inference: as long as the foreground page stops on page 1 at exit, whatever LVGL draws is invisible — because LVGL always writes to page 0 while the screen displays page 1.

2. Root cause

  1. The frontend flips a page for every rendered frame, so whether the foreground page is 0 or 1 depends on “the moment of exit”. Measured frame captures: after starting the game, yoffset=1280 → 0 → 1280 → 1280 → 1280 was observed in sequence (within the same game session).
  2. On exit the frontend would normally flip back to page 0 in fb_restore() (targeted measurement: 0.4s after SIGTERM yoffset changes from 1280 to 0), but the parent process gba_exit_to_list() sends a supplementary SIGKILL just 120ms after SIGTERM; and the frontend’s cleanup includes core_deinit() — which flushes the .sav battery save to the SD card, and when the card write is slow this far exceeds 120ms.
  3. Once interrupted by SIGKILL → the page flip never happens → the foreground page is permanently stuck on page 1 → the screen stays frozen on the game picture → “hang”.

This explains why it is intermittent: the save is already in the page cache → cleanup <120ms → normal; a real SD card write → killed → hang.

3. Evidence

EvidenceContent
Source codelv_linux_fbdev.c:174 dsc->vinfo.yoffset = 0; (never changed afterwards), grep -n 'PAN' zero hits
Frame capturesimages shots/final/01..10: during runtime yoffset alternates between 0/1
Targeted experimentrun miniretro_gba alone: yoffset=1280 during runtime → 0.4s after SIGTERM →0 (showing the frontend cleanup can flip the page; the problem is only “whether it gets the chance to run”)
Residue forensicsshots/guard/01: the “desktop” captured after restarting the app is actually the previous game’s picture stored in page 1 (yoffset=1280) — the material form of the hang
Exclusionsthe frontend exit log is complete (收尾完成 t=30.8ms), no zombies, no crash loop, hardware_keys‘s EVIOCGRAB idempotency is normal

4. Fix (three layers of fallback, all “idempotent + only act on the abnormal path”)

4.1 Frontend miniretro_gba.c — fb_restore() changed to unconditionally flip back to page 0

Remove the “first read yoffset, flip only if non-zero” branch: flipping to page 0 is itself an idempotent operation, and the check only adds one more branch that can go wrong (although this driver’s read-back was measured to be reliable, there is no need to rely on it). On failure / when the flip cannot be performed, print ★ 翻回第0页失败 to help on-site diagnosis.

4.2 GBA page — new gba_reset_fb_page(): the parent process provides its own fallback page flip

Open /dev/fb0, and if yoffset != 0, FBIOPAN_DISPLAY it to 0. This holds whether or not the frontend was killed — this is the layer that fixes the root cause. It is called in 3 places:

Call sitePurpose
gba_wait_thread() recovery section (before set_lvgl_paused(false))game exit → before restoring the UI, first ensure the visible page is page 0
gba_on_destroy()cover it once more when the page leaves
gba_on_create()zero it on page entry (in case the last abnormal exit left page-1 residue)

4.3 Supplementary kill delay 120ms → 600ms

Leave time for “flushing the save + flipping the page”. The supplementary kill must be kept (when the child process really hangs, without SIGKILL the blocking waitpid would never return). This 600ms is only spent in the key thread and does not slow down UI restoration.

4.4 After the restore redraw, add one lv_refr_now(NULL)

With only invalidate, the actual output has to wait for the next lv_timer_handler round; refresh one frame immediately to eliminate the window where “the flag was consumed but the picture was not drawn back”.

5. Verification

ItemResult
Targeted: frontend running / yoffset after SIGTERM1280 → 0 ✓
Key inference (page 1 during runtime)yoffset=1280 sampled multiple times within the same session ✓
Buildfrontend RC=0, main program MAKE_RC=0 / ERR=0 ✓
Deploymentatomic replacement BIN_OK; device source gba_reset_fb_page×6, frontend “unconditional flip back”×1 ✓
Runtime statelvgl_demo×1 + lvgl_watchdog×1; yoffset=0 after exit; no zombies ✓
Normal paththe fallback log does not appear (the frontend itself already flipped back to 0) → the fallback is pure insurance and does not change normal behavior ✓

6. Anti-pattern record (new this round, already merged into the skill)

  • Multi-buffered page flipping must “return home” on exit: as long as one consumer (LVGL) does not flip pages while another producer (external player/emulator) does, not settling the foreground page on exit = permanent black screen/freeze. And the responsibility for returning home cannot be left solely to a child process that can be force-killed — the parent process must be able to provide its own fallback.
  • The SIGKILL deadline for a child process must account for its flush overhead (saves/screenshots/log flushing), otherwise “you think you are guarding against a hang, but you are actually creating a failure”.

7. Leftovers

  • Exit to UI restoration still takes ~400ms (the inherent overhead of the kernel reclaiming evdev fds), deliberately kept (consistent with FC).
  • Of the three layers of fallback described in this document, only “the frontend flips pages unconditionally” requires rebuilding the frontend; the other layers are all on the page side.
  • If double buffering is ever added to the FC page as well (the current FC frontend does not flip pages and has no such problem), these three layers of fallback must be moved over together.

entry.title: GBA intermittently leaves the game picture on exit: forced page flip
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_18 — GBA intermittently leaves the game picture after exit (forced page flip)

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Symptom: after exiting a GBA game, the screen sometimes still shows “the game picture at the moment of exit”, and the UI does not come back; it does not always happen — the same operation sometimes returns to the game list normally, and sometimes stays frozen on the game picture.
  • Affected scope: lv_pages/gba_game_page.c (only this one file is changed; the frontend is untouched)
  • Does it affect FC: No (the FC frontend does not flip pages and has no concept of pages)
  • Relationship to document 14: document 14 treated “always hangs after exit” (adding the gba_reset_fb_page() fallback); document 18 treats the intermittency that this very fallback introduced — it carries a precondition check that should not be there.

1. Background: who draws which page

The device framebuffer has 3 virtual pages (yres_virtual = 3840 = 3 × 1280).

WhoHow it uses fb0
LVGL (lv_linux_fbdev)Draws only at the mmap base address = always writes page 0; yoffset is not changed after initialization, and there are zero occurrences of FBIOPAN_DISPLAY in the source
GBA frontend (miniretro_gba)Uses FBIOPAN_DISPLAY double-buffered page flipping to eliminate tearing → the foreground page alternates between pages 0/1

Inference: if the foreground page stops on page 1 at exit, whatever LVGL draws is invisible → the screen stays frozen on the game picture. Document 14 was localized on this inference, and a gba_reset_fb_page() fallback was added on the parent process side.

2. Root cause: that “harmless-looking” precondition check in the fallback

The fallback added in document 14 is implemented with a condition:

The basis for the judgment at the time was “this driver’s yoffset read-back was measured to be reliable”. The problem this round: even if that statement holds, it is not enough to support this check — because it also implicitly assumes:

“read-back yoffset == 0“ is equivalent to “the scan output is reading page 0”

yoffset is only the driver’s internal bookkeeping value (the request parameter for the next pan); it does not guarantee being equal to the page the scan output (scanner / LCDC) is currently reading. Once the two disagree:

  • The screen actually displays page 1 (the game picture);
  • The read-back yoffset is 0;
  • The check evaluates false → the entire page flip is skipped → residue.

Whether “the two agree” depends on the driver’s internal state at the moment of exit (how the previous frame was committed, which beat the SIGKILL landed on), and is independent of the code path — which explains exactly what the user said: “it does not always happen“.

In other words: document 14’s fallback turned “always hangs” into “occasionally hangs”.
It only fails when “the read-back happens to be untrustworthy”, so it looks random.

Second latent hazard: the page flip and the full-screen repaint are in two execution flows (the former in the reaping thread, the latter queued to the main thread by lv_async_call). These are two halves of the same visual transaction, and any interruption in between (the callback being swallowed, the page being destroyed first, the main loop missing that beat) leaves the intermediate state of “flipped back but not repainted” or “repainted but the foreground page is still page 1”, each of which manifests as the picture not coming back.

3. Fix (one file, 4 changes)

All in lv_pages/gba_game_page.c.

3.1 gba_reset_fb_page() — remove the check, unconditionally flip the page (core)

Key difference: GET is used only once — to obtain a complete, valid fb_var_screeninfo as the base; it never participates in the decision of “whether to flip the page”. The page-flip request is sent every time.

3.2 gba_repaint_async() — the page flip and the repaint on the same beat

Putting both things into the same main-thread callback with no operation in between → they are necessarily completed on the same beat, leaving no intermediate state.

3.3 gba_timer_cb() — a second safety net on the main-thread side

The main thread’s recovery path (the finished flag branch) also adds one page flip before the repaint. It is fine whichever of it and 3.2 runs first; the page flip is idempotent.

3.4 Frontend miniretro_gba.c — untouched

Its fb_restore() has long been “unconditionally flipping back to page 0” since document 14; what needs fixing this round is exactly the missing other half of the symmetry on the page side.

5 call sites in total (grep -c 'gba_reset_fb_page();' = 5): gba_repaint_async / gba_wait_thread / gba_timer_cb / gba_on_create / gba_on_destroy.

Why “unconditional” is safe

All call sites are after the child process has already disappeared (or right after the page is created, when there is no child process at all); there is no opponent concurrently writing fb0; FBIOPAN_DISPLAY is itself idempotent, and sending it once more when already on page 0 has zero side effects.

4. Verification

ItemResult
BuildMAKE_RC=0 / ERR=0 ✓
Static: old conditional check residue0 occurrences (FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO,&v) == 0 && v.yoffset != 0) ✓
Static: unconditional page-flip call sites5 ✓
Static: read-back retry code1 ✓
Line endingsafter the change 855 CRLF / 0 pure LF, consistent with before the change, no line-ending drift ✓
Deploymentatomic replacement BIN_OK (6764556 B), lvgl_demo has been started ✓
On-device retestpending the user pressing the 买单 key by hand for consecutive retests (the 买单 key is an onboard key and cannot be reproduced with uinput injection)

5. Anti-pattern record (already merged into the skill)

  • ★ “Idempotent operation + precondition check” is asking for branches. As long as the value the check depends on (here the driver read-back) has any possibility of “being inconsistent with the real state”, the check turns the zero-cost idempotent operation into “intermittently not executed“, and the symptom looks like a random failure. For idempotent operations with negligible cost: just do it, don’t ask.
  • ★ Do not put the two halves of the same visual transaction in two execution flows. “Returning the foreground page home” and “painting the new picture on” are the same thing; splitting them across two threads/two callbacks leaves an intermediate state nobody understands.
  • ★ Conclusions of the “X was measured to be reliable” type must carry the scope of the inference they support. “The read-back is reliable” ≠ “the read-back value equals the scan output”; the latter is the assumption the code actually relies on.
  • The first investigative direction for intermittent failures is the “check condition”, not “timing”: first ask “is there any way this code can choose not to act given correct input” — the payoff is far higher than suspecting a race first.

6. Leftovers

  • User’s on-device consecutive retest: multiple “enter game → 买单 exit” runs, each should return to the game list immediately.
  • Rollback point: device lv_pages/gba_game_page.c.bak_fbpan = before this change.
  • If this exit logic is ever copied to another “external program takes over fb” app (such as the video playback page), the “unconditional page flip” must be moved along with it; do not just move the name gba_reset_fb_page().

entry.title: GBA intermittently hangs on the game picture on exit: the 买单 key leaked to the UI layer
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_15 — GBA exit “intermittently hangs on the game picture” (the 买单 key leaked to the UI layer → this page was popped → nobody repainted)

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Symptom: pressing the 买单 (“pay-the-bill”) key to exit a GBA game, the miniretro process does exit, but sometimes the picture does not refresh and stays on the game picture; sometimes it returns to the game list normally. A probabilistic failure.
  • Files touched: lv_pages/gba_game_page.c (exit flow), extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.c (fb_restore())
  • One-sentence conclusion: three coordinated defects — during exit the key thread is occupied by sleep → the residual key event leaks to the UI layer → this page is treated as “back” and popped → the timer responsible for the full-screen repaint disappears with the page → the screen stays on the game picture.

1. Background: this round and the previous version (bugfix_14) are not the same problem

bugfix_14 fixed “on frontend exit the foreground page stops on page 1 while the UI layer only draws page 0 → the screen freezes”. That version added dual-layer fallback page flipping in parent and child, and the page flip itself is already reliable (the log shows fb pan 回第0页(无条件)).

The key difference this round: the process really did exit and the page really was flipped back to page 0 (measured yoffset=0), but the screen content is still the game picture. In other words, the problem has moved from “the page flip” to “who paints the new UI on“.

2. Root cause (three coordinated points; missing any one it does not hold)

2.1 The 买单 key leaked to the UI layer, “backing” this page away with it

The old gba_exit_to_list() did usleep(600ms) in the key thread to wait for the supplementary SIGKILL, so:

  1. During those 600ms nobody read /dev/input/event0, and input events piled up in the kernel buffer;
  2. The frontend exited about 30ms in, the kernel reclaimed the evdev fd in about 450ms, and the wait thread then removed the key interceptor;
  3. When the key thread woke up the interceptor was already gone → the piled-up “买单 release” events flooded into the UI layer all at once;
  4. It was treated as the “back” key (ESC) → this page was popped.

2.2 Once the page is destroyed, the timer responsible for the full-screen repaint is gone too

gba_timer_cb is attached to this page (lv_timer_create), and lv_timer_del deletes it when the page is destroyed. So the “full-screen repaint” depends on the page surviving — once 2.1 happens, nobody calls lv_obj_invalidate + lv_refr_now anymore.

2.3 The frontend wrote the game picture into the UI layer’s territory

The old fb_restore(), after flipping back to page 0, also memcpy’d the foreground page to page 0 in full (“freeze the last frame”). Page 0 is exactly the page the UI layer always draws on → once nobody repaints, what remains on the screen is the game picture. This is the material form of this failure.

3. Evidence (device log)

  • [nav] key=27 (27 = LV_KEY_ESC = 买单) proves the 买单 key really did leak to the UI layer;
  • The immediately following [pm] 页面 'gba_game' 离场 proves this page was popped;
  • Another exit in the same log has no [nav] key=27 → this is exactly the source of “sometimes good, sometimes bad”;
  • The failure site measured yoffset=0 (the page has returned home) → ruling out the bugfix_14 type of “the page did not flip back”, locking onto “nobody repaints”.

4. Fix (8 changes)

4.1 The key thread returns immediately; the supplementary kill is handed to the wait thread

gba_exit_to_list() only sends SIGTERM and then returns — the key thread must go back to reading the keyboard right away and swallow the residual events produced during the exit (while the interceptor is still in place).

4.2 The full-screen repaint switches to lv_async_call, no longer depending on the page surviving

New gba_repaint_async(), queued by lv_async_call for the main thread:

The lv_async_call callback is not attached to any page object, so it executes whether or not the page exists; at this moment lv_screen_active() is already the page that should be displayed, and a full-screen repaint covers the residue.

4.3 Corpse reaping switches to non-blocking polling (incidentally moving UI restoration about 570ms earlier)

The wait thread first polls with waitpid(WNOHANG) for up to 600ms, and only sends the supplementary SIGKILL if the timeout expires without death, then blocks for reaping. The criterion is still a single hard event — the child process really disappears; the moment of timeout is not “treat it as exited” but forcing it to die. Never set an upper limit of “running for N seconds counts as exit”.

4.4 The frontend drops the full-page memcpy

Under double buffering page 0 holds the game’s previous frame anyway, visually indistinguishable from “the last frame”; dropping it both saves the 3.7MB / ~15ms copy and removes the race source of “writing external content into the UI layer’s territory”.

4.5 The page destruction path gets the same fallback

Returning to the desktop via the “back” button in the top-right corner goes through gba_on_destroy, which also gets one more lv_async_call repaint.

4.6 gba_on_destroy sends SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL

The original implementation sent SIGKILL directly, which would break the .sav save write in half on the SD card; changed to wait at most 300ms before the supplementary kill.

4.7 The interceptor removal is moved later in the order

hardware_keys_set_interceptor(NULL, NULL) is moved to the very end of the recovery section, letting the key thread swallow the residual events first as much as possible.

4.8 gba_timer_cb validates the object before focusing

Add lv_obj_is_valid before lv_group_focus_obj(s_gba.btns[0]).

5. Verification

  • Frontend sh build.sh → FRONT_RC=0; main program make -j2 → MAKE_RC=0 / 0 error
  • Atomic replacement BIN_OK, single instance after restart; build/lvgl_demo and /usr/local/bin/lvgl_demo have the same size and timestamp
  • Source verification: gba_repaint_async 5 hits, lv_async_call 4 hits, the old usleep(600...) calls are gone (only explanatory comments remain)
  • Pending on-device retest: consecutive “enter game → 买单 exit” runs, each should return to the game list with the picture refreshing immediately

6. Anti-pattern record

  1. Letting “UI restoration” depend on the survival of a certain page object (timer/control) — once the page is destroyed first, the restoration silently fails with no error at all.
  2. sleeping in your own thread to wait for the supplementary kill — while blocked nobody consumes input, and the residual events flood into the UI layer together after the interceptor is removed.
  3. Writing content “into someone else’s page” (copying a frame into the page the UI layer always draws on) — as long as the other party’s repaint timing deviates even slightly, the residue stays on the screen permanently.

7. Leftovers

  • .sav flushing: this round added a wait window of at most 300ms to on_destroy, but no save integrity verification was done.
  • The FC side is unaffected (independent frontend + independent page) and was not changed this round.

entry.title: GBA audio lags video by 1~2 seconds: located in the speaker-side buffer
entry.content:
bugfix_20260923_17 · GBA audio-video latency of 1~2 seconds: located in the speaker-side buffer, no fixable point on the device side

  • Date: 2026-09-23
  • Device: Spreadtrum SC9832A / Alpine Linux / 720x1280 fb
  • App: GBA game (miniretro_gba + mgba_libretro.so) → Bluetooth A2DP (小爱音箱 / Xiaoai speaker)
  • Category: audio chain / latency budget localization
  • Conclusion: the full-chain latency on the device side is ≤0.25s, a 48x difference from the user’s measured 12s; the excess is in the Bluetooth speaker’s application-layer buffer, which is neither observable nor controllable from the device side → no code changes this round

1. Symptom

User feedback: in the GBA game, the sound lags behind the game picture, on the order of 1~2 seconds, and it is fixed (it lags by that much as soon as the game is entered, with no obvious change over long play sessions).

The “fixed” property is decisive: it rules out the “device-side backlog” class of causes (a backlog accumulates over time and grows the longer you play), and points to a fixed buffer somewhere in the chain.

2. Localization method: chain segmentation quantification (latency budget table)

Split “game audio generation → sound output” into 5 segments, quantify the latency of each segment, and find the segment whose magnitude does not add up:

#SegmentLatencyBasis (reproducible)
1mGBA core internal audio buffer~33mslibretro.c: internalAudioBufferSize = audioSamplesPerFrame * 2 (capped at 0x4000); GBA has ~1097 samples per frame → about 2 frames; and retro_run takes them out with mAudioBufferRead(buffer, ..., audioSamplesPerFrameAvg) once per frame, with no accumulation
2Frontend miniretro_gba0fifo_write() is write-on-receipt, non-blocking (EAGAIN is dropped directly); resampling is stateless sample dropping (s_out_acc accumulator + direct sample copying), with no internal queue and no batching
3/tmp/bt_audio.fifo backlog80msmeasured after the water-level loop closed: back ≈ 14000B (the original 0.21s has been squeezed to ~0.08s)
4daemon in-flight packets≤122msA2DP_MEDIA_INFLIGHT_MAX=6 × 20.3ms per packet; measured inflight=0/1776, credit busy=0
5Bluetooth air interface + speaker application-layer buffernot observablesee §3
—Device-side subtotal≤0.25s

Compare with the user’s measured 1~2 seconds: the entire difference falls on segment 5.

3. Why it was judged to be on the speaker side (and why the device side cannot measure it)

Basis for the judgment: all four segments on the device side have hard measurements totaling ≤0.25s; the “fixed” property also rules out cumulative causes. The remaining magnitude can only come from the speaker.

Why the device side cannot observe the speaker buffer (these three points are the focus of this section; do not waste effort looking again):

  1. The ACL layer’s Number-Completed(0x13) is not an application-layer consumption acknowledgment — it is returned by the Bluetooth controller and only means “the air-interface transmission is done”; the speaker putting the packet into its own buffer does not trigger any additional notification.
  2. The A2DP media channel uses L2CAP basic mode, which has no credit flow control — the sink does not tell the source “how much I still have on hand”.
  3. The daemon’s sending cadence is the device side’s absolute clock (one packet every 20.3ms), fully decoupled from the speaker’s consumption cadence; the device side can only know “how much I have sent”, not “where it has played to”.

Corroborating evidence: the daemon source comment (from the v48R22 fix) states “sink 缓冲约 2s“. That was observed in an abnormal state (pushing the stream without START), but it indirectly confirms that this speaker’s buffer depth is on the order of seconds.

4. This round’s conclusion and decision

  • No code changes on the device side. Reason: the only remaining compressible amount on the device side is about 90ms (fifo water level 60→30ms, in-flight window 6→3), which is a 5% magnitude relative to 1~2s, with negligible benefit; and tightening the Bluetooth sending window carries a historical “CP reset” risk, making the risk/benefit ratio not worth it.
  • The fifo water-level loop already landed in the previous round (squeezing the backlog from 0.21s to 0.08s) is kept; it is an effective, side-effect-free improvement.
  • The feasible improvement direction is only on the speaker side: the speaker app / speaker unit’s “low latency / game mode” switch; or swapping in a Bluetooth speaker/headphones with lower latency for a comparison.

5. Verification

  • The user has confirmed: fixed lag, on the order of 1~2 seconds → fully consistent with the “speaker fixed buffer” model.
  • Comparison experiment (recommended for the user, one step to a conclusion): connect the device to another Bluetooth headphone/speaker; if the latency changes significantly → 100% confirmed to be on the speaker side; if it is still 1~2 seconds regardless of the swap → go back and check the chain.

6. Anti-patterns and pitfalls

  • ★ Do not use “device-side buffer metrics” to explain “second-order” latency — first make a latency budget table, see which magnitude does not add up, then dig into that segment. Guessing “it must be the buffer” by intuition will keep you spinning on the device side.
  • ★ Number-Completed ≠ application-layer consumption acknowledgment (see §3.1); using it to estimate the speaker buffer is wrong.
  • ★ Pay attention to the counting method when measuring: only differencing whole-file counts is meaningful; using “fixed-prefix counts” for differencing is necessarily 0 (a pit I dug for myself; it was really stepped on this round); log rotation can also pollute the difference.
  • ★ Using FIONREAD to measure fifo backlog is trustworthy: it returns the number of readable bytes inside the pipe, independent of the number of readers; reading only FIONREAD without read will not steal the consumer’s data.
  • ★ The frontend’s design of “stretching audio to real time” is correct: the core’s output varies with the actual frame rate, and the frontend normalizes by s_fpc × s_fps_meas and always outputs at 44100 frames per second, keeping audio and video content rate in sync (at the cost of pitch dropping with the frame rate). Stop doubting this part.

7. Related files

  • Device source: extern/miniretro/miniretro_gba.c, extern/miniretro/build.sh, /tmp/bt_user_daemon_v49.c
  • Upstream evidence: /home/GBAgame/mgba/src/platform/libretro/libretro.c (audio buffer lines 877910, retro_run delivery lines 618648)
  • Diagnostic scripts: ssh_tools/_tmp/{audio_probe,sample_audio,rate2,mgba_lr_read,delay_send}.sh
  • Related archives: bugfix_20260923_03 ~ _16
