entry.title: bluetooth
entry.content:
展讯 SC9832A 设备（HT0）蓝牙打通 —— AI 执行指导手册

读者对象：AI 助手（豆包 / 其他大模型），需在同类设备（展讯 SC9832A，安卓内核 + Alpine 用户态）上快速解决蓝牙不可用问题
使用方式：先读 §1–§3 建立上下文 → 按 §5 标准流程执行 → 按 §6 验证 → 遇故障查 §7 决策表
核心价值：本文所有事实均已实测验证；照着做最快 5 分钟确认底层是否通，避免重复数天踩坑

1. 设备与环境速览

项目值
设备型号HT0（对照机：H709，跑安卓 6.0，可作信息源）
主机名 / 内核spd-box / Linux 3.10.65 #13 SMP PREEMPT armv7l
系统组合保留安卓 6.0 内核 + switchroot 到 Alpine Linux（关键！）
SSHroot@<设备IP>（RNDIS 调试口，密码见环境记录）/ WiFi: <WiFi-IP>
无线芯片展讯 Marlin combo WCN（WiFi + 蓝牙同一颗芯片）
蓝牙 HCI/dev/ttyS0，3M 波特率 + CRTSCTS，H4 协议
蓝牙唤醒/proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite（写 1）
当前状态底层已打通，用户态 daemon + LVGL 蓝牙设置页已部署，开机自启

⚠️ 重启后 SSH 可能短暂不可达（USB 口切换），需轮询重试；/tmp 目录重启后保留（chroot 环境、工具都在）。

2. 已确认的硬事实（无需重新探查，直接信任）

  1. 蓝牙固件随 WiFi 一起下载：执行 chroot /tmp/aand /bin/download -i wlan0 时，combo 固件（含蓝牙部分）已整体烧入芯片 → WiFi 拉起 = 蓝牙固件已就绪，不需要单独烧蓝牙固件。
  2. pskey 已生效：download 读 /tmp/aand/etc/marlinba/connectivity_configure.ini 的 [SETCTION 6] 下发蓝牙 pskey；实测 Read Features 返回 ff ff 8d fe 与 pskey_bt.txt 的 feature_set 完全一致 → 不要纠结”缺 pskey”，不需要单独发。
  3. BT-OPEN 失败头号根因：chroot 内 /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* 权限 600 → chmod 666 /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* 后返回 WCNBTWIFI-CMD OK。重启后必做。
  4. btwrite 是 HCI 有响应的前提：蓝牙引擎省电休眠，必须周期性（1.5~2s）写 1 唤醒；缺它 → HCI 无响应或只回一次 SPRD3 身份帧。
  5. SPRD3 身份帧 = 引擎启动信号：55 7e 00 81 00 06 53 50 52 44 33 00 57 0a 7e（”SPRD3”=展讯标识），收到它说明 HCI 通道活了。
  6. 扫描前置：必须先发 Write Scan Enable（0x0c1a, 0x03）再发 Inquiry（GIAC 0x33 0x8b 0x9e），否则 Inquiry 被接受（CMD_STATUS 0x00）但永远无 Inquiry Result。
  7. 固件真实 MAC：11:22:14:31:93:27（探针响应值，不是伪造）。
  8. 波特率：固件 BT 初始化后 115200→3M；daemon 直接以 3M 打开 ttyS0。
  9. 已扫到设备样例：48:f1:ae:25:7e:48 class=5a420c（手机，BR/EDR）。
  10. 进程链：logdw → download(常驻) → wcnd → bt_once(BT-OPEN) → bt_wake.sh(btwrite) → bt_user_daemon(socket)。

3. 已验证死路（不要重试，浪费轮次）

路线结果原因
内核 hci_uart.ko 驱动hci0 能注册（DOWN INIT RUNNING）但 hciconfig up 超时、TX=03.10 安卓定制内核，tty_struct 偏移与驱动不匹配；Alpine gcc14.2 编老内核模块报 invalid module format
vhci 虚拟方案用户明令否决—
反复黑盒试引导命令序列不完整、状态不稳定引导协议需对照机抓包，且不影响扫描功能达成，不值得死磕
ps | grep 内嵌模式杀 daemon误杀执行命令的 shell 自身用 pkill -9 -x bt_user_daemon
/tmp/reset_tty 恢复 ldisc段错误用 python fcntl.ioctl(fd, 0x5421, b'\x00\x00\x00\x00')（TIOCSETD=0x5421, N_TTY=0）
杀掉 download “重启干净环境”破坏 WiFi/蓝牙固件状态，需整机重启恢复download 常驻勿杀

4. 系统模型：四层 + 每层验证标准

排查纪律：哪一层验证不过，就只在这一层及其上游找原因，不要跨层瞎试。

5. 标准执行流程（可直接复制）

5.1 确认环境

5.2 拉起 WiFi（蓝牙前提）

5.3 蓝牙上电 + 唤醒 + daemon

5.4 验证（设备端 python3，无 socat）

6. 验证标准清单（逐项确认）

#检查期望
1cat /sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1/device0x2331
2grep 'CMD OK' /tmp/bt_once.logpush(17): WCNBTWIFI-CMD OK
3/tmp/bt_probe_full 20六步全通（Reset/Ver/BD_ADDR/Buffer/Features/Scan Enable）
4cat /proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite 可写echo 1 > ... 返回 WRITE_OK
5socket stateOK ON
6socket scan 15OK N + 设备行（无设备则 N=0，不算失败）
7pgrep -x bt_user_daemon单实例
8LVGL 桌面”蓝牙”图标 → 开关/搜索/列表页面正常

7. 故障 → 根因 → 修复 决策表

症状大概率根因修复
BT-OPEN FAILmdbg 权限 600chmod 666 /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* 重试
HCI 无响应 / 只回一次 SPRD3缺 btwrite 唤醒启动 bt_wake.sh；确认 btwrite 可写
扫描无结果未先 Write Scan Enable用 daemon scan 命令（内部已处理）
socket connect 失败daemon 多实例抢 socketpkill -9 -x bt_user_daemon → 单实例重启
daemon 日志 “Not a tty”tty ldisc 被占python ioctl TIOCSETD=0x5421 恢复 N_TTY
WiFi/蓝牙一起没了download 被杀整机重启，按 §5.2 重拉
屏幕程序反复”变回旧版”watchdog/开机脚本指向 build 路径统一改为 /usr/local/bin/lvgl_demo（已做）
重启后 22 端口不通USB 口切换轮询重连（本机可复用 bt_auto_resume.py）

8. 用户态 daemon 架构（改动/维护必读）

协议（文本行，客户端 shutdown(SHUT_WR) 后读到 EOF）：

  • state → OK ON / OK OFF
  • on / off → 开关蓝牙（HCI Reset + Scan Enable 使能/关闭）
  • scan N → 扫描 N 秒，返回 OK <count> + 每行 bd_addr class rssi
  • list → 列出最近扫描结果
  • connect <bd> → 尝试连接（BR/EDR 对方未接受时返回 RC -2，属预期）

实现要点（重构时勿破坏）：

  • B3000000 + CRTSCTS，VMIN=1 阻塞读
  • 帧读取按 H4 帧头：buf[1]=evt、buf[2]=len，select 超时保护
  • 扫描流程固定为：Write Scan Enable(0x0c1a,0x03) → Inquiry(0x0401, 33 8b 9e) → 收 Inquiry Result
  • socket 0666，单实例（openrc command_background 管理）
  • 日志：/tmp/btud.log（stdout）、/tmp/btud_dbg.log（TX/RX hex）

9. 红线与运维纪律

  1. download 常驻勿杀 —— 全杀破坏固件状态，只能整机重启恢复。
  2. 驱动加载顺序：marlin_fm.ko 先、sprdwl.ko 后（符号依赖）。
  3. 杀进程：一律 pkill -9 -x <名字>，禁止 ps | grep 内嵌模式。
  4. 重启后必做：mdbg chmod 666（开机脚本已自动做，手动调试时别忘）。
  5. 蓝牙扫描时保持 btwrite 唤醒（bt_wake.sh 别停）。
  6. 不要动 USB OTG / 网络模式配置（用户明确约束）。
  7. 多实例打架 = 先 pkill 清干净再起，别在残留上叠加。

10. 设备上已有工具清单（复用，勿重造）

工具位置用途
bt_user_daemon/usr/local/bin/bt_user_daemon生产 daemon（已部署）
bt_probe_full/tmp/bt_probe_fullHCI 六步探针诊断
hci_3m/tmp/hci_3m3M 原始 HCI 测试
bt_once/tmp/bt_onceBT-OPEN 触发
bt_wake.sh/tmp/bt_wake.shbtwrite 周期唤醒
bt_daemon/etc/init.d/bt_daemonopenrc 自启（rc-update add default）
wifi.start/etc/local.d/wifi.start开机 WiFi + download 链
lvgl_demo/usr/local/bin/lvgl_demoLVGL 桌面（含蓝牙页，git 已提交）
pskey_bt.txt/mnt/android_sys/lib/modules/pskey_bt.txt蓝牙参数权威值
btud_dbg.log/tmp/btud_dbg.logdaemon TX/RX hex 日志

11. 后续增强方向（当前未完成）

项说明建议路径
真实配对/连接daemon connect 只在 BR/EDR 层测试过（RC -2 属预期）抓对照机 H709 蓝牙开启时 ttyS0 完整流量，重放初始化序列（含引导命令）
BLE 支持当前只验证 BR/EDR 扫描扩展 HCI LE 命令（LE Set Scan Parameters/Enable）
音频 A2DP无协议栈，暂不可用需引入 BlueZ 或轻量 A2DP 栈
daemon 连接状态持久化当前连接尝试不保存页面可加”已连接设备”状态展示

12. 5 分钟快速验收路径

以上两条通过 → 蓝牙底层 + 应用链路全部 OK，直接进入”增强方向”工作；不通过 → 按 §7 决策表逐项定位。

文档版本：v1.0（蓝牙打通后沉淀）
关联文档：操作手册（人用）、启动流程对比、工作过程总结

entry.title: WiFi打通_AI指导手册
entry.content:
展讯 SC9832A 设备（HT0）WiFi 打通 —— AI 执行指导手册

读者对象：AI 助手（豆包 / 其他大模型），需在同类设备（展讯 SC9832A，安卓内核 + Alpine 用户态）上快速解决 WiFi 不可用 / 无法连接问题
使用方式：先读 §1–§3 建立上下文 → 按 §5 标准流程执行 → 按 §6 验证 → 遇故障查 §7 决策表
核心价值：本文所有命令均取自设备上实测通过的 wifi.start 开机脚本；照着做可在同类设备上直接拉起 WiFi，避免重复踩坑
关联：WiFi 与蓝牙共用同一颗 Marlin combo 芯片，WiFi 是蓝牙的物理前提（见蓝牙 AI 指导手册）

1. 设备与环境速览

项目值
设备型号HT0（对照机：H709，跑安卓 6.0，可作信息源）
主机名 / 内核spd-box / Linux 3.10.65 #13 SMP PREEMPT armv7l
系统组合保留安卓 6.0 内核 + switchroot 到 Alpine Linux（关键！）
SSHroot@<设备IP>（RNDIS 调试口）/ WiFi 联网后 <WiFi-IP>
WiFi 芯片展讯 Marlin combo WCN（SC2331，WiFi+蓝牙同芯片，SDIO 接口）
WiFi 接口wlan0（驱动 sprdwl.ko + marlin_fm.ko）
固件下载安卓原版 download 二进制，在 chroot /tmp/aand 内运行
当前状态WiFi 已打通：download → 驱动 → wpa_supplicant → DHCP，开机脚本已固化

⚠️ 重启后 SSH 可能短暂不可达（USB 口切换），需轮询重试；/tmp 重启后保留（chroot 环境、工具都在）。

2. 已确认的硬事实（无需重新探查，直接信任）

  1. WiFi 固件必须由安卓原版 download 烧录：chroot /tmp/aand /bin/download -i wlan0，芯片才有固件可跑；WiFi 与蓝牙固件是一体的，WiFi 拉起 = 蓝牙固件也已就绪。
  2. download 依赖完整的 chroot 安卓用户态：/tmp/aand 内需有 Android 的 lib（含 libiwnpi.so）、/etc/marlinba/*.ini 配置、设备节点、分区软链（by-name: wcnfdl→mmcblk0p14、wcnmodem→mmcblk0p15、boot→mmcblk0p16）。这些 wifi.start 已自动搭建。
  3. SDIO 枚举是固件下载成功的标志：/sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1 出现且 device=0x2331。
  4. 驱动加载顺序硬约束：marlin_fm.ko 必须先于 sprdwl.ko（sprdwl 依赖 marlin_fm 导出的 fm_read 符号），反了报 Unknown symbol。
  5. download 必须常驻：全杀 download/logdw 会破坏芯片固件状态，只能整机重启恢复。
  6. wpa_supplicant 配置：/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.conf，ctrl_interface=/run/wpa_supplicant，update_config=1；LVGL 网络页通过 wpa_cli 与该配置交互。
  7. LVGL 网络设置页（lv_pages/network_page.c）：开关=ip link up/down，扫描=wpa_cli -i wlan0 scan + scan_results，连接=add_network→set_network→select_network→save_config→reconnect。
  8. 开机脚本已固化：/etc/local.d/wifi.start（幂等设计，已就绪步骤自动跳过），git 副本在 shell/wifi.start。
  9. DHCP：用 udhcpc -i wlan0（Alpine 默认）；若持续”获取中”，优先查 wpa 连接状态与驱动。
  10. 时间问题：设备 RTC 曾退回 2016 年，已用 hwclock/ntpd 修复并固化（/etc/local.d/time_sync.start 之类脚本），若日期错乱先修时间再排网络（证书/握手会受日期影响）。

3. 已验证死路（不要重试，浪费轮次）

路线结果原因
杀掉 download/logdw “干净重来”芯片固件状态被破坏，WiFi/蓝牙一起失效必须整机重启才能恢复；正确做法是让 wifi.start 幂等重跑
用主线 Linux 内核替换安卓内核未采用安卓内核含展讯专属定制（SDIO/电源/固件时序），主线内核无对应支持，风险极高
改 USB OTG / 网络模式用户明确禁止会破坏 RNDIS 调试口 / 网络拓扑
直接 insmod sprdwl.ko 不加载 marlin_fmUnknown symbol 加载失败模块符号依赖，顺序不能反
重启后 22 端口不通时反复重连同一 IP无效USB 口切换导致，需轮询双 IP 重试
手写自研 download 替代安卓原版高风险不采用固件下载时序（power_ctl 上电序列 + UART 握手 + SDIO 大块写入）是芯片保密协议，原版二进制最可靠

4. 系统模型：分层 + 每层验证标准

排查纪律：哪一层验证不过，只在这一层及其上游找原因。例：连不上 WiFi 先查 wpa_supplicant 状态（③），而不是去重烧固件（①）。

5. 标准执行流程（可直接复制）

5.1 完整链路（对应 wifi.start，建议直接依赖开机脚本幂等重跑）

5.2 手动分步（调试时用）

5.3 连接 WiFi（wpa_cli 交互，LVGL 网络页同款逻辑）

6. 验证标准清单（逐项确认）

#检查期望
1cat /sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1/device0x2331
2lsmod | grep sprdwlsprdwl + marlin_fm（依赖关系 1 sprdwl）
3ip -br link show wlan0UP
4iwconfig wlan0ESSID 已关联 / 无 ESSID 则未连
5pgrep -x wpa_supplicant进程存在
6wpa_cli -i wlan0 statuswpa_state=COMPLETED
7ip addr show wlan0 | grep 'inet '有 IPv4 地址
8ip route有 default via 网关
9LVGL 网络页开关/扫描/已保存/附近列表/连接均正常

7. 故障 → 根因 → 修复 决策表

症状大概率根因修复
日志 ERROR: SDIO not enumerated, download may have failed固件下载未完成（时序/权限/节点问题）看 /tmp/logdw.log 尾部；确认 /dev/power_ctl 可写、by-name 软链存在；重跑 wifi.start
日志 bind logdw failed: No such file or directorylogdw 未就位（/tmp/logdw 不存在或非可执行）ls -la /tmp/logdw；从 /mnt/android_sys/bin/ 重新拷贝
download started pid=（pid 空）download 进程没起来ps -eo pid,comm | grep download；chroot 环境是否完整
wlan0 不出现在驱动加载后驱动加载失败 / 芯片未枚举dmesg | tail；先确认 SDIO 0x2331；rmmod 重载
扫描为空wpa_supplicant 未起 / 接口未 uppgrep wpa_supplicant；ip link set wlan0 up；wpa_cli scan 后再 scan_results
连上但 IP 一直”获取中”DHCP 未跑 / wpa 未 COMPLETEDwpa_cli status 看 wpa_state；udhcpc -i wlan0 -q -n 手动跑
重启后 SSH 不通RNDIS 口未恢复 / IP 变化轮询 <设备IP> 与 ；等开机脚本跑完
日期 2016 年RTC 未同步hwclock -s / ntpd 同步，写入 /etc/local.d 开机脚本（已固化，勿重复）
WiFi 正常但蓝牙起不来蓝牙链未跑见蓝牙 AI 指导手册 §5（mdbg 权限 / wcnd / bt_once / btwrite）

8. 组件架构（改动/维护必读）

chroot 关键节点（download 依赖，缺失即 SDIO 枚举失败）：

  • /tmp/aand/bin/download（安卓原版）
  • /tmp/aand/lib/libiwnpi.so + 全套 Android lib
  • /tmp/aand/etc/marlinba/connectivity_configure.ini（固件路径/校准配置，也含蓝牙 pskey）
  • /tmp/aand/dev/block/platform/sdio_emmc/by-name/{wcnfdl→mmcblk0p14, wcnmodem→mmcblk0p15, boot→mmcblk0p16}
  • /dev/power_ctl（download 写入 SLEEP→POWER_ON→POWER_RST 上电序列）

LVGL 网络页（lv_pages/network_page.c，1677 行，WiFi 设置 UI 模板）：

  • 开关：ip link set wlan0 up/down + wpa_cli disconnect/reconnect
  • 扫描：wpa_cli scan → 定时 3s → wpa_cli scan_results → 解析 bssid/signal/flags/ssid
  • 连接：add_network / set_network（ssid/psk/key_mgmt/scan_ssid/priority）/ select_network / save_config
  • 已保存列表：wpa_cli list_networks

9. 红线与运维纪律

  1. download 常驻勿杀 —— 全杀破坏芯片固件状态，只能整机重启。
  2. 驱动顺序：marlin_fm.ko 先、sprdwl.ko 后。
  3. wifi.start 幂等 —— 想重来直接 sh /etc/local.d/wifi.start，它会先杀净再拉起，不要手动零散操作。
  4. 不要改 USB OTG / 网络模式配置（用户明确约束）。
  5. 不要换主线内核 —— 展讯专属定制（SDIO/电源/固件）依赖安卓内核。
  6. 日期必须正确 —— WiFi 握手/证书受系统时间影响，先修时间再排网络。
  7. **进程清理用 pkill -9 -x <名>**，勿用 ps | grep 内嵌模式（误杀自身 shell）。

10. 设备上已有工具/文件清单（复用，勿重造）

工具/文件位置用途
wifi.start/etc/local.d/wifi.start（git: shell/wifi.start）WiFi 开机自启 + 全链路（幂等）
启动日志/var/log/wifi_boot.logwifi.start 输出（排障首选）
download/tmp/aand/bin/download固件下载（chroot 内）
logdw/tmp/logdw固件下载日志守护
安卓用户态/mnt/android_sys（mmcblk0p17）Android system 只读挂载（库/配置源）
驱动/lib/modules/marlin_fm.ko、/lib/modules/sprdwl.koWiFi 驱动（设备预编译）
wpa 配置/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.confwpa_supplicant 配置（含已保存网络）
网络页lv_pages/network_page.c（LVGL 项目）WiFi 设置 UI（wpa_cli 交互模板）
DHCPudhcpc（Alpine 自带）获取 IP

11. 后续增强方向（当前未完成）

项说明建议路径
IPv4 稳定性部分场景 IPv6 有地址而 IPv4 未取到检查 wpa_state=COMPLETED 后立即 udhcpc，加 -n 重试与日志
自动重连策略掉线后仅靠 wpa_supplicant 自动重连可加网络页”断开重连”按钮与信号强度展示（scan_results signal 已有）
多网络优先级当前单 network 配置扩展 wpa_cli list_networks 管理 + 排序 UI
与蓝牙共存WiFi 常驻 + 蓝牙扫描并行共用 download/wcnd，实测无冲突，但可加互斥电源管理

12. 5 分钟快速验收路径

以上通过 → WiFi 底层 + 协议 + 网络全链路 OK；不通过 → 按 §7 决策表逐项定位。

文档版本：v1.0（WiFi 打通后沉淀）
关联文档：WiFi 操作手册（人用）、WiFi 启动流程对比、WiFi 工作过程总结、蓝牙打通 AI 指导手册

entry.title: WiFi芯片打通工作过程与思路总结
entry.content:
WiFi 芯片打通 —— 工作过程与思路总结

主题：从”Alpine 下 WiFi 完全失效”到”可扫描、可连接”的完整排查与解决过程复盘。
文档目标：记录我（执行者）的分析思路、逐步拆解、关键决策与原因，方便复盘和迁移到类似问题。
文档版本：v1.0　|　2026-09

1. 问题定义（先做对题目）

现象：

  • 设备 spd-box（SC9832A，Android 6 内核 3.10.65 + Alpine Linux 3.21 armhf）；
  • WiFi/蓝牙在 Android 下可用；
  • switchroot 后 WiFi 失效：dmesg 反复 SDIO dev not ready，GPIO94 READY 恒 0，内核枚举不到芯片。

**我做的第一件事是”界定问题边界”**：

  • 硬件坏了吗？→ 用户明确说 Android 下可用，且有一台同型号 H709 正常 → 排除硬件故障。
  • 内核错了吗？→ 内核还是 Android 3.10.65，没换 → 内核大概率不是根因。
  • 那差异只剩两个：根文件系统（用户态） 和 DTB/配置。

这个”先排除不可能项”的界定，让后续排查没有走弯路去重编内核或怀疑硬件。

2. 第一阶段：正面尝试（约 6 类方案全部失败）

在拿到对照机之前，我先尝试在 Alpine 里”手工模拟”上电，全部失败，记录如下：

#尝试方案结果失败原因（事后归因）
1手动 ioctl 组合（POWER_ON/POWER_RST 各种顺序）无效上电时序不是简单 ioctl 能复刻的，需完整状态机
2往 DTB 注入电源属性（vddwifipa/vddcon/always-on/runtime）无效属性本身不缺，缺的是”用户态驱动固件下载”这个动作
3GPIO 采样引导（跟踪引脚电平找时机）无效READY 恒 0 说明芯片根本没被激活
4/dev/mem mmap 直写寄存器无效寄存器级操作无法替代芯片引导协议
5设备上编内核模块（想加驱动逻辑）失败设备无 kernel build 目录，交叉编译链不可用
6p21（recovery）dtb 修改无效非活动分区，改了不生效

关键认知（为什么我停下来了）：

  • 失败 1-4 的共同点是”我在模仿一个我不知道完整细节的协议”；
  • 芯片的上电+固件下载是厂商私有协议，逆向它成本极高、成功率低；
  • 换思路：既然 Android 里有现成实现（download 服务），与其模仿，不如复用。

方法论一：遇到”协议未知”的问题，优先寻找”现成实现”而不是逆向协议。

3. 第二阶段：对照机取证（用事实代替猜测）

用户提出关键建议：有一台同型号、Android 正常的设备，可以做对照实验。这解决了”不知道正确行为是什么”的问题。

3.1 连接与取证

通过 WatchTools adb（AndroidWatch_ADB_ToolBox\adb\adb.exe）连接 H709（root=Magisk）：

拿到的事实：

项目值
分区映射boot=p16、wcnfdl=p14、wcnmodem=p15、system=p17、recovery=p21
boot 镜像boot_p16_android.img（20MB，ANDROID! 头，FDT @0xB71800）
原版 DTBandroid_orig.dtb（53,967 字节）
上电程序/system/bin/download + /system/lib/libiwnpi.so
固件分区wcnfdl（p14）、wcnmodem（p15）
用户态配置/etc/marlinba/*.ini

为什么这些是决定性的：

  • 分区映射告诉我”固件在哪、boot 在哪”；
  • download 二进制告诉我”Android 是怎么给芯片上电的”；
  • 原版 DTB 告诉我”硬件应该被怎么描述”。

方法论二：对照”已知正确的系统”取证，把猜测变成可验证的事实。取证要拿能跑的东西（二进制、固件、配置），不只是看日志。

3.2 关键决策：chroot 复用 Android 二进制

观察 Android 的架构后我判断：

  • download 服务的硬件操作（写 /dev/power_ctl、ttyS0 握手、SDIO 写固件）都通过内核驱动完成；
  • 它本身是普通 ELF，只要能加载进内存并找到设备节点/固件，就能驱动内核干活；
  • 它需要 Android 的库和 linker → 用 chroot 提供迷你 Android 文件系统即可。

于是方案定型：

方法论三：遇到”用户态组件依赖特定根文件系统”的问题，chroot 是低成本的隔离复用手段——不用改主系统，只搭最小依赖集。

4. 第三阶段：逐个击破 chroot 运行的障碍（strace 驱动）

chroot 后第一次运行 download 必然报错。我采用 strace 定位法（不猜，看系统调用）：

报错信号（strace 看到）根因修复
open("/dev/power_ctl") 失败chroot 内 /dev 是空的mount --bind /dev /tmp/aand/dev
open(...wcnfdl) 失败download 按 by-name 找固件分区建链接 wcnfdl → /dev/block/mmcblk0p14、wcnmodem → /dev/block/mmcblk0p15
缺 .so 库迷你环境不完整从 /mnt/android_sys/lib/ 复制全套 .so

关键突破点：mount --bind /dev 后，download 能打开内核节点；链接 wcnfdl/wcnmodem 后它能找到固件。跑通后 dmesg 出现决定性证据：

这一刻意味着：

  • 芯片被成功上电；
  • 固件被成功写入；
  • GPIO94 READY 拉高；
  • 内核枚举出 SDIO 从设备。

方法论四：用 strace 看”它到底在找什么”，每个 ENOENT 都是一条精确的修复指令。比读文档/猜配置高效得多。

5. 第四阶段：DTB 修正（消除隐性变量）

现象：download 跑通有时仍不稳定。进一步核查发现 p16 的 dtb 曾有被改过的痕迹（早期尝试注入电源属性）。

决策：直接用 Android 原版 DTB 覆盖 p16 中 dtb 段：

  • seek=20008（512B 块）对应 boot 内 dtb 的字节偏移 0x9C5000；
  • 换回原版后，电源/时钟描述与 Android 一致，消除 DTB 这一隐性变量。

为什么必须做：download 的上电时序设计时是对着 Android 原版 DTB 的电源模型来的；DTB 被改过之后，即使程序逻辑对，硬件描述也对不上。

方法论五：当”程序对但行为不对”时，检查环境描述层（DTB/配置文件）是否被改过。先恢复原厂基线，再谈优化。

6. 第五阶段：驱动与用户态 supplicant

芯片枚举成功 ≠ WiFi 可用，还要走完数据通路：

6.1 驱动加载（顺序敏感）

  • 顺序反了会报 Unknown symbol；
  • 成功后出现 wlan0（MAC a2:d2:f3:bf:8c:10）→ 驱动绑定成功。

6.2 wpa_supplicant（踩过坑的决策）

第一次尝试：直接在 Alpine chroot 里跑 Android 原版 wpa_supplicant 2.5：

  • 报 CANNOT LINK（缺库）→ 复制 /mnt/android_sys/lib/*.so 后仍 Aborted；
  • 根因：Android Bionic libc 与 glibc/musl 环境不兼容，linker 机制不同。

决策转向：不再复用 Android 的 supplicant，改用 Alpine armhf 原生包：

  • wpa_supplicant-2.10-r11.apk + libnl3.apk + pcsc-lite-libs-2.2.3-r1.apk；
  • Alpine 官方/镜像源当时不可用（证书/到期），从电脑端下载 apk 后 apk add --allow-untrusted 装到设备。

配置：

为什么这个分工合理：

  • 底层固件下载（厂商私有、内核相关）→ 复用 Android 二进制（chroot）；
  • 用户态 supplicant（标准网络协议、与 libc 相关）→ 用 Alpine 原生包。

方法论六：按”与内核/硬件的耦合度”切分复用边界——硬件私有的复用原厂，标准化的用新系统原生实现。两边都不硬凑。

6.3 扫描成功

至此 WiFi 芯片完全打通：上电 → 固件 → 枚举 → 驱动 → 扫描。

7. 时间线总览

阶段关键动作结果
界定问题排除硬件/内核，锁定用户态+DTB方向正确
正面尝试6 类手工模拟上电全部失败（私有协议不可模仿）
对照取证adb 连 H709，拿分区/固件/download/DTB拿到”正确行为的全套素材”
chroot 方案搭 /tmp/aand 迷你 Android 环境方案定型
strace 排障bind /dev + 固件链接 + 补库download 跑通，芯片枚举
DTB 修正恢复 Android 原版 dtb消除隐性变量
驱动marlin_fm.ko → sprdwl.kowlan0 出现
supplicantAlpine armhf 原生包扫描/连接可用
UI 层launcher 网络页接线用户在界面上可操作

8. 方法论沉淀（可迁移到其他板子/芯片）

  1. 先排除不可能项（硬件/内核/系统），再集中火力在真实差异层；
  2. 私有协议不要逆向，要复用——找原系统的现成实现（二进制/服务）；
  3. 对照机取证：同型号正常设备是”正确行为”的最权威来源，尽量拿能跑的素材；
  4. chroot 隔离复用：为第三方二进制搭最小依赖集，不污染主系统；
  5. strace 驱动排障：每个 open/ENOENT 都是精确修复指令，不靠猜；
  6. 恢复原厂基线：环境描述层（DTB/配置）被改过就先还原，再做新改动；
  7. 按耦合度切分复用边界：硬件私有的复用原厂，标准化的用原生实现；
  8. 单向依赖链思维：上电→固件→枚举→驱动→supplicant 逐级验证，每级有 dmesg/日志证据再进下一级。

9. 遗留事项与后续方向

  • 开机自启动固化：download 上电 + 驱动加载 + wpa_supplicant 已通过 local 脚本/模块配置固化（详见《操作手册》4.10）；
  • 蓝牙：SC2331 是 Combo 芯片，蓝牙同源同路，可参考同一套”chroot download + 驱动 + 用户态”流程打通（尚未展开）；
  • 连接稳定性：扫描已稳定，连接/漫游行为需实网长测；
  • UI 层：launcher 网络配置页已能扫描、显示列表、连接，后续可加”已保存网络管理、信号强度排序优化”。

本总结复盘了从”现象”到”根因”再到”解决方案”的完整链路。核心一句话：芯片没坏、内核没坏，坏在”Alpine 缺了 Android 的芯片初始化服务”——用 chroot 把这一步借回来，链路即通。

版权声明：本文为 whiteleibniz 原创文章（AI 协作整理），版权归 whiteleibniz 所有，转载请注明出处与原文链接：https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: WiFi芯片启动流程对比_Android_vs_Alpine
entry.content:
WiFi 芯片启动流程对比 —— Android 原生 vs Alpine Linux（该设备）

主题：Marlin SC2331 WiFi 芯片在 Android 6.0（出厂系统）与 Alpine Linux（switchroot 后）两种环境下的启动流程对比、原理差异，以及”如何在 Alpine 里复刻 Android 的启动序列”。
文档版本：v1.0　|　2026-09

1. 为什么对比这两者

  • 该设备出厂跑 Android 6.0，WiFi/蓝牙正常——说明硬件、固件、驱动本身没问题。
  • switchroot 到 Alpine Linux 3.21（保留 Android 内核 3.10.65）后，WiFi 彻底失效，内核枚举不出芯片。
  • 硬件没变、内核没变，变的只是根文件系统。差异必然出在用户态启动逻辑上。
  • 因此：把 Android 的启动流程和 Alpine 的启动流程逐环节对比，就能精确定位”Alpine 缺了什么”。

2. 硬件与芯片背景

项目说明
SoC展锐 SC9832A（四核 ARMv7，集成 WCN 子系统控制器）
WiFi/BT 芯片Marlin SC2331（Combo 芯片），SDIO 接口
内核枚举地址mmc2:8800:1，device 0x2331
关键引脚GPIO94 = 芯片 READY 信号（上电完成后拉高）
固件所在分区wcnfdl（p14）、wcnmodem（p15）
电源/下载控制节点/dev/power_ctl、/dev/download（由内核驱动创建）

SC2331 的典型特性：不先上电并下载固件，SDIO 总线上的从设备不会就绪，内核自然枚举不到。这是整条问题的物理根因。

3. Android 6.0 原生启动流程

Android 流程的三个要点：

  1. 上电+固件下载是”用户态服务”干的，不是内核开机自动完成的；
  2. 服务读取的固件、ini 配置、设备节点全在 Android 文件系统里；
  3. DTB 提供了正确的电源/时钟描述，download 服务才能把电上对。

4. Alpine Linux（switchroot 后）原生启动流程（失败态）

Alpine 失败态的三个缺口：

  1. 缺上电动作（无人写 /dev/power_ctl）；
  2. 缺固件下载（无人读 wcnfdl/wcnmodem 并写入芯片）；
  3. 缺正确的 DTB（部分尝试阶段 Alpine 侧 DTB 电源属性不完整）。

5. 逐环节对比表

环节Android 6.0（正常）Alpine（原始，失败）差异性质
内核3.10.65 Android 内核同一内核✅ 一致
设备树 DTBAndroid 原版（电源/时钟完整）初始为 Android 原版，中途有被改坏的风险⚠️ 需确保原版
SDIO 控制器驱动初始化初始化✅ 一致
power_ctl / download 节点注册注册✅ 一致
上电序列download 服务写 /dev/power_ctl无人执行❌ 核心缺口
固件下载download 服务读 wcnfdl/wcnmodem 刷入芯片无人执行❌ 核心缺口
ttyS0 芯片握手download 服务负责无人执行❌ 核心缺口
GPIO94 READY上电完成后拉高恒 0结果差异
SDIO 从设备枚举mmc2:8800:1（0x2331）不存在结果差异
WiFi 驱动sprdwl.ko + marlin_fm.ko存在但加载无效（芯片没起来）依赖前置
用户态配置Android wpa_supplicant需另装 Alpine 版 wpa_supplicant需要补齐
开机自启init.rc 常驻 downloadopenrc 无对应服务需要补齐

6. 原理分析：为什么 Alpine 不能直接工作

6.1 直接原因

SC2331 芯片上电不下载固件 = 不工作，而下载固件这件事在 Android 里由用户态常驻服务完成，不是内核自动行为。Alpine 只是换掉了用户态，没人做这件事。

6.2 深层原因（为什么不能简单”装个驱动”）

  • 驱动 sprdwl.ko 依赖芯片已枚举（mmc2:8800:1 存在）才能绑定；
  • 芯片枚举依赖固件已下载；
  • 固件下载依赖上电序列正确执行；
  • 上电序列依赖 DTB 电源描述 + /dev/power_ctl 可写 + Android 的 download 二进制及配套库/固件。

这就是一条单向依赖链，任何一环缺失都会让 WiFi 表现为”硬件坏了”。

6.3 为什么 Android 的 wpa_supplicant 不能直接用

曾尝试在 Alpine chroot 里直接跑 Android 的 wpa_supplicant 2.5：

  • 报 CANNOT LINK（缺库）→ 补了 /mnt/android_sys/lib/*.so 后仍 Aborted；
  • 原因：Android Bionic libc 与 glibc/musl 环境、linker 机制不兼容，二进制无法稳定运行。
  • 结论：用户态 supplicant 用 Alpine 原生包（armhf），只复用 Android 的底层固件下载逻辑。

7. 解决方案的原理：在 Alpine 里”借壳” Android

不重写上电逻辑，而是复用 Android 原版 download 二进制，给它搭一个最小运行环境：

为什么能成功：

  • 上电序列的硬件操作（写 power_ctl、ttyS0 握手、SDIO 写固件）是内核驱动的 ioctl/设备操作，与用户态 libc 无关；
  • download 二进制只要能找到设备节点、固件、ini，就能驱动内核完成整套动作；
  • 所以只要 chroot 环境文件齐全 + 设备节点 bind + 固件分区链接，Android 二进制在 Alpine 内核上可以原样工作。

原理上的分工总结：

层由谁负责在 Alpine 里如何获得
电源/时钟描述内核 + DTB用 Android 原版 DTB
上电时序Android download 用户态chroot 复用 Android 二进制
固件下载Android download 用户态chroot 复用 Android 二进制
芯片枚举内核（自动）前置完成后自动出现
WiFi 数据通路sprdwl.ko 驱动Alpine 内核模块（已备好）
扫描/连接wpa_supplicantAlpine armhf 原生包
开机自启openrc自定义 /etc/local.d 脚本

8. 一次完整的”理想启动时序”（打通后）

关键区别一句话：Android 靠 init.rc 常驻 download 服务完成芯片”初始化”；Alpine 用 chroot + local 脚本人工复刻了这一步，之后的一切（驱动、supplicant）都回到常规 Linux 流程。

对比结论：硬件与内核相同，差异集中在用户态”上电+固件下载”服务。复刻它，WiFi 即通。

entry.title: WiFi芯片打通操作手册
entry.content:
WiFi 芯片打通 —— 人工操作手册

适用设备：spd-box（SC9832A 四核，armv7l，Android 6 内核 3.10.65 + switchroot Alpine Linux 3.21 armhf）
WiFi 芯片：Marlin SC2331（SDIO 接口，mmc2:8800:1，device 0x2331）
文档目标：不依赖任何 AI 辅助，人工按本手册从零把该设备的板载 WiFi 打通到”可扫描、可连接”状态。
文档版本：v1.0　|　2026-09

目录

  1. 背景与问题定义
  2. 工具与物料清单
  3. 总体思路
  4. 操作流程
    • 4.1 设备与系统确认
    • 4.2 从 Android 对照机取证
    • 4.3 提取并替换 Android 原版设备树（DTB）
    • 4.4 搭建 Android 用户态 chroot 环境
    • 4.5 执行固件下载（download 上电序列）
    • 4.6 验证 SDIO 枚举
    • 4.7 加载 WiFi 驱动
    • 4.8 安装并配置 wpa_supplicant
    • 4.9 扫描验证
    • 4.10 开机自启动固化
  5. 故障排查速查表
  6. 注意事项与风险

1. 背景与问题定义

  • 设备出厂为 Android 6.0，WiFi/蓝牙在 Android 下完全可用（硬件无故障）。
  • 用户将该设备 switchroot 为 Alpine Linux（保留 Android 内核 3.10.65，仅替换根文件系统）。
  • 换到 Alpine 后 WiFi 完全不工作，典型现象：
    • dmesg 反复出现 SDIO dev not ready；
    • GPIO94（芯片 READY 引脚）恒为 0；
    • 内核从未枚举出 SDIO WiFi 设备（/sys/bus/sdio/devices/ 为空）。
  • 根因：SC2331 芯片的上电时序 + 固件下载由 Android 系统里的常驻 download 服务完成（写 /dev/power_ctl、/dev/download，并把 wcnfdl/wcnmodem 分区的固件刷进芯片）。Alpine 没有这套服务，芯片从未被”激活”。

2. 工具与物料清单

类别工具/物料用途备注
远程操作SSH 客户端（paramiko / PuTTY / OpenSSH）连接 Alpine 设备root@<设备IP>
对照取证WatchTools adb（AndroidWatch_ADB_ToolBox\adb\adb.exe）连接同型号 Android 机 H709需 root（Magisk）
分区读写dd、cat、ls提取/写入分区、设备节点设备内自带（BusyBox/coreutils）
系统跟踪strace定位 download 服务失败原因Alpine 用 apk add strace
固件文件download（Android 二进制）、libiwnpi.so、wcnfdl/wcnmodem 分区镜像上电 + 固件下载从 Android 系统提取
设备树android_orig.dtb（约 53,967 字节）替换 p16 分区中的 dtb从 Android boot 镜像提取
内核模块marlin_fm.ko、sprdwl.koWiFi 驱动放在 /lib/modules/
用户态wpa_supplicant + wpa_cli（v2.10-r11）扫描/连接Alpine armhf 包
依赖库libnl3、pcsc-lite-libswpa_supplicant 依赖Alpine armhf 包
辅助chroot、mount --bind运行 Android 二进制设备自带

3. 总体思路

一句话：芯片的上电与固件下载逻辑在 Android 用户态（download 服务）里，Alpine 缺它 → 把 Android 原版 download 二进制 + 固件 + 设备节点搬进 chroot，在 Alpine 里”借壳”跑完上电序列，让内核枚举出 SDIO 芯片，再加载驱动、配 wpa_supplicant。

链路分四段，缺一不可：

4. 操作流程

4.1 设备与系统确认

4.2 从 Android 对照机取证

需要一台同型号、Android 系统正常的设备（H709），WiFi/蓝牙都好的那台。

4.3 提取并替换 Android 原版设备树（DTB）

Android 原版 DTB 里含 WiFi 电源/时钟的正确描述。这是后续 download 能正常工作的前提之一。

4.3.1 电脑端：从 boot 镜像提取 DTB

4.3.2 设备端：写入 p16 分区

⚠️ 写入 boot 分区有风险，务必先做备份。若刷错可 dd 回备份。

4.4 搭建 Android 用户态 chroot 环境

目的：让 Android 原版 download 二进制能在 Alpine 里运行（它依赖 Android 的库、设备节点、分区链接）。

排错要点：strace 看到 open("/dev/power_ctl") 失败 → 确认 mount --bind /dev；看到 open(...wcnfdl) 失败 → 确认 by-name 链接。

4.5 执行固件下载（download 上电序列）

若固件下载失败（卡在握手/写入错误），检查：DTB 是否正确（回 4.3）、/dev/power_ctl 是否可写、固件分区是否为原版。

4.6 验证 SDIO 枚举

4.7 加载 WiFi 驱动

⚠️ 加载顺序不能反：sprdwl.ko 依赖 marlin_fm.ko 导出的符号（fm_read），反过来会报 Unknown symbol。

4.8 安装并配置 wpa_supplicant

Alpine 官方源若不可用，直接下载 armhf 的 apk 手动安装。

4.9 扫描验证

4.10 开机自启动固化

设备重启后，内核枚举、固件、驱动、wpa_supplicant 都要自动恢复。

5. 故障排查速查表

现象可能原因排查/修复
dmesg 一直 SDIO dev not ready芯片未上电/固件未下载确认跑过 download（4.5），看 /dev/power_ctl 是否可写
GPIO94 READY 恒 0上电序列没执行用 strace 跟踪 download 的 ioctl/write 是否报错
download 报 open 设备失败chroot 内缺设备节点mount --bind /dev /tmp/aand/dev
download 报找不到 wcnfdl/wcnmodem缺 by-name 链接ln -sf /dev/block/mmcblk0p14 .../wcnfdl
download 跑完但 SDIO 无枚举DTB 不对确认 p16 已是 Android 原版 dtb（4.3）
insmod sprdwl.ko 报 Unknown symbol模块加载顺序错先 insmod marlin_fm.ko
wlan0 不出现固件下载未完成就加载驱动等 dmesg 出现 mmc2:8800:1 再 insmod
wpa_cli scan 失败wpa_supplicant 未跑 / 接口未 upip link set wlan0 up + 确认 supplicant 进程
wpa_cli 找不到PATH 缺 /sbinexport PATH=$PATH:/sbin
重启后 WiFi 丢失未做自启动按 4.10 固化
拔插 USB 外设后 SSH 断设备 USB 口复用（网口/键盘）重插电脑 USB 并重启设备恢复

6. 注意事项与风险

  1. 刷 p16（boot）分区有变砖风险——必须先备份（/root/p16_boot_backup.img），刷错可回滚。
  2. USB 口复用：设备的 USB 口既做 SSH 网口又插外设。插入键盘/鼠标会断 SSH，需要拔掉外设、插回电脑 USB 并重启设备。
  3. 固件版本匹配：download 上电成功后，驱动和固件要来自同一 Android 版本，否则可能出现 wlan0 有接口但扫描失败。
  4. 模块路径：确认 marlin_fm.ko / sprdwl.ko 在 /lib/modules/ 且与内核 3.10.65 匹配（不匹配会 invalid module format）。
  5. wpa_supplicant 版本：设备 armhf，务必用 armhf 包；x86_64 包会报 Exec format error。
  6. dtb 偏移：写 p16 时 seek=20008（512 字节块）对应字节偏移 0x9C5000，不同固件可能不同，先解析 boot 镜像确认。

本手册基于实际打通过程整理，操作顺序不可颠倒，关键步骤（DTB → 上电 → 驱动 → supplicant）缺一不可。

版权声明：本文为 whiteleibniz 原创文章（AI 协作整理），版权归 whiteleibniz 所有，转载请注明出处与原文链接：https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: Bluetooth Boot Process: Android vs Alpine Comparison
entry.content:
Spreadtrum SC9832A Bluetooth Boot Process — Android vs Alpine (this device) Comparison

Hardware: Spreadtrum Marlin combo WCN chip (WiFi + Bluetooth on the same chip)
This device: retains the Android 6.0 kernel (3.10.65) + switchroot to Alpine Linux
Purpose: explain the complete Bluetooth flow from boot to usability, comparing the principle differences between native Android and the current Alpine approach

1. Chip Physical Architecture (shared by both systems)

  • SDIO: data channel (WiFi data and bulk Bluetooth firmware downloads both go through here)
  • UART ttyS0: Bluetooth HCI control channel (3M baud rate + hardware flow control CRTSCTS, H4 protocol)
  • btwrite node: /proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite — writing 1 wakes the Bluetooth engine (power-saving mode management)

2. Native Android 6.0 Bluetooth Boot Process

Key information on the Android side comes from the original machine’s init.board.rc / init.rc / ueventd.rc:

2.1 Boot Chain

2.2 Key Android Points

StageAndroid approach
Firmware downloaddownload runs oneshot at boot, reads connectivity_configure.ini (includes Bluetooth pskey [SETCTION 6]) + calibration, writes in bulk over SDIO
Power-on controlwcnd (BT-OPEN command triggers Bluetooth subsystem power-on)
Wake-up managementlibbt-vendor periodically wakes with btwrite (H709 log: writes 1 every 30s → 1.5s → writes 2)
HCI channeltraditionally hciattach uses /dev/sttybt0 sprd_shark; this machine actually relies on libbt-vendor managing the UART directly (uart_conf controls the baud rate)
Protocol stackBluedroid (bluetooth.default.so + libbt-vendor.so)
User toolsBluetoothCtrl (Spreadtrum custom Bluetooth control)
Nodes/permissionsinit.board.rc does unified chmod/chown at boot

3. Alpine (this device) Bluetooth Boot Process

3.1 Boot Chain (currently hardened)

3.2 Key Alpine Points

StageAlpine approach
Firmware downloadreuses the original Android download, running inside the chroot /tmp/aand (depends on Android libraries/nodes/partition symlinks), with the parameter -i wlan0 (WiFi mode; the Bluetooth firmware is downloaded together with the combo)
Power-on controlreuses the original Android wcnd (inside chroot) + bt_once to trigger BT-OPEN
Wake-up managementself-written /tmp/bt_wake.sh writes btwrite=1 every 1.5~2s (more frequent than Android’s 30s, ensuring stable HCI response)
HCI channelself-written userland daemon opens /dev/ttyS0 directly (3M+CRTSCTS, H4), not depending on the kernel hci_uart driver
Protocol stackno Bluedroid; the daemon implements a minimal HCI command set (Reset/Version/BD_ADDR/Features/Scan)
User toolsLVGL Bluetooth settings page (communicates with the daemon via unix socket)
Nodes/permissionsboot script chmod 666 mdbg + bt_daemon openrc management

4. Stage-by-Stage Comparison Table

Comparison itemNative Android 6.0Alpine (this device)Reason for the difference
Firmware downloaddownload (oneshot, system user)download (chroot, resident)Alpine has no Android init; the process must be kept alive to prevent the chip from losing firmware
Firmware sourcepartitions wcnfdl/wcnmodemsame partitions (by-name symlinks into the chroot)same kernel, partition layout unchanged
pskey deliverylibbt-vendor sends VSC at initializationdelivered via connectivity_configure.ini when download runsthe firmware already received the pskey during the download phase (feature_set verified live)
BT power-onwcnd + BT-OPEN (triggered by init)wcnd (chroot) + bt_oncereuses the original; only the executor differs
Wake-uplibbt-vendor btwrite every 30sbt_wake.sh btwrite every 1.5~2sno libbt-vendor in userland; a more frequent self-written wake-up ensures no missed responses
HCI channellibbt-vendor manages the UART directlyself-written daemon reads /dev/ttyS0 directlyboth bypass the kernel protocol stack and operate the serial port directly
Kernel driverno hci_uart (vendor manages directly)tried hci_uart.ko → abandoned (TX=0)the 3.10 kernel’s tty_struct offsets do not match the newer driver
Protocol stackBluedroid (complete stack)no protocol stack; the daemon is HCI layer onlyAlpine has no Bluedroid; the LVGL application layer consumes HCI scan results directly
Scan implementationBluedroid Inquirydaemon Inquiry + Write Scan Enable firstSpreadtrum firmware behavior: without enabling scan first, no Inquiry Result is returned
Management toolBluetoothCtrlLVGL Bluetooth settings page (socket)custom UI for desktop applications
Baud rate115200 → 3M (switched by uart_conf)opens ttyS0 directly at 3Mthe firmware switches to 3M after BT initialization; the daemon always uses 3M

5. Key Principles (why it works)

  1. The same combo chip has WiFi+BT combined firmware — when download downloads with -i wlan0, the Bluetooth firmware portion has already entered the chip along with the combo image; therefore “after WiFi is up, the Bluetooth firmware is ready”, and only power-on + wake-up + HCI communication are needed afterwards; there is no need to burn the Bluetooth firmware separately.

  2. The SPRD3 identity frame is the engine start signal — after wake-up the firmware returns 55 7e 00 81 00 06 53 50 52 44 33 00 57 0a 7e (“SPRD3” = Spreadtrum chip identifier), indicating the Bluetooth engine is running and the HCI channel is alive; only after this can standard HCI commands be sent.

  3. btwrite is the power-saving switch — the Bluetooth engine enters low power when idle, so 1 must be written periodically to wake it; without this step, HCI commands sent out get no response (one of the common root causes of all early test failures).

  4. Write Scan Enable is the prerequisite for scanning — the Spreadtrum firmware requires sending 0x0c1a (0x03) first to enable scan, and only then will Inquiry return the Inquiry Result event; a bare Inquiry is accepted (CMD_STATUS 0x00) but results never come.

  5. Userland approach vs kernel driver — this device’s kernel is a custom Android 3.10.65; the tty_struct internal layout that hci_uart.ko depends on is inconsistent with mainline, and the hardcoded offsets cause TX=0 and up timeouts. Reading/writing /dev/ttyS0 directly from userland bypasses the kernel protocol stack and is instead the most reliable (the Android vendor did exactly this).

6. One-Sentence Summary

Android: init → download → wcnd/BT-OPEN → libbt-vendor (btwrite wake-up + pskey + HCI) → Bluedroid → BluetoothCtrl
Alpine (this device): boot scripts → chroot download (WiFi mode, combo firmware downloaded together) → wcnd/bt_once → bt_wake.sh (btwrite) → self-written userland daemon (H4 HCI) → LVGL Bluetooth settings page

The underlying hardware chain is exactly the same; the difference lies only in “who executes it”: Android relies on init + a complete protocol stack, while this device relies on boot scripts + a self-written userland daemon, replacing that entire set of Android dependencies with a minimal implementation.

Copyright: This article is an original work by whiteleibniz (organized with AI assistance). All rights reserved. Please credit the source and keep the original link: https://whiteleibniz.github.io

entry.title: Bluetooth Bring-up: Work Process Summary
entry.content:
Spreadtrum SC9832A Bluetooth Bring-up — Work Process Summary

Records the complete analysis path, key decisions, failed routes, and final solution from “Bluetooth unusable” to “LVGL Bluetooth settings page usable”
Timeline: after the WiFi bring-up, the Bluetooth effort lasted several days and ultimately concluded with the userland approach

1. Task Background and Initial Goals

The device is a Spreadtrum SC9832A tablet with “the Android 6.0 kernel (3.10.65) retained + switchroot to Alpine Linux”; WiFi was already up (download → insmod drivers → wpa_supplicant → udhcpc, with the boot script hardened). The user’s goal:

Add a “Bluetooth settings” app to the LVGL launcher, with the same features as the WiFi settings: on/off + search list + connect.
The user gave full authority: “Open up all permissions, use your most reasonable approach, I only look at results, and even a self-written userland program is fine.”

2. Analytical Framework: First Split “Bluetooth” into Four Layers

Before starting, establish a mental model first — for Bluetooth to work, all four layers must be connected:

Each layer has a clear “pass criterion”; if a layer fails, investigate the next layer, avoiding wasted time at the wrong level.

3. The Effort Process (by timeline)

Stage A: BT-OPEN failure investigation — discovering the mdbg permission root cause

Symptom: after bringing things up per the WiFi flow, bt_once sending BT-OPEN keeps returning FAIL.

Investigation:

  1. Compared with the successful WiFi path: WiFi does not depend on BT-OPEN (after download, drivers load directly), but Bluetooth must power on via BT-OPEN
  2. strace wcnd and observe what it accesses during BT-OPEN → points to /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/*
  3. Inspection found the mdbg node permissions inside the chroot are 600, so wcnd, running as the system user, cannot read them

Fix: chmod 666 /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* → BT-OPEN returns WCNBTWIFI-CMD OK

Lesson: the Android userland inside the chroot needs to access proc nodes; the permission model (600) is the easiest pitfall after porting.

Stage B: HCI channel verification — confirming the firmware is alive

Method: without depending on any driver, open /dev/ttyS0 directly from userland and send an HCI Reset.

Result: hci_3m (3M + CRTSCTS) received the firmware response 04 0e 04 01 03 0c 00 — the firmware HCI channel is completely normal.

Significance: proves the chip, firmware, and UART are all OK, and the problem lies only in how the upper layers hook in.

Stage C: Kernel driver route — tried then abandoned (important decision)

Attempt:

  • Loaded the device’s bundled precompiled hci_uart.ko + custom attach → hci0 registers (DOWN INIT RUNNING)
  • hciconfig hci0 up times out, TX=0

Root cause analysis: this kernel is a custom Android 3.10.65; the tty_struct offsets hardcoded inside hci_uart.ko do not match this kernel → data cannot be sent out.

  • Alpine gcc 14.2 compiling the old 3.10 kernel module → insmod invalid module format (symbol/signature mismatch)

Decision: abandon the kernel driver route. Reasons:

  1. The kernel module can only use the existing precompiled version on the device; it cannot be modified
  2. The user rejected the vhci virtual approach (“Stop using virtualization”)
  3. The original Android vendor never used the kernel hci_uart — libbt-vendor operates the UART directly, so the userland approach is the “orthodox” one

Stage D: Birth of the userland daemon (v1 → v4 iterations)

Approach: write a C daemon, going H4 directly on /dev/ttyS0 at 3M+CRTSCTS, serving externally over a unix socket.

Bugs stepped on during iteration (each a real lesson):

VersionProblemFix
v1compile failuremissing <stdint.h> / <sys/stat.h>
v2frame read truncation (non-blocking read n=7)changed to blocking read (VMIN=1) + select timeout, reading the full length per the H4 frame header (buf[1]=evt, buf[2]=len)
v3multiple instances fighting, socket connect droppingclean up with pkill -9 -x bt_user_daemon (do not use the ps|grep inline pattern, which kills the shell itself)
v4Inquiry Result not received when scanningsee Stage F

Stage E: btwrite wake-up — the final kick to get HCI through

Symptom: HCI Reset gets a response, but after sending standard commands the firmware goes silent.

Investigation:

  • Disassembled the device’s original bt_vendor.default.so; strings confirm the complete flow: btwrite wake-up → connect to wcnd (BT-OPEN) → read uart_conf → send pskey → HCI
  • Discovered that /proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite exists and is writable (previously misjudged as “the kernel has no such driver”)
  • The H709 reference machine’s log shows Bluetooth writes 1 with btwrite every 30s periodically

Fix: echo 1 > /proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite → HCI responds immediately! The firmware returns the SPRD3 identity frame (55 7e ... 53 50 52 44 33 ...)
→ self-write /tmp/bt_wake.sh to wake every 1.5~2s (more frequent than Android’s 30s, ensuring no missed responses during scanning)

Key insight: the Bluetooth engine has a power-saving mode; wake-up is a continuous, periodic action, not a one-time thing.

Stage F: Root cause of scan failure — Write Scan Enable must come first

Symptom: Inquiry is accepted (CMD_STATUS 0x00) but an Inquiry Result never arrives.

Investigation: compared probe rounds — the round that scanned devices had done Write Scan Enable.

Fix: send Write Scan Enable 0x0c1a (0x03) before scanning → Inquiry Result returns stably immediately
Live test: OK 1 / 48:f1:ae:25:7e:48 5a420c 0 (a real phone was scanned)

This is a hidden requirement of the Spreadtrum firmware: without enabling scan first, Inquiry simply “sinks like a stone”.

Stage G: The pskey mystery — clarified rather than ground on

Question: the Android libbt-vendor must send pskey before the firmware is ready; am I missing this?

Conclusion (decisive evidence):

  • the [SETCTION 6] section of connectivity_configure.ini is the Bluetooth pskey structure (pskey_cmd=0x001C0101, device_addr, UART0 HCI configuration)
  • download reads this file → the pskey was already delivered during the firmware download phase
  • the measured Read Features returns ff ff 8d fe, exactly matching the feature_set in pskey_bt.txt → the pskey is already in effect

Decision: no need to send pskey separately, avoiding wasted time on a non-question.

Stage H: Protocol frame details — SLIP and the SPRD3 boot frame

Symptom: standard H4 raw frames sometimes get no response, and the firmware returns 7e 00 8b 00 00 cb ab 7e (a bootloader state error frame).

Analysis:

  • Frame format confirmed: 7e <type:2B> <len:2B> <data> <crc16> 7e (same as the download protocol)
  • CRC decoded: XMODEM (0x1021/init 0), stored little-endian
  • The firmware steadily returning the SPRD3 identity frame = the engine is in a boot loop, waiting for a specific initialization sequence

Decision: black-box boot command trials are incomplete; the most reliable approach is to capture and replay the complete ttyS0 traffic when the reference machine (H709) enables Bluetooth. The user assisted by using WatchTools ADB to connect to the reference machine and collect Android-side information (init.rc, ueventd.rc, pskey_bt.txt, bt_vendor library) — after confirming the approach is viable, stop grinding on the boot sequence, because:

  1. Standard HCI commands (Reset/Version/BD_ADDR/Features/Scan) all respond already
  2. The scan function is through → the application-layer goal (search list) is satisfied
  3. The boot sequence only affects the complete initialization of “pairing/connection”, which is a future enhancement

Stage I: Hardening boot auto-start

  • openrc /etc/init.d/bt_daemon (command_background=yes), rc-update add default
  • Together with wifi.start (resident download) + lvgl_demo.start, forms the complete boot chain
  • Live test after reboot: SDIO 0x2331, wcnd/bt_once/logdw/download/bt_wake all running, daemon single instance

Stage J: LVGL Bluetooth settings page

  • Written bluetooth_page.c/h following the verified network_page.c (WiFi template)
  • Launcher registered in three places: enum + s_apps array + open_app switch (LV_SYMBOL_BLUETOOTH exists)
  • daemon text protocol: state/on/off/scan/list/connect
  • Fixed a deployment path issue: the boot script and watchdog originally pointed to build/lvgl_demo (the old version); changed uniformly to /usr/local/bin/lvgl_demo

4. Key Decisions Review (why it is done this way)

Decision pointChoiceReason
Kernel driver vs userlanduserlandkernel 3.10 offsets do not match (TX=0); the original Android vendor manages the UART directly in userland; the user rejected vhci
Self-written daemon vs porting Bluedroidself-written minimal daemonAlpine lacks the Bluedroid dependency chain (libraries/property service/HAL); the porting cost is far higher than writing the HCI layer yourself
Reusing the original Android download/wcndreuse (chroot)the firmware download/power-on sequence is the chip’s closely guarded timing; the original binaries are the most reliable; self-writing download is high-risk, low-reward
Whether to send pskey separatelydo not sendthe evidence chain is complete: download already delivered it (configure.ini) + Read Features confirms it is in effect
Black-box boot sequence vs reference machine packet capturestop once viability is confirmedthe application goal (scan list) is achieved; the boot sequence is a pairing enhancement and does not block the main line
Wake-up period 1.5~2smore frequent than Android’s 30sthe userland has no power-saving coordination of a complete protocol stack; frequent wake-ups ensure stable HCI responses

5. Final Results and Distillation

6. Lessons Learned (reusable for other modules)

  1. Layer first, then localize — each layer has a clear pass criterion (BT-OPEN OK / HCI Reset response / SPRD3 / Inquiry Result); do not skip layers and try blindly.
  2. Permission problems are the number one pitfall in porting — proc node 600 permissions inside the chroot caused the BT-OPEN failure; chmod 666 solved it in a minute, whereas hours might have been wasted before.
  3. The reference machine is a goldmine — the original Android init.rc / ueventd.rc / pskey_bt.txt / bt_vendor library provided the complete truth of the flow; disassembly + string extraction turned “not knowing how to do it” into “just follow it”.
  4. Understand vendor firmware behavior — Write Scan Enable coming first is a hidden requirement of the Spreadtrum firmware; this kind of “does not work unless stated” behavior can only be discovered through comparison experiments.
  5. Do not get stuck on dead ends — abandoned the kernel driver’s TX=0 decisively; when black-box boot sequences are incomplete, stop grinding, and after evaluating “current results already satisfy the user’s goal”, stop and put energy into the application layer.
  6. Process hygiene — multiple instances fighting over the socket, ps|grep killing itself, the watchdog auto-starting the old path — these “operational details” repeatedly create the illusion of “it was fixed but it reverted”.

entry.title: Bluetooth Bring-up: AI Guidance Manual
entry.content:
Spreadtrum SC9832A Device (HT0) Bluetooth Bring-up — AI Execution Guidance Manual

Intended audience: AI assistants (Doubao / other large models) that need to quickly resolve Bluetooth unavailability on similar devices (Spreadtrum SC9832A, Android kernel + Alpine userland)
How to use: first read §1–§3 to build context → execute per the standard flow in §5 → verify per §6 → consult the decision table in §7 when problems occur
Core value: all facts in this article have been verified by live testing; following it confirms whether the lower layers are connected in as little as 5 minutes, avoiding days of repeated pitfall-hitting

1. Device and Environment at a Glance

ItemValue
Device modelHT0 (reference machine: H709, running Android 6.0, usable as an information source)
Hostname / kernelspd-box / Linux 3.10.65 #13 SMP PREEMPT armv7l
System combinationretains the Android 6.0 kernel + switchroot to Alpine Linux (critical!)
SSHroot@<设备IP> (RNDIS debug port, password in the environment record) / WiFi: <WiFi-IP>
Wireless chipSpreadtrum Marlin combo WCN (WiFi + Bluetooth on the same chip)
Bluetooth HCI/dev/ttyS0, 3M baud rate + CRTSCTS, H4 protocol
Bluetooth wake-up/proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite (write 1)
Current statelower layers are up; the userland daemon + LVGL Bluetooth settings page are deployed, with boot auto-start

⚠️ After reboot, SSH may be briefly unreachable (USB port switching); polling retries are needed. The /tmp directory survives reboot (the chroot environment and tools are all there).

2. Confirmed Hard Facts (no need to re-investigate; trust directly)

  1. Bluetooth firmware is downloaded together with WiFi: when chroot /tmp/aand /bin/download -i wlan0 runs, the combo firmware (including the Bluetooth part) has already been burned into the chip as a whole → WiFi up = Bluetooth firmware ready; there is no need to burn the Bluetooth firmware separately.
  2. pskey is already in effect: download reads the [SETCTION 6] section of /tmp/aand/etc/marlinba/connectivity_configure.ini to deliver the Bluetooth pskey; the measured Read Features returns ff ff 8d fe, exactly matching the feature_set in pskey_bt.txt → do not fuss over “missing pskey”; it does not need to be sent separately.
  3. Number one root cause of BT-OPEN failure: permissions 600 on /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* inside the chroot → after chmod 666 /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* it returns WCNBTWIFI-CMD OK. This must be done after every reboot.
  4. btwrite is the prerequisite for HCI responses: the Bluetooth engine sleeps to save power, so 1 must be written periodically (1.5~2s) to wake it; without it → no HCI response, or only a single SPRD3 identity frame in reply.
  5. SPRD3 identity frame = engine start signal: 55 7e 00 81 00 06 53 50 52 44 33 00 57 0a 7e (“SPRD3” = Spreadtrum identifier); receiving it means the HCI channel is alive.
  6. Scanning prerequisite: you must first send Write Scan Enable (0x0c1a, 0x03) before Inquiry (GIAC 0x33 0x8b 0x9e); otherwise Inquiry is accepted (CMD_STATUS 0x00) but never returns an Inquiry Result.
  7. Firmware real MAC: 11:22:14:31:93:27 (probe response value, not spoofed).
  8. Baud rate: after firmware BT initialization, 115200→3M; the daemon opens ttyS0 directly at 3M.
  9. Sample scanned device: 48:f1:ae:25:7e:48 class=5a420c (phone, BR/EDR).
  10. Process chain: logdw → download(resident) → wcnd → bt_once(BT-OPEN) → bt_wake.sh(btwrite) → bt_user_daemon(socket).

3. Verified Dead Ends (do not retry; it wastes turns)

RouteResultReason
Kernel hci_uart.ko driverhci0 registers (DOWN INIT RUNNING) but hciconfig up times out, TX=0custom Android 3.10 kernel; tty_struct offsets do not match the driver; Alpine gcc14.2 building the old kernel module reports invalid module format
vhci virtual approachexplicitly rejected by the user—
Repeatedly trying boot command sequences black-boxincomplete, unstable statethe boot protocol needs packet capture from a reference machine, and it does not affect achieving the scan function; not worth grinding on
ps | grep inline pattern to kill the daemonaccidentally kills the shell executing the command itselfuse pkill -9 -x bt_user_daemon
/tmp/reset_tty to restore ldiscsegmentation faultuse python fcntl.ioctl(fd, 0x5421, b'\x00\x00\x00\x00') (TIOCSETD=0x5421, N_TTY=0)
Killing download to “restart a clean environment”breaks WiFi/Bluetooth firmware state; requires a full machine reboot to recoverdownload is resident — do not kill it

4. System Model: Four Layers + a Pass Criterion per Layer

Troubleshooting discipline: whichever layer fails verification, look for the cause only in that layer and its upstream; do not skip layers and try blindly.

5. Standard Execution Flow (directly copyable)

5.1 Confirm the environment

5.2 Bring up WiFi (Bluetooth prerequisite)

5.3 Bluetooth power-on + wake-up + daemon

5.4 Verify (python3 on the device, no socat)

6. Verification Checklist (confirm item by item)

#CheckExpected
1cat /sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1/device0x2331
2grep 'CMD OK' /tmp/bt_once.logpush(17): WCNBTWIFI-CMD OK
3/tmp/bt_probe_full 20all six steps pass (Reset/Ver/BD_ADDR/Buffer/Features/Scan Enable)
4cat /proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite writableecho 1 > ... returns WRITE_OK
5socket stateOK ON
6socket scan 15OK N + device lines (N=0 if no devices, not a failure)
7pgrep -x bt_user_daemonsingle instance
8LVGL desktop “Bluetooth” icon → on/off/search/listpage works normally

7. Fault → Root Cause → Fix Decision Table

SymptomMost likely root causeFix
BT-OPEN FAILmdbg permissions 600chmod 666 /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* and retry
No HCI response / only a single SPRD3 replymissing btwrite wake-upstart bt_wake.sh; confirm btwrite is writable
No scan resultsWrite Scan Enable not sent firstuse the daemon scan command (handled internally)
socket connect failuredaemon multiple instances fighting over the socketpkill -9 -x bt_user_daemon → restart as a single instance
daemon log “Not a tty”tty ldisc occupiedpython ioctl TIOCSETD=0x5421 to restore N_TTY
WiFi/Bluetooth both gonedownload was killedfull machine reboot, re-bring-up per §5.2
Screen program repeatedly “reverts to the old version”watchdog/boot script points to the build pathchange uniformly to /usr/local/bin/lvgl_demo (already done)
Port 22 unreachable after rebootUSB port switchingpoll and reconnect (bt_auto_resume.py is reusable on the local machine)

8. Userland Daemon Architecture (required reading for modifications/maintenance)

Protocol (text lines; the client reads until EOF after shutdown(SHUT_WR)):

  • state → OK ON / OK OFF
  • on / off → toggle Bluetooth (HCI Reset + Scan Enable enable/disable)
  • scan N → scan for N seconds, returns OK <count> + one line per device bd_addr class rssi
  • list → list the most recent scan results
  • connect <bd> → attempt to connect (returns RC -2 when the BR/EDR peer does not accept, which is expected)

Implementation points (do not break these when refactoring):

  • B3000000 + CRTSCTS, VMIN=1 blocking read
  • frame reading per the H4 frame header: buf[1]=evt, buf[2]=len, with select timeout protection
  • the scan flow is fixed as: Write Scan Enable(0x0c1a,0x03) → Inquiry(0x0401, 33 8b 9e) → receive Inquiry Result
  • socket 0666, single instance (managed by openrc command_background)
  • logs: /tmp/btud.log (stdout), /tmp/btud_dbg.log (TX/RX hex)

9. Red Lines and Operational Discipline

  1. download is resident — do not kill it — killing everything breaks firmware state; recovery is only possible with a full machine reboot.
  2. Driver load order: marlin_fm.ko first, sprdwl.ko second (symbol dependency).
  3. Killing processes: always pkill -9 -x <name>; the ps | grep inline pattern is forbidden.
  4. Must-do after reboot: mdbg chmod 666 (already automated in the boot script; do not forget during manual debugging).
  5. Keep the btwrite wake-up active during Bluetooth scanning (do not stop bt_wake.sh).
  6. Do not touch USB OTG / network mode configuration (explicit user constraint).
  7. Multiple instances fighting = pkill clean first, then start; do not stack on top of leftovers.

10. Existing Tools Inventory on the Device (reuse; do not reinvent)

ToolLocationPurpose
bt_user_daemon/usr/local/bin/bt_user_daemonproduction daemon (already deployed)
bt_probe_full/tmp/bt_probe_fullHCI six-step probe diagnostics
hci_3m/tmp/hci_3m3M raw HCI test
bt_once/tmp/bt_onceBT-OPEN trigger
bt_wake.sh/tmp/bt_wake.shperiodic btwrite wake-up
bt_daemon/etc/init.d/bt_daemonopenrc auto-start (rc-update add default)
wifi.start/etc/local.d/wifi.startboot WiFi + download chain
lvgl_demo/usr/local/bin/lvgl_demoLVGL desktop (includes the Bluetooth page; committed to git)
pskey_bt.txt/mnt/android_sys/lib/modules/pskey_bt.txtauthoritative values of Bluetooth parameters
btud_dbg.log/tmp/btud_dbg.logdaemon TX/RX hex log

11. Future Enhancement Directions (currently incomplete)

ItemDescriptionSuggested path
Real pairing/connectionthe daemon connect has only been tested at the BR/EDR layer (RC -2 is expected)capture the complete ttyS0 traffic when the reference machine H709 enables Bluetooth, and replay the initialization sequence (including boot commands)
BLE supportonly BR/EDR scanning is verified so farextend the HCI LE commands (LE Set Scan Parameters/Enable)
Audio A2DPno protocol stack, temporarily unavailableneeds to introduce BlueZ or a lightweight A2DP stack
daemon connection state persistencecurrent connection attempts are not savedthe page can add a “connected devices” status display

12. 5-Minute Quick Acceptance Path

Both commands above pass → the entire Bluetooth lower layer + application chain is OK; proceed directly to the “enhancement directions” work. If they do not pass → localize item by item per the decision table in §7.

Document version: v1.0 (distilled after the Bluetooth bring-up)
Related documents: operation manual (for humans), boot process comparison, work process summary

entry.title: Bluetooth Chip Bring-up: Operation Manual
entry.content:
Spreadtrum SC9832A Bluetooth Chip Bring-up — Manual Operation Manual

Scope: Spreadtrum SC9832A devices retaining the Android kernel + switchroot to Alpine Linux (hostname spd-box, kernel Linux 3.10.65)
Purpose: without relying on an AI assistant, manually bring up the Bluetooth lower layers, verify the HCI channel, deploy the userland daemon, and set up boot auto-start
All commands in this article have been verified on the device

0. Prerequisite Concepts (building intuition in 30 seconds)

This device’s WiFi and Bluetooth are the same Spreadtrum Marlin combo chip (WCN); SDIO carries the data channel, and UART (ttyS0) carries the Bluetooth HCI control channel. The chip firmware does not “reside” in the system; at every boot, the original Android download bootloader must burn the firmware into the chip before the chip can work.

RoleFile/processWhat it does
Firmware burning/tmp/aand/bin/download (chroot Android environment)burns the wcnfdl/wcnmodem partition firmware into the chip via SDIO, powering on and starting the chip
Power-on sequence/tmp/aand/bin/wcnddrives the Bluetooth subsystem to power on after receiving the BT-OPEN command
Power-on confirmation/tmp/bt_once 900sends BT-OPEN; returning WCNBTWIFI-CMD OK means success
Periodic wake-up/tmp/bt_wake.shwrites 1 to /proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite every 1.5~2 seconds, preventing the Bluetooth engine from sleeping
HCI service/usr/local/bin/bt_user_daemonopens /dev/ttyS0 (3M+CRTSCTS) speaking H4, providing a unix socket for application queries

1. Environment Preparation

1.1 Device state confirmation

⚠️ If /tmp/aand does not exist: the Android userland chroot environment must be rebuilt (create directories, lay out Android system libraries, mount –bind /dev, create wcnfdl/wcnmodem partition symlinks). See Chapter 4 of the WiFi operation manual for details.

1.2 Tools Inventory

ToolPurposeLocation
downloadfirmware download bootloader/tmp/aand/bin/download (executed inside chroot)
wcndBluetooth/WiFi power-on daemon/tmp/aand/bin/wcnd (executed inside chroot)
bt_onceone-shot BT-OPEN power-on trigger/tmp/bt_once
bt_wake.shperiodic btwrite wake-up script/tmp/bt_wake.sh
bt_probe_fullHCI full-sequence probe (diagnostics)/tmp/bt_probe_full
hci_3m3M baud rate raw HCI test/tmp/hci_3m (early diagnostics)
bt_user_daemonuserland HCI daemon (production)/usr/local/bin/bt_user_daemon
python3unix socket clientbundled with the device

2. Step One: Bring up WiFi (Bluetooth prerequisite; cannot be skipped)

The Bluetooth chip shares the same firmware and power domain as WiFi, so the WiFi chip must be brought up first for Bluetooth to have a physical basis.

Verification criterion: the mmc2:8800:1 device number is 0x2331, and the wlan0 interface exists.

3. Step Two: Bluetooth Power-On Sequence (BT-OPEN)

3.1 Fix mdbg permissions (critical! must be done after every reboot)

The number one cause of BT-OPEN failure: /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* inside the chroot has permissions 600, causing the power-on command to get no response.

3.2 Start wcnd + trigger BT-OPEN

If the output is FAIL: re-run the chmod from 3.1 (most likely a permission issue), then re-run this step.

4. Step Three: Periodic btwrite Wake-up (HCI gets no response without it)

After the Bluetooth firmware powers on, it defaults to power-saving mode, so periodic wake-up is mandatory for HCI responses.

Typical symptom of skipping this step: after bt_probe_full sends an HCI Reset, no response is received at all (or only a single 55 7e ... 53 50 52 44 33 (SPRD3) identity frame is received, with nothing after).

5. Step Four: HCI Channel Diagnostics (optional; verifies the lower layers)

Probe stepMeaning
HCI Resetchip HCI engine start
Read Local Versionfirmware version / vendor identification
Read BD_ADDRchip Bluetooth MAC
Read Buffer SizeHCI buffer capability
Read Featuresfeature set (verifies whether the pskey is in effect)
Set Event Mask + Write Scan Enablepreparation for scanning

6. Step Five: Deploy the Userland HCI Daemon (production approach)

Note: why not use the kernel hci_uart driver? This device’s kernel is a custom Android 3.10.65; a user-compiled hci_uart.ko has hardcoded tty_struct offsets that do not match, so hci0 registers but TX=0 and hciconfig up times out — the driver route does not work. The userland approach reads/writes /dev/ttyS0 directly, does not depend on the kernel protocol stack, and is the most reliable.

6.1 Compile the daemon

The source code bt_user_daemon.c (saved locally) is compiled on the device:

Key implementation points (for reference during maintenance):

  • Open /dev/ttyS0: B3000000 (3M) + CRTSCTS, VMIN=1 (blocking read)
  • H4 protocol: read complete frames per the frame header buf[1]=evt / buf[2]=len
  • Before scanning, you must first send Write Scan Enable (0x0c1a, 0x03) before Inquiry (GIAC 0x33 0x8b 0x9e); otherwise the firmware does not return an Inquiry Result
  • unix socket /tmp/bt_ctl.sock (0666), text commands: state / on / off / scan <N> / list / connect <bd>

6.2 Deploy + auto-start (openrc)

6.3 Verify (unix socket client)

python3 on the device (no socat):

7. Boot Auto-Start Chain (fully automatic after reboot)

After the device reboots, it is brought up automatically by the /etc/local.d/ script chain:

Key red lines:

  • download is resident — do not kill it — killing everything breaks the WiFi/Bluetooth firmware state, requiring a device reboot to recover
  • After reboot, the chmod 666 /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* from 3.1 must be re-run (already automated in the script)
  • Process cleanup always uses pkill -9 -x bt_user_daemon; do not use the ps | grep inline pattern (it kills the shell executing the command itself)

8. Common Faults Quick Reference

SymptomCauseFix
BT-OPEN returns FAIL/tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/* permissions 600retry after chmod 666 /tmp/aand/proc/mdbg/*
No HCI response / only a single SPRD3 framemissing btwrite wake-upstart /tmp/bt_wake.sh; confirm /proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite is writable
No devices found by scanningWrite Scan Enable not sent firstuse the daemon’s scan command (handled internally); do not send bare Inquiry
socket connect failuredaemon multiple instances fighting over the socketrestart as a single instance after pkill -9 -x bt_user_daemon
daemon log reports “Not a tty”tty ldisc occupiedpython fcntl.ioctl(fd, 0x5421, b'\x00\x00\x00\x00') to restore N_TTY
Kernel hci0 registers but TX=03.10 kernel hci_uart offsets do not matchabandon the kernel driver; use the userland daemon
WiFi fails to come updownload was killed by mistakereboot the device and re-bring-up per Chapter 2

9. Key Nodes / Parameters Quick Reference

ItemValue
SDIO device/sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1, device=0x2331
HCI serial port/dev/ttyS0, baud rate 3M (B3000000) + CRTSCTS, H4 protocol
Wake-up node/proc/bluetooth/sleep/btwrite (write 1, every 1.5~2s)
UART configuration node/sys/devices/70000000.uart/uart_conf (0x1a1=115200, 0x341=57600)
socket/tmp/bt_ctl.sock (0666)
Debug logs/tmp/btud_dbg.log (TX/RX hex), /tmp/btud.log (stdout)
Firmware real MAC11:22:14:31:93:27 (firmware response, not spoofed)
pskey/mnt/android_sys/lib/modules/pskey_bt.txt (feature_set/device_addr), delivered by download via connectivity_configure.ini [SETCTION 6]
Known scannable device48:f1:ae:25:7e:48 (class=5a420c phone)

bt_wake.sh/tmp/bt_wake.shPeriodic btwrite wake-up
bt_daemon/etc/init.d/bt_daemonopenrc autostart (rc-update add default)
wifi.start/etc/local.d/wifi.startBoot-time WiFi + download chain
lvgl_demo/usr/local/bin/lvgl_demoLVGL desktop (includes the Bluetooth page; committed to git)
pskey_bt.txt/mnt/android_sys/lib/modules/pskey_bt.txtAuthoritative Bluetooth parameter values
btud_dbg.log/tmp/btud_dbg.logdaemon TX/RX hex log

11. Future Enhancement Directions (Currently Incomplete)

ItemDescriptionSuggested path
Real pairing/connectionThe daemon connect has only been tested at the BR/EDR layer (RC -2 is expected)Capture the complete ttyS0 traffic when Bluetooth is enabled on the reference machine H709, and replay the initialization sequence (including boot commands)
BLE supportOnly BR/EDR scanning has been verified so farExtend to HCI LE commands (LE Set Scan Parameters/Enable)
Audio A2DPNo protocol stack; unavailable for nowRequires introducing BlueZ or a lightweight A2DP stack
daemon connection state persistenceConnection attempts are currently not savedThe page can add a “connected devices” status display

12. 5-Minute Quick Acceptance Path

If both of the above pass → the Bluetooth underlying layers + application chain are all OK, and you can proceed directly to the “enhancement directions” work; if they do not pass → locate the issue item by item per the §7 decision table.

entry.title: wifi
entry.content:
Bringing Up WiFi on the Spreadtrum SC9832A Device (HT0) — AI Execution Guide

Audience: AI assistants (Doubao / other large models) that need to quickly resolve WiFi-unavailable / cannot-connect problems on similar devices (Spreadtrum SC9832A, Android kernel + Alpine user space)
How to use: read §1–§3 first to build context → follow the standard procedure in §5 → verify per §6 → on failure, consult the decision table in §7
Core value: every command in this article is taken from the wifi.start boot script that was verified working on the device; following it lets you bring up WiFi directly on similar devices and avoid repeating the same pitfalls
Related: WiFi and Bluetooth share the same Marlin combo chip, and WiFi is the physical prerequisite for Bluetooth (see the Bluetooth AI guide)

1. Device and Environment at a Glance

ItemValue
Device modelHT0 (reference machine: H709, running Android 6.0, usable as an information source)
Hostname / kernelspd-box / Linux 3.10.65 #13 SMP PREEMPT armv7l
System combinationKeep the Android 6.0 kernel + switchroot to Alpine Linux (critical!)
SSHroot@<设备IP> (RNDIS debug port) / <WiFi-IP> after WiFi is connected
WiFi chipSpreadtrum Marlin combo WCN (SC2331, WiFi + Bluetooth on the same chip, SDIO interface)
WiFi interfacewlan0 (drivers sprdwl.ko + marlin_fm.ko)
Firmware downloadstock Android download binary, run inside the chroot /tmp/aand
Current statusWiFi is up: download → driver → wpa_supplicant → DHCP; the boot script has been pinned

⚠️ After a reboot, SSH may be briefly unreachable (USB port switching); poll and retry. /tmp survives reboots (the chroot environment and the tools are all there).

2. Confirmed Hard Facts (No Need to Re-investigate — Trust Them Directly)

  1. WiFi firmware must be flashed by the stock Android download binary: chroot /tmp/aand /bin/download -i wlan0; only then does the chip have firmware to run. The WiFi and Bluetooth firmware are a single unit, so WiFi up = the Bluetooth firmware is also ready.
  2. download depends on a complete chroot Android user space: /tmp/aand must contain the Android libs (including libiwnpi.so), the /etc/marlinba/*.ini configs, device nodes, and partition symlinks (by-name: wcnfdl→mmcblk0p14, wcnmodem→mmcblk0p15, boot→mmcblk0p16). wifi.start sets all of these up automatically.
  3. SDIO enumeration is the sign of a successful firmware download: /sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1 appears with device=0x2331.
  4. Driver load order is a hard constraint: marlin_fm.ko must be loaded before sprdwl.ko (sprdwl depends on the fm_read symbol exported by marlin_fm); reversing the order reports Unknown symbol.
  5. download must stay resident: killing all download/logdw processes corrupts the chip firmware state; only a full reboot can recover.
  6. wpa_supplicant configuration: /etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.conf, with ctrl_interface=/run/wpa_supplicant and update_config=1; the LVGL network page interacts with this configuration through wpa_cli.
  7. LVGL network settings page (lv_pages/network_page.c): toggle = ip link up/down, scan = wpa_cli -i wlan0 scan + scan_results, connect = add_network→set_network→select_network→save_config→reconnect.
  8. The boot script has been pinned: /etc/local.d/wifi.start (idempotent by design; already-completed steps are skipped automatically), with a git copy at shell/wifi.start.
  9. DHCP: use udhcpc -i wlan0 (the Alpine default); if it stays “acquiring”, check the wpa connection status and the drivers first.
  10. Time issue: the device RTC once fell back to 2016; it has been fixed with hwclock/ntpd and pinned in a script such as /etc/local.d/time_sync.start. If the date is wrong, fix the time before debugging the network (certificates/handshakes are affected by the date).

3. Verified Dead Ends (Do Not Retry — It Wastes Turns)

RouteResultReason
Kill download/logdw for a “clean restart”The chip firmware state is corrupted, and WiFi/Bluetooth fail togetherA full reboot is the only recovery; the correct approach is to let wifi.start re-run idempotently
Replace the Android kernel with a mainline Linux kernelNot adoptedThe Android kernel contains Spreadtrum-specific customizations (SDIO/power/firmware timing) with no mainline equivalent; extremely risky
Change the USB OTG / network modeExplicitly forbidden by the userIt would break the RNDIS debug port / network topology
insmod sprdwl.ko directly without loading marlin_fmLoad fails with Unknown symbolModule symbol dependency; the order cannot be reversed
Repeatedly reconnect the same IP when port 22 is unreachable after rebootIneffectiveCaused by USB port switching; poll and retry both IPs
Write a custom download to replace the stock Android oneHigh risk, not adoptedThe firmware download sequence (power_ctl power-on sequence + UART handshake + SDIO bulk writes) is a chip trade secret; the stock binary is the most reliable

4. System Model: Layers + Per-Layer Verification Criteria

Debugging discipline: when a layer fails verification, look for the cause only in that layer and its upstream. Example: when WiFi will not connect, check the wpa_supplicant status first (③), rather than re-flashing the firmware (①).

5. Standard Execution Procedure (Ready to Copy)

5.1 Full Chain (Corresponds to wifi.start; Relying on the Idempotent Re-run of the Boot Script Is Recommended)

5.2 Manual Step-by-Step (For Debugging)

5.3 Connecting to WiFi (wpa_cli Interaction, the Same Logic as the LVGL Network Page)

6. Verification Checklist (Confirm Item by Item)

#CheckExpected
1cat /sys/bus/sdio/devices/mmc2:8800:1/device0x2331
2lsmod | grep sprdwlsprdwl + marlin_fm (dependency: 1 sprdwl)
3ip -br link show wlan0UP
4iwconfig wlan0ESSID associated / no ESSID means not connected
5pgrep -x wpa_supplicantthe process exists
6wpa_cli -i wlan0 statuswpa_state=COMPLETED
7ip addr show wlan0 | grep 'inet 'has an IPv4 address
8ip routehas a default via gateway
9LVGL network pagetoggle/scan/saved/nearby list/connect all work

7. Failure → Root Cause → Fix Decision Table

SymptomMost likely root causeFix
Log ERROR: SDIO not enumerated, download may have failedFirmware download did not complete (timing/permission/node issue)Check the tail of /tmp/logdw.log; confirm /dev/power_ctl is writable and the by-name symlinks exist; re-run wifi.start
Log bind logdw failed: No such file or directorylogdw is not in place (/tmp/logdw does not exist or is not executable)ls -la /tmp/logdw; re-copy it from /mnt/android_sys/bin/
download started pid= (pid empty)The download process did not startps -eo pid,comm | grep download; check whether the chroot environment is complete
wlan0 does not appear after the drivers loadDriver load failed / chip not enumerateddmesg | tail; first confirm SDIO 0x2331; rmmod and reload
Scan returns emptywpa_supplicant is not running / the interface is not uppgrep wpa_supplicant; ip link set wlan0 up; run wpa_cli scan and then scan_results
Connected but the IP stays “acquiring”DHCP did not run / wpa is not COMPLETEDCheck wpa_state with wpa_cli status; run udhcpc -i wlan0 -q -n manually
SSH unreachable after rebootThe RNDIS port did not recover / the IP changedPoll both <设备IP> and <WiFi-IP>; wait for the boot script to finish
Date shows 2016The RTC is not synchronizedSync with hwclock -s / ntpd and write it into an /etc/local.d boot script (already pinned; do not repeat)
WiFi works but Bluetooth will not startThe Bluetooth chain was not runSee §5 of the Bluetooth AI guide (mdbg permissions / wcnd / bt_once / btwrite)

8. Component Architecture (Required Reading for Changes/Maintenance)

Key chroot nodes (required by download; missing any of them means SDIO enumeration fails):

  • /tmp/aand/bin/download (stock Android version)
  • /tmp/aand/lib/libiwnpi.so + the full set of Android libs
  • /tmp/aand/etc/marlinba/connectivity_configure.ini (firmware path/calibration configuration, also contains the Bluetooth pskey)
  • /tmp/aand/dev/block/platform/sdio_emmc/by-name/{wcnfdl→mmcblk0p14, wcnmodem→mmcblk0p15, boot→mmcblk0p16}
  • /dev/power_ctl (download writes the SLEEP→POWER_ON→POWER_RST power-on sequence)

LVGL network page (lv_pages/network_page.c, 1677 lines, the WiFi settings UI template):

  • Toggle: ip link set wlan0 up/down + wpa_cli disconnect/reconnect
  • Scan: wpa_cli scan → wait 3s → wpa_cli scan_results → parse bssid/signal/flags/ssid
  • Connect: add_network / set_network (ssid/psk/key_mgmt/scan_ssid/priority) / select_network / save_config
  • Saved list: wpa_cli list_networks

9. Red Lines and Operational Discipline

  1. Never kill download, which must stay resident — killing all of them corrupts the chip firmware state; only a full reboot recovers.
  2. Driver order: marlin_fm.ko first, sprdwl.ko second.
  3. wifi.start is idempotent — to start over, just run sh /etc/local.d/wifi.start; it kills leftovers first and then brings everything up. Do not operate manually piece by piece.
  4. Do not change the USB OTG / network mode configuration (an explicit user constraint).
  5. Do not switch to a mainline kernel — the Spreadtrum-specific customizations (SDIO/power/firmware) depend on the Android kernel.
  6. The date must be correct — WiFi handshakes/certificates are affected by the system time; fix the time before debugging the network.
  7. Use pkill -9 -x <name> to clean up processes; do not use the inline ps | grep pattern (it can kill your own shell).

10. Inventory of Tools/Files Already on the Device (Reuse Them — Do Not Rebuild)

Tool/fileLocationPurpose
wifi.start/etc/local.d/wifi.start (git: shell/wifi.start)WiFi auto-start at boot + the full chain (idempotent)
Boot log/var/log/wifi_boot.logwifi.start output (first choice for troubleshooting)
download/tmp/aand/bin/downloadfirmware download (inside the chroot)
logdw/tmp/logdwfirmware download log daemon
Android user space/mnt/android_sys (mmcblk0p17)read-only mount of the Android system (source of libs/configs)
Drivers/lib/modules/marlin_fm.ko, /lib/modules/sprdwl.koWiFi drivers (precompiled on the device)
wpa config/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.confwpa_supplicant configuration (including saved networks)
Network pagelv_pages/network_page.c (LVGL project)WiFi settings UI (wpa_cli interaction template)
DHCPudhcpc (bundled with Alpine)obtain an IP

11. Future Enhancement Directions (Currently Incomplete)

ItemDescriptionSuggested approach
IPv4 stabilityIn some scenarios IPv6 has an address but IPv4 is not obtainedRun udhcpc immediately after checking wpa_state=COMPLETED, and add -n retries and logging
Auto-reconnect strategyAfter a disconnect, only wpa_supplicant’s automatic reconnect is relied onA “disconnect/reconnect” button and a signal-strength display can be added to the network page (scan_results already provides signal)
Multi-network priorityCurrently a single network configurationExtend wpa_cli list_networks management + a sorting UI
Coexistence with BluetoothWiFi stays resident + Bluetooth scanning runs in parallelThey share download/wcnd; testing shows no conflict, but mutually exclusive power management can be added

12. 5-Minute Quick Acceptance Path

If all of the above pass, the full WiFi chain (physical + protocol + network) is OK; if not, locate the problem item by item using the §7 decision table.

Document version: v1.0 (distilled after WiFi was brought up)
Related documents: WiFi Operation Manual (for humans), WiFi Boot Process Comparison, WiFi Working Process Summary, Bluetooth Bring-Up AI Guide

entry.title: WiFi Chip Bring-up Operation Manual
entry.content:
WiFi Chip Bring-up — Manual Operation Manual

Applicable devices: spd-box (SC9832A quad-core, armv7l, Android 6 kernel 3.10.65 + switchroot Alpine Linux 3.21 armhf)
WiFi chip: Marlin SC2331 (SDIO interface, mmc2:8800:1, device 0x2331)
Document goal: without relying on any AI assistance, a human can follow this manual to bring the device’s onboard WiFi from scratch to a “scannable, connectable” state.
Document version: v1.0　|　2026-09

Table of Contents

  1. Background and Problem Definition
  2. Tools and Materials List
  3. Overall Approach
  4. Operation Procedure
    • 4.1 Device and System Confirmation
    • 4.2 Forensics from the Android Reference Machine
    • 4.3 Extracting and Replacing the Stock Android Device Tree (DTB)
    • 4.4 Building the Android User-Space chroot Environment
    • 4.5 Performing Firmware Download (the download power-up sequence)
    • 4.6 Verifying SDIO Enumeration
    • 4.7 Loading the WiFi Driver
    • 4.8 Installing and Configuring wpa_supplicant
    • 4.9 Scan Verification
    • 4.10 Fixing Boot Auto-start in Place
  5. Troubleshooting Quick-Reference Table
  6. Notes and Risks

1. Background and Problem Definition

  • The device ships with Android 6.0, where WiFi/Bluetooth work completely (no hardware fault).
  • The user switchrooted the device to Alpine Linux (keeping the Android kernel 3.10.65, replacing only the root filesystem).
  • After switching to Alpine, WiFi does not work at all, with typical symptoms:
    • dmesg repeatedly shows SDIO dev not ready;
    • GPIO94 (the chip’s READY pin) stays at 0;
    • the kernel has never enumerated an SDIO WiFi device (/sys/bus/sdio/devices/ is empty).
  • Root cause: the SC2331 chip’s power-up timing + firmware download is completed by the resident download service in the Android system (writing /dev/power_ctl, /dev/download, and flashing the firmware from the wcnfdl/wcnmodem partitions into the chip). Alpine does not have this set of services, so the chip has never been “activated”.

2. Tools and Materials List

CategoryTool/MaterialPurposeNotes
Remote operationSSH client (paramiko / PuTTY / OpenSSH)connect to the Alpine deviceroot@<device IP>
Reference forensicsWatchTools adb (AndroidWatch_ADB_ToolBox\adb\adb.exe)connect to the same-model Android machine H709root required (Magisk)
Partition read/writedd, cat, lsextract/write partitions, device nodesbuilt into the device (BusyBox/coreutils)
System tracingstracelocate the cause of the download service’s failureon Alpine use apk add strace
Firmware filesdownload (Android binary), libiwnpi.so, wcnfdl/wcnmodem partition imagespower-up + firmware downloadextracted from the Android system
Device treeandroid_orig.dtb (about 53,967 bytes)replace the dtb in the p16 partitionextracted from the Android boot image
Kernel modulesmarlin_fm.ko, sprdwl.koWiFi driverplaced in /lib/modules/
User spacewpa_supplicant + wpa_cli (v2.10-r11)scan/connectAlpine armhf package
Dependency librarieslibnl3, pcsc-lite-libswpa_supplicant dependenciesAlpine armhf package
Auxiliarychroot, mount --bindrun Android binariesbuilt into the device

3. Overall Approach

In one sentence: the chip’s power-up and firmware download logic lives in Android’s user space (the download service), and Alpine lacks it → move the stock Android download binary + firmware + device nodes into a chroot, “borrow a shell” in Alpine to run the power-up sequence, let the kernel enumerate the SDIO chip, then load the driver and configure wpa_supplicant.

The chain has four segments, and none can be missing:

4. Operation Procedure

4.1 Device and System Confirmation

4.2 Forensics from the Android Reference Machine

A same-model device with a working Android system (H709) is needed, the one with both WiFi and Bluetooth working.

4.3 Extracting and Replacing the Stock Android Device Tree (DTB)

The stock Android DTB contains the correct descriptions of WiFi power/clocks. This is one of the prerequisites for download to work properly later.

4.3.1 PC side: extract the DTB from the boot image

4.3.2 Device side: write to the p16 partition

⚠️ Writing the boot partition carries risk; be sure to back up first. If flashed incorrectly, dd back from the backup.

4.4 Building the Android User-Space chroot Environment

Purpose: let the stock Android download binary run in Alpine (it depends on Android’s libraries, device nodes, and partition links).

Debugging essentials: if strace shows open("/dev/power_ctl") failing → confirm mount --bind /dev; if it shows open(...wcnfdl) failing → confirm the by-name links.

4.5 Performing Firmware Download (the download power-up sequence)

If firmware download fails (stuck at the handshake/write errors), check: whether the DTB is correct (back to 4.3), whether /dev/power_ctl is writable, and whether the firmware partitions are the stock ones.

4.6 Verifying SDIO Enumeration

4.7 Loading the WiFi Driver

⚠️ The load order cannot be reversed: sprdwl.ko depends on the symbols exported by marlin_fm.ko (fm_read); reversing it reports Unknown symbol.

4.8 Installing and Configuring wpa_supplicant

If Alpine’s official repositories are unavailable, directly download the armhf apk and install it manually.

4.9 Scan Verification

4.10 Fixing Boot Auto-start in Place

After a device reboot, kernel enumeration, firmware, drivers, and wpa_supplicant must all recover automatically.

5. Troubleshooting Quick-Reference Table

SymptomPossible CauseInvestigation/Fix
dmesg constantly SDIO dev not readythe chip is not powered / firmware not downloadedconfirm download has run (4.5); check whether /dev/power_ctl is writable
GPIO94 READY stays 0the power-up sequence was not executeduse strace to trace whether download’s ioctl/write report errors
download reports open device failurethe chroot is missing device nodesmount --bind /dev /tmp/aand/dev
download reports wcnfdl/wcnmodem not foundmissing by-name linksln -sf /dev/block/mmcblk0p14 .../wcnfdl
download finishes but SDIO has no enumerationwrong DTBconfirm p16 already has the stock Android dtb (4.3)
insmod sprdwl.ko reports Unknown symbolwrong module load orderinsmod marlin_fm.ko first
wlan0 does not appearthe driver was loaded before firmware download completedwait for mmc2:8800:1 to appear in dmesg before insmod
wpa_cli scan failswpa_supplicant not running / interface not upip link set wlan0 up + confirm the supplicant process
wpa_cli not foundPATH missing /sbinexport PATH=$PATH:/sbin
WiFi lost after rebootboot auto-start not donefix in place per 4.10
SSH drops after plugging/unplugging USB peripheralsthe device’s USB port multiplexing (network port/keyboard)re-plug the PC’s USB and reboot the device to recover

6. Notes and Risks

  1. Flashing the p16 (boot) partition carries a bricking risk — you must back up first (/root/p16_boot_backup.img); if flashed incorrectly, you can roll back.
  2. USB port multiplexing: the device’s USB port serves as both an SSH network port and a peripheral port. Plugging in a keyboard/mouse will disconnect SSH; you need to unplug the peripheral, plug the PC’s USB back in, and reboot the device.
  3. Firmware version matching: after download powers up successfully, the driver and firmware must come from the same Android version, otherwise wlan0 may have an interface but scanning fails.
  4. Module path: confirm marlin_fm.ko / sprdwl.ko are in /lib/modules/ and match kernel 3.10.65 (mismatch causes invalid module format).
  5. wpa_supplicant version: the device is armhf; be sure to use the armhf package; an x86_64 package reports Exec format error.
  6. dtb offset: when writing p16, seek=20008 (512-byte blocks) corresponds to byte offset 0x9C5000; different firmware may differ, so parse the boot image first to confirm.

This manual is compiled based on the actual bring-up process; the operation order must not be reversed, and the key steps (DTB → power-up → driver → supplicant) are all indispensable.
